title_en: Trump ‘whiplash’ on deportations putting Afghans in turmoil: ‘People already survived a war’
title_zh: 特朗普对驱逐令阿富汗人陷入混乱表示“严厉打击”：“人们已经从战争中幸存下来”
summary: Members of Congress and advocates warn that returning people to their home countries could be a death sentence Dozens of Afghans who are currently in the US but fear being deported back to Afghanistan along with a larger group and possibly killed by the Taliba
summary_zh: 国会议员和倡导者警告说，将人们遣返回国可能会被判处死刑。
body_en: Members of Congress and advocates warn that returning people to their home countries could be a death sentence

Dozens of Afghans who are currently in the US but fear being deported back to Afghanistan along with a larger group and possibly killed by the Taliban are experiencing “fragile relief” this weekend after it appeared that the Trump administration had put on hold plans to remove them within days.
Members of Congress and advocates have repeatedly warned that the deportations could effectively be a death sentence.

A flight originally scheduled to transport the group out of the US on election day earlier this month had stayed grounded after a federal judge issued a court order temporarily blocking its departure to Afghanistan or neighboring Pakistan. The whole group numbers more than 150 Afghans, the New York Times reported . And the AP previously reported that the federal government intends to route these detainees to their home country via Pakistan.

Then, as the temporary court order expired last weekend, immigration advocates battling to prevent the deportations talked of dreading that the detainees could be forced to leave the US during the week of 16 November . This prospect was based on a rescheduled removal date given for at least one Afghan man currently in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detention who was due to be on the flight.
As that date loomed, suddenly there was another development amid frantic advocacy efforts.

Late on Tuesday, it was learned that that detainee, along with a handful of other detained Afghans on the original flight manifest, now no longer had a specified departure date issued by the US government.

Some immigration lawyers also reported that their Afghan clients had been moved from staging facilities to long-term detention facilities, suggesting they would not be forced onto a deportation flight in the coming days after all.

Amid some confusion and often few details from the administration, Shawn VanDiver, founder and president of the US non-profit coalition #AfghanEvac, said that a sensation of “fragile relief” had descended on the people involved.

Some of the Afghans in the targeted group have relatives who assisted the US war on Afghanistan after the terrorist attacks on the US on 11 September 2001 that drove out the Taliban, VanDiver said. He had already called Donald Trump’s efforts to remove Afghans from the US cruel and being done in “a heinous matter” as a scare tactic against others.

“In a matter of days, these allies were told they were being sent through Pakistan into the hands of the Taliban, then told they were safe, then told that nobody knows. That isn’t immigration policy. It’s whiplash inflicted on people who already survived a war,” he said. “These men and women kept their promise to America, and it’s time we kept ours by ending these removals for good.”
VanDiver has slammed any option to use Pakistan as a conduit for “forced rendition” .

Immigration advocates are hoping continued pressure will result in further delays and the ultimate cancellation of that flight and any others planned for the coming weeks. In the meantime, #AfghanEvac is pushing what will become the newly Democratic-controlled Congress in January to pass a bipartisan bill that has been drafted and would give Afghans who are already in the US temporary protected status (TPS) through July 2029, with a vetting process. The US supreme court in June allowed the Trump administration to strip such protections, including from Afghans .
Such legislation would “keep people we already vetted and brought here from being sent back to the Taliban while their cases are decided”, VanDiver said.

Among the passengers reported to be on the blocked flight were Afghans whose relatives helped American troops, women, at least one gay man and members of the minority ethnic Hazara group – some who have said they were previously beaten by the Taliban.

Human Rights First, the US-based human rights group, has warned about “ grave, systematic dangers ” for Afghans returned to Afghanistan. That includes “arbitrary detentions, executions, public flogging, and retaliatory violence”, as well as restrictions on basic freedoms for women and girls.

The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) said in response to questions and a request for comment that the agency complies with all lawful court orders and that US Immigration and Customs Enforcement ( ICE ) does not comment on or confirm prospective removal operations, for operational security reasons, and the safety of its officers.

Sari Arvey, director of policy, refugee and immigrant rights at Human Rights First, said that the Trump administration’s targeting of Afghans reflects a broader trend of creating arrangements with other governments to send people back to war zones, security crises and countries that don’t have diplomatic relations with the US.
The US suspended relations with Afghanistan after the Taliban government took over in 2021, forcing a scrambled US evacuation.
body_zh: 国会议员和倡导者警告说，将人们遣返回国可能会被判处死刑
目前在美国的数十名阿富汗人担心与更大的群体一起被驱逐回阿富汗，并可能被塔利班杀害，在特朗普政府似乎搁置了几天内驱逐他们的计划后，本周末他们正经历“脆弱的缓解”。
国会议员和支持者一再警告说，驱逐出境实际上可能等于死刑。
原定于本月早些时候选举日将这群人运出美国的航班在联邦法官发布法院命令暂时阻止其飞往阿富汗或邻国巴基斯坦后一直处于停飞状态。据《纽约时报》报道，整个组织有 150 多名阿富汗人。美联社此前报道称，联邦政府打算将这些被拘留者经巴基斯坦送回祖国。
然后，随着临时法院命令于上周末到期，努力阻止驱逐的移民倡导者谈到了担心被拘留者可能会在 11 月 16 日这一周被迫离开美国。这一前景是基于为至少一名目前被移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 拘留的阿富汗男子重新安排的遣送日期，该男子原定登机。
随着这一日期的临近，在疯狂的宣传工作中突然出现了另一个进展。
周二晚些时候，据悉，该被拘留者以及原始航班名单上的其他几名被拘留的阿富汗人现在不再有美国政府发布的指定出发日期。
一些移民律师还报告说，他们的阿富汗客户已从临时设施转移到长期拘留设施，这表明他们在未来几天内不会被迫乘坐驱逐航班。
美国非营利联盟 #AfghanEvac 的创始人兼主席肖恩·范迪弗 (Shawn VanDiver) 表示，在一些混乱和政府提供的细节往往很少的情况下，相关人员感到了一种“脆弱的救济”的感觉。
范迪弗说，目标群体中的一些阿富汗人的亲属在 2001 年 9 月 11 日美国发生恐怖袭击并赶走了塔利班之后，曾协助美国对阿富汗进行战争。他已经称唐纳德·特朗普将阿富汗人赶出美国的努力是残酷的，而且是“令人发指的事情”，是针对其他人的恐吓策略。
“几天之内，这些盟友就被告知，他们将通过巴基斯坦被送到塔利班手中，然后被告知他们是安全的，然后被告知没有人知道。这不是移民政策。这是对已经在战争中幸存下来的人的鞭打，”他说。 “这些男男女女兑现了对美国的承诺，现在是我们履行我们的承诺、永远结束这些迁移的时候了。”
VanDiver 猛烈抨击了任何利用巴基斯坦作为“强迫引渡”渠道的选择。
移民倡导者希望持续的压力将导致进一步的延误，并最终取消该航班以及未来几周计划的任何其他航班。与此同时，#AfghanEvac 正在推动将于 1 月份新成立的民主党控制的国会通过一项已起草的两党法案，该法案将在 2029 年 7 月之前给予已经在美国的阿富汗人临时保护身份 (TPS)，并进行审查程序。美国最高法院六月允许特朗普政府取消此类保护，包括对阿富汗人的保护。
范迪弗说，这样的立法将“防止我们已经审查并带到这里的人在案件得到裁决期间被送回塔利班”。
据报道，被封锁航班上的乘客中有阿富汗人，他们的亲属曾帮助过美国军人、妇女、至少一名同性恋者以及少数族裔哈扎拉族成员——其中一些人表示，他们以前曾遭到塔利班的殴打。
总部位于美国的人权组织“人权第一”警告称，返回阿富汗的阿富汗人将面临“严重的、系统性的危险”。这包括“任意拘留、处决、公开鞭打和报复性暴力”，以及对妇女和女童基本自由的限制。
美国国土安全部 (DHS) 在回答问题和置评请求时表示，该机构遵守所有合法的法院命令，并且出于操作安全原因及其官员的安全，美国移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 不会对预期的遣返行动发表评论或确认。
人权第一组织政策、难民和移民权利主任萨里·阿维表示，特朗普政府针对阿富汗人的做法反映了一种更广泛的趋势，即与其他政府做出安排，将人们送回战区、安全危机地区和与美国没有外交关系的国家。
2021年塔利班政府上台后，美国暂停了与阿富汗的关系，迫使美国紧急撤离。

title_en: ICE reports record immigration arrests, deportations since Trump White House return
title_zh: 自特朗普重返白宫以来，ICE 报告记录了移民逮捕和驱逐出境的情况
summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history
summary_zh: 美国移民和海关执法局表示，最近 12 个月内逮捕和驱逐的人数比其 23 年来的任何时候都要多。
body_en: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement says it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history
WASHINGTON -- U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said Thursday that it arrested and deported more people during a recent 12-month period than at any time in its 23-year history.

ICE said it deported 483,200 people in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30, up 9% from its previous high of 442,640 in the same period a year earlier and up 78% from 271,480 in 2024, the last year of Joe Biden's presidency.
ICE arrested 474,850 people in the most recent 12-month period, roughly double the 239,890 arrests a year earlier and more than quadruple the 113,430 arrests in 2024.
ICE had not released such precise counts since President Donald Trump returned to the White House, including for 2025.

title_en: Democrat wins Alaska governor’s seat for first time in nearly 30 years
title_zh: 民主党近 30 年来首次赢得阿拉斯加州州长席位
summary: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins’ victory means Democrats will now hold 30 US governorships after midterm blowout Democrats have captured Alaska ’s governor’s seat for the first time in nearly three decades, marking another major victory for their party in a midterm el
summary_zh: 乔纳森·克莱斯-汤姆金斯的胜利意味着民主党在中期选举井喷式夺取阿拉斯加州州长职位后将拥有 30 个美国州长职位。
body_en: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins’ victory means Democrats will now hold 30 US governorships after midterm blowout

Democrats have captured Alaska ’s governor’s seat for the first time in nearly three decades, marking another major victory for their party in a midterm election period that has dramatically shifted political power across the US.

Former Alaska state legislator Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republican opponents, including a candidate backed by Donald Trump , becoming the first Democrat elected governor of Alaska since 1998.

His victory – called by the Associated Press on Friday, 10 days after the polls closed – adds to a growing list of Democratic gains nationwide, bringing the party’s total to 30 US governorships. Democrats have also taken control of governor’s offices in several other longtime Republican strongholds, including Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.
‘We must deliver’: jubilant Democrats gather in Denver to chart way forward
Kreiss-Tomkins, widely known as JKT, secured the win having mounted a political comeback three years after departing the Alaska house of representatives.
The 37-year-old traveled extensively throughout the state during his campaign, building support around economic concerns and a promise to change the direction of Alaska’s government.

His platform centered on tackling affordability, ensuring full funding for public education, and requiring all oil and gas producers to pay corporate income taxes. He also pushed for a temporary halt to new datacenter developments until state lawmakers establish regulations governing their construction.
Throughout the campaign, Kreiss-Tomkins sharply criticized the leadership of outgoing the Republican governor, Mike Dunleavy, arguing that Alaska had become “broken” during his eight years in office.
“Alaskans are hungry for change,” Kreiss-Tomkins said. “We’ve been running the same campaign since we launched in February, and I don’t take anyone’s vote for granted.”

Among his criticisms was the deterioration of the state’s ferry system, which Kreiss-Tomkins said had been left in disarray as service to numerous communities was drastically reduced. The ferry network serves as a critical transportation link for communities in south-east Alaska that lack road connections, including some with limited access to air travel.

Despite his criticism of the outgoing administration, Kreiss-Tomkins presented himself as a leader willing to work across political divisions. He pledged to assemble a cabinet that includes Democrats, Republicans and independents.

Unlike most states, Alaska allows voters to rank candidates by preference through ranked-choice voting – a system that also permits multiple candidates from the same political party to run against one another.
But Kreiss-Tomkins avoided the need for additional rounds of vote counting after winning more than 50% of first-choice votes, securing an outright victory.

The Alaska result comes just days after Democrats scored another major gubernatorial win in staunchly conservative Kansas, where the Democratic state senator Cindy Holscher narrowly defeated the Republican state senate president, Ty Masterson.

Masterson, who received Trump’s endorsement, faced a campaign in which Holscher repeatedly highlighted his ties to the Republican president. At the same time, Holscher maintained that she would remain willing to cooperate with the Trump administration on issues where common ground could be found.
The back-to-back victories in Alaska and Kansas underscore the scale of Democratic gains in what has become a nationwide electoral shift.

The party’s long-anticipated “blue wave” has now materialized , with Democrats flipping eight seats in the US Senate, gaining more than two dozen seats in the House and significantly expanding their control of governors’ offices after the 3 November midterms.

Such gains have handed Democrats a strong majority in Congress for the latter half of Trump’s second presidency, delivering a major shift in the balance of power in Washington and state governments across the US.
body_zh: 乔纳森·克莱斯-汤姆金斯的胜利意味着民主党在中期选举井喷后将拥有 30 个美国州长职位
民主党近三十年来首次夺得阿拉斯加州州长席位，标志着该党在中期选举期间取得的又一次重大胜利，这场选举极大地改变了美国各地的政治权力。
前阿拉斯加州议员乔纳森·克莱斯·汤姆金斯击败了三名共和党对手，其中包括唐纳德·特朗普支持的候选人，成为自 1998 年以来第一位民主党当选的阿拉斯加州州长。
美联社周五在投票结束 10 天后宣布他的胜利，为民主党在全国范围内取得的胜利增添了新的一笔，使该党在美国州长职位上的席位总数达到 30 个。民主党还控制了其他几个共和党长期据点的州长办公室，包括爱荷华州、佐治亚州、俄亥俄州和德克萨斯州。
“我们必须兑现承诺”：兴高采烈的民主党人齐聚丹佛，规划前进方向
克莱斯-汤姆金斯（Kreiss-Tomkins），即广为人知的 JKT，在离开阿拉斯加州众议院三年后，在政治上东山再起，赢得了这场胜利。
这位 37 岁的总统在竞选期间走遍了该州各地，围绕经济问题争取支持，并承诺改变阿拉斯加州政府的方向。
他的政纲重点是解决负担能力问题，确保公共教育获得全额资助，并要求所有石油和天然气生产商缴纳企业所得税。他还推动暂时停止新数据中心的开发，直到州立法者制定管理其建设的法规。
在整个竞选过程中，克莱斯-汤姆金斯尖锐批评即将离任的共和党州长迈克·邓利维的领导，认为阿拉斯加在他执政的八年里已经“支离破碎”。
“阿拉斯加人渴望改变，”克莱斯-汤姆金斯说。 “自二月份推出以来，我们一直在开展同样的活动，我不认为任何人的投票是理所当然的。”
他的批评之一是该州渡轮系统的恶化，克莱斯-汤姆金斯表示，由于对许多社区的服务大幅减少，该系统陷入混乱。轮渡网络是阿拉斯加东南部缺乏道路连接的社区（包括一些航空旅行受限的社区）的重要交通纽带。
尽管克莱斯-汤姆金斯对即将卸任的政府提出批评，但他仍将自己描绘成一位愿意跨政治分歧开展工作的领导人。他承诺组建一个由民主党人、共和党人和独立人士组成的内阁。
与大多数州不同，阿拉斯加州允许选民通过排名选择投票对候选人进行优先排序——这一系统还允许来自同一政党的多名候选人相互竞争。
但克莱斯-汤姆金斯在赢得超过 50% 的第一选择选票后，避免了额外计票的需要，获得了彻底胜利。
阿拉斯加选举结果公布的几天前，民主党在坚定保守的堪萨斯州取得了另一场重大州长选举胜利，民主党州参议员辛迪·霍尔舍尔以微弱优势击败了共和党州参议院议长泰·马斯特森。
获得特朗普支持的马斯特森面临着一场竞选活动，霍尔舍尔在竞选中反复强调他与共和党总统的关系。与此同时，霍尔舍尔坚称，她仍愿意在能够找到共同点的问题上与特朗普政府合作。
阿拉斯加和堪萨斯州的连续胜利突显了民主党在全国选举转变中取得的巨大进展。
该党期待已久的“蓝色浪潮”现已成为现实，民主党在美国参议院夺取了八个席位，在众议院赢得了二十多个席位，并在 11 月 3 日中期选举后大幅扩大了对州长办公室的控制。
这些进展使民主党在特朗普第二任总统任期后半段在国会获得了绝对多数席位，从而使华盛顿和美国各州政府的权力平衡发生了重大转变。

title_en: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
title_zh: 共和党州官员推动恢复特朗普对 2028 年大选的邮件投票限制
summary: Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.
summary_zh: 一些共和党州官员正在对法院阻止 Posta 的命令提出上诉，以重启对 2028 年大选邮寄投票的限制。
body_en: GOP state officials appeal block on 2028 mail voting limits : NPR

GOP state officials appeal block on 2028 mail voting limits Some Republican state officials are reviving a bid for mail-in voting restrictions for the 2028 election by appealing a court order blocking the Postal Service from carrying out a revised ballot rule.
An election worker sorts mail-in ballots at the Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Office in Doral for Florida's primary election in August. Lynne Sladky/AP hide caption
Voting for this year's midterm elections just concluded, but Republican officials in a number of states are already looking to shape how votes are cast in 2028.
Twelve GOP state attorneys general are pushing to revive the president's bid for mail-in voting restrictions in time for the 2028 election.

On Thursday, they started the process of appealing a September order by U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols, one of the two judges who blocked the U.S. Postal Service from carrying out a plan released in response to an executive order by President Trump .

The Republican state attorneys general represent Alabama, Florida, Indiana, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Oklahoma, South Carolina, South Dakota and Texas. It's not clear, however, how long some of these states will continue this case, given that Democrats won up and down the ballot in the midterms. In Texas and Kansas, Democratic candidates are set to take control of their states' attorney general's offices in January.
The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue

In September, the Supreme Court refused to pause a similar ruling by U.S. District Judge Indira Talwani, who is based in Boston. That order stopped USPS from working on its revised rule for federal ballot mail, but it only applied to this year's midterm elections.
Nichols' preliminary injunction blocks USPS from implementing the plan for all federal elections, including the 2028 race.
In a court filing , Justice Department attorneys confirmed the Trump administration is not appealing Nichols' ruling. The appeal deadline was Thursday.
The blocked rule — which the Postal Service released in late August — would require states to turn over lists of voters' names and addresses in order to have them delivered by USPS.
Tens of millions cast ballots for midterms despite worries of Trump's interference
Nichols, a Washington, D.C.-based judge who was nominated by Trump, found that the mailing agency likely has no power to impose that requirement on states.

"As the Government concedes, the Postal Service could issue (and enforce) the Rule only if Congress gave it the authority to do so, but here no statute grants the Postal Service the power to issue key parts of the Rule," Nichols wrote.

The administration's earlier push to put these new restrictions in place for the midterms alarmed many election officials, who were concerned about last-minute changes causing major disruptions to the tens of millions who regularly vote by mail. Some voters with disabilities and those in places without polling sites, they feared, could have lost the ability to exercise their right to cast a ballot.
While the Supreme Court ultimately stopped implementation of the USPS rule for the midterms, Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas dissented from that ruling.

Fellow conservative Justice Brett Kavanaugh said in a concurring opinion that he believed state and local election officials did not have enough time to "reasonably implement the rule" this time. But Kavanaugh noted that "there is at least a fair prospect that the final rule falls within the Postal Service's statutory authority."
A previous version of this story incorrectly said the deadline for the Justice Department to appeal a court order was Nov. 13. The deadline was Nov. 12.
body_zh: 共和党州官员对 2028 年邮件投票限制的阻止提出上诉：NPR
共和党州官员对阻止 2028 年邮寄投票限制提出上诉一些共和党州官员正在对法院阻止邮政局执行修订后的投票规则的命令提出上诉，以重启对 2028 年选举邮寄投票限制的提议。
一名选举工作人员在位于多拉尔的迈阿密戴德县选举办公室主管处对佛罗里达州 8 月份初选的邮寄选票进行分类。琳恩·斯拉基/美联社隐藏标题栏
今年中期选举的投票刚刚结束，但一些州的共和党官员已经在考虑制定 2028 年的投票方式。
十二名共和党州总检察长正在推动总统在 2028 年大选前及时恢复邮寄投票限制的提议。
周四，他们开始对美国地区法官卡尔·尼科尔斯 (Carl Nichols) 9 月份的命令提出上诉，卡尔·尼科尔斯是阻止美国邮政局执行针对特朗普总统行政命令而发布的计划的两名法官之一。
共和党州检察长代表阿拉巴马州、佛罗里达州、印第安纳州、堪萨斯州、路易斯安那州、密苏里州、蒙大拿州、内布拉斯加州、俄克拉荷马州、南卡罗来纳州、南达科他州和德克萨斯州。然而，鉴于民主党在中期选举中获胜，目前尚不清楚其中一些州将继续这种情况多久。在德克萨斯州和堪萨斯州，民主党候选人将于一月份控制该州的总检察长办公室。
特朗普政府的选民名册运动可能会继续
9月，最高法院拒绝暂停美国波士顿地区法官英迪拉·塔尔瓦尼(Indira Talwani)的类似裁决。该命令阻止美国邮政局制定联邦选票邮件的修订规则，但仅适用于今年的中期选举。
尼科尔斯的初步禁令阻止 USPS 实施所有联邦选举的计划，包括 2028 年的竞选。
在一份法庭文件中，司法部律师证实特朗普政府不会对尼科尔斯的裁决提出上诉。上诉截止日期是周四。
邮政服务于八月下旬发布的封锁规则将要求各州交出选民姓名和地址清单，以便由美国邮政局投递。
尽管担心特朗普的干涉，仍有数千万人为中期选举投票
由特朗普提名的华盛顿特区法官尼科尔斯发现，邮政机构可能无权将这一要求强加于各州。
尼科尔斯写道：“正如政府承认的那样，只有国会授权邮政服务才能发布（并执行）该规则，但没有任何法规授予邮政服务发布该规则关键部分的权力。”
政府早些时候推动在中期选举中实施这些新的限制措施，令许多选举官员感到震惊，他们担心最后一刻的变化会对数千万定期通过邮寄投票的人造成重大干扰。他们担心，一些残疾选民和那些没有投票站的地方的选民可能会失去行使投票权的能力。
虽然最高法院最终停止执行美国邮政局关于中期选举的规则，但法官塞缪尔·阿利托和克拉伦斯·托马斯对该裁决持有异议。
同为保守派的法官布雷特·卡瓦诺在一份一致意见中表示，他认为州和地方选举官员这次没有足够的时间“合理地执行该规则”。但卡瓦诺指出，“最终规则至少有可能属于邮政服务的法定权力范围。”
本文之前的版本错误地称司法部对法院命令提出上诉的截止日期是 11 月 13 日。截止日期是 11 月 12 日。

title_en: Progressive versus moderate? Democrats deny party rift as they head into new Congress
title_zh: 渐进式还是温和式？民主党在进入新一届国会时否认党派分歧
summary: Incoming lawmakers have more in common with each other than they have divisions, even across ideological factions Democrats who won in the midterms, including those in places previously considered off the blue map and those in Democratic strongholds, crafted t
summary_zh: 即将上任的立法者之间的共同点多于分歧，即使是在意识形态派别之间，在中期选举中获胜的民主党人也是如此。
body_en: Incoming lawmakers have more in common with each other than they have divisions, even across ideological factions

D emocrats who won in the midterms, including those in places previously considered off the blue map and those in Democratic strongholds, crafted their campaigns around economic populism and accountability.

Lawmakers in the anti-establishment incoming congressional class have more in common with each other than divisions, even across ideological factions. Voters sent a resounding message to work on affordability and rein in the Trump administration, and Democrats across the party have many more shared goals than Republicans, who face a more existential level of discord.
Who is Chris Van Hollen? The senator challenging Schumer as a progressive voice for Democrats

The challenge comes when this class of newcomers meets a Washington machine that they view as stuck to the status quo, and as they confront institutional barriers – and a president with a veto pen at the ready – that could prevent them from installing the tangible changes voters demanded.

But, political operatives and officials said, the shared agenda is clear, and Democrats need to stay focused on it, lest they lose the seats they just won in parts of the country where they previously weren’t getting traction.

“They got to just keep being who they are,” said Joe Maxwell, president of Farm Action Fund, a non-profit focused on building back rural communities. “There’s a whole different rhythm and politics and narrative to be able to be effective in Washington DC.”

Before the new lawmakers take their oath of office, they will have to decide whether to keep their party’s leaders. In the US Senate , Chris Van Hollen announced a challenge to longtime leader Chuck Schumer. On the House side, Hakeem Jeffries so far appears to have the speaker job.
In a speech at the Democrats’ meetup in Denver on Friday, Van Hollen said his bid was a response to voters’ calls for a political system that serves them.

“We should not be preserving our institutions if they are not delivering for the American people,” he continued. “And we should be making delivering for the American people the single mission of our government, even when that means shaking things up.”
Disagreements over a leader don’t mean there are deep disagreements on the path forward, though, Democrats insist.

“There’s a very small set of consultants and self-interested commentators and donor-aligned op-ed writers who are crashing out on the internet right now,” said Maurice Mitchell, the leader of the Working Families party. “I think it would be a distraction to focus on a factional fight that they are so thirsty for, when Tuesday suggested that you should be past the narrow politics of factionalism inside the Democratic party.”

This month’s wins present a “generational opportunity” to deliver results for the American people, Mitchell said, and trying to fit that into a “narrow framework” that pits moderates versus progressives misses the point.
“We just want to get things done, and we think that there’s a big terrain to get things done,” he said.

The Democratic party once again becomes a big tent, full of people from different parts of the country with varying life experiences. Because so many different Democrats got elected, there is an “interesting mix of basically a slice of America governing”, said Jane Kleeb, the chair of the Nebraska Democratic party.
“For me, that means we’re going to have a much more durable party,” she said. “It’s not going to be a one-note party.”

As former CBS News journalist John Dickerson put it : “A party big enough to win everywhere has to hold people who disagree. The tension comes with winning. When coverage treats that tension as a crack-up or a flaw, it mistakes how the game works for a threat to the game. Tackling isn’t an obstacle to football. Tackling is football.”

Newly elected Democratic lawmakers have expressed a willingness to talk to anyone. They’ve highlighted speaking with voters who disagreed with them on the campaign trail and ran against how both parties do politics. Abdul El-Sayed, the progressive who won the US Senate race in Michigan, has said Trump can call Medicare for All “Trumpcare for All” if he wants, as long as it makes it into law.

Some new members will join multiple Democratic caucuses that may seem to have competing ideologies. Indeed, the various caucuses announced big increases in membership after the election, from the progressive to the centrist New Democrats. Sam Forstag, a smoke jumper who flipped a congressional district in Montana, joined both the Progressive and Blue Dog caucuses, saying he would be one of few Democrats sitting in both. Being in both rooms would give him “a chance to fight for populist economic policies that are actually going to help working people and finally put us all back at the front of the line”, he said.
body_zh: 即将上任的立法者之间的共同点多于分歧，即使在意识形态派别之间也是如此
在中期选举中获胜的民主党人，包括那些以前被认为在蓝色地图之外的地方和民主党据点的民主党人，围绕经济民粹主义和问责制制定了竞选活动。
即将上任的反建制国会阶层议员之间的共同点多于分歧，即使是在不同的意识形态派别之间也是如此。选民们发出了响亮的信息，要求致力于提高负担能力和控制特朗普政府，全党民主党人比共和党人有更多的共同目标，而共和党人面临着更存在的不和谐。
克里斯·范霍伦是谁？参议员挑战舒默作为民主党的进步声音
当这类新来者遇到他们认为固守现状的华盛顿机器时，当他们面临体制障碍 — — 以及一位准备好否决笔的总统 — — 这可能会阻止他们实施选民要求的切实变革时，挑战就来了。
但是，政治人士和官员表示，共同的议程是明确的，民主党人需要继续关注它，以免他们失去在他们之前没有获得支持的国家部分地区刚刚赢得的席位。
“他们必须继续做自己，”农场行动基金总裁乔·麦克斯韦说，该基金是一家致力于重建农村社区的非营利组织。 “要在华盛顿特区发挥作用，需要完全不同的节奏、政治和叙事。”
在新议员宣誓就职之前，他们必须决定是否保留本党领导人。在美国参议院，克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 宣布向长期领导人查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 发起挑战。在众议院方面，哈基姆·杰弗里斯到目前为止似乎担任议长一职。
周五在丹佛举行的民主党聚会上发表讲话时，范霍伦表示，他的竞选是对选民要求建立一个为他们服务的政治制度的呼声的回应。
他在科罗拉多州举行的由多数民主党主办的峰会上表示：“如果我们的机构不能为美国人民带来好处，我们就不应该保留它们。” “我们应该把为美国人民服务作为我们政府的唯一使命，即使这意味着要改变现状。”
不过，民主党人坚称，对领导人的分歧并不意味着在前进道路上存在深刻分歧。
“现在有一小部分顾问、自私的评论员和与捐助者结盟的专栏作家在互联网上崩溃，”工作家庭党领袖莫里斯·米切尔说。 “我认为，当周二建议你应该超越民主党内部狭隘的派系政治时，专注于他们如此渴望的派系斗争会分散注意力。”
米切尔说，本月的胜利提供了一个为美国人民带来成果的“一代人的机会”，试图将其纳入一个让温和派与进步派对立的“狭隘框架”中，但没有抓住要点。
“我们只是想把事情做好，而且我们认为完成事情有很大的空间，”他说。
民主党再次成为一个大帐篷，里面挤满了来自全国各地、有着不同生活经历的人。内布拉斯加州民主党主席简·克利布表示，由于有如此多不同的民主党人当选，因此“基本上是美国执政的一部分的有趣组合”。
“对我来说，这意味着我们将举办一个更持久的派对，”她说。 “这不会是一场单调的派对。”
正如前哥伦比亚广播公司新闻记者约翰·迪克森所说：“一个足够大的政党要想在所有地方获胜，就必须容纳不同意见的人。胜利伴随着紧张。当报道将这种紧张视为一种崩溃或缺陷时，它就会错误地认为比赛的运作方式是对比赛的威胁。抢断不是足球的障碍。抢断就是足球。”
新当选的民主党议员表示愿意与任何人交谈。他们强调与在竞选过程中与他们意见不同并反对两党政治方式的选民进行交谈。在密歇根州赢得美国参议院竞选的进步人士阿卜杜勒·赛义德表示，如果特朗普愿意，他可以将全民医疗保险称为“全民医疗保险”，只要将其纳入法律即可。

一些新成员将加入多个民主党核心小组，这些小组似乎具有相互竞争的意识形态。事实上，选举后各个党团会议都宣布大幅增加成员数量，从进步派到中间派新民主党。萨姆·福斯塔格 (Sam Forstag) 是一名跳伞运动员，他推翻了蒙大拿州的一个国会选区，他同时参加了进步党和蓝狗党团会议，并表示他将是同时参加这两个党团的少数民主党人之一。他说，在这两个房间里，他将“有机会为民粹主义经济政策而奋斗，这些政策实际上会帮助劳动人民，并最终让我们所有人重新站在前线”。

title_en: How ICE raids in Kansas meatpacking country sparked fury – and turned voters against Trump
title_zh: ICE 在堪萨斯州肉类加工国家的突袭如何引发愤怒，并让选民反对特朗普
summary: In region where migrants have settled to work at abattoirs and feedyards, harsh raids pushed people to vote Democrat José Del Real looked over the crowd from the stage in a park, at hundreds of his neighbors with furious signs tucked under their arms, voicing
summary_zh: 在移民定居在屠宰场和饲料场工作的地区，严厉的突袭迫使人们投票给民主党人何塞·德尔·雷亚尔（José Del Real）。
body_en: In region where migrants have settled to work at abattoirs and feedyards, harsh raids pushed people to vote Democrat

J osé Del Real looked over the crowd from the stage in a park, at hundreds of his neighbors with furious signs tucked under their arms, voicing their anger at immigration agents who had descended on their town and started rounding up their friends and family. His daughters, in the front row, were crying.

Del Real, an army veteran who served two tours in Iraq, hadn’t voted in a decade. He thought it would not matter in this ruby red corner of Kansas . But the midterm election was weeks away. He draped an American flag over his shoulders, put on his Iraq veteran cap and ended his speech with a message: “None of this matters if you do not vote. Let’s go vote.”

They did. This county and two of its neighbors in south-western Kansas, Republican strongholds where a steady stream of immigrants have settled over the decades to work at feedlots and slaughterhouses, swung wildly to the left. The shift helped elect a Democratic US Senator from Kansas for the first time in nearly a century, signaling the limits of Donald Trump’s aggressive deportation agenda.

Since Democrats won back control of Congress in a decisive rebuke to Republicans, Trump has sent mixed messages about how he plans to handle immigration enforcement going forward. He suggested that his approach to deportations was too harsh but also named hardliner Stephen Miller as his new White House chief of staff. Both parties will be recalibrating their approach ahead of the next presidential campaign.
Here in Kansas, late September raids ignited a maelstrom of rage, turning many who had been apathetic, like Del Real, into determined voters.

Masked officers in tactical gear banged on doors before dawn. They stopped cars in the middle of intersections. Businesses shuttered. Families feared leaving their houses. Children stopped going to school. Some live-streamed themselves being detained. One man pleaded “God help me” in Spanish, his hands shaking, as he asked anyone watching to let his family know.

The resistance came not only from Democrats or the Latino population, which has grown to about two-thirds of Dodge City. Kansas’s embattled Republican senator, Roger Marshall, who would lose his reelection bid to Adam Hamilton, issued a statement pleading with the administration to consult local officials before launching raids.
Del Real regrets he didn’t vote in 2024, when Trump roared back into office pledging mass deportations.
“We had to see it in front of us,” Del Real said. “I had to see it in the flesh.”

This corner of Kansas is responsible for much of the country’s beef. The gates leading into Dodge City boast that it’s the “Queen of the Cowtowns” Its main street is named after the classic western set here, Gunsmoke. Murals celebrating cowboy history mix with evidence of a changing culture: storefronts showcasing quinceañera dresses, Mexican bakeries, city signs printed in both Spanish and English.

Del Real’s family came from Mexico when he was a kindergartner. Like most here, they came to work. The area – Dodge City and the region’s other hubs, Garden City and Liberal – is known as the Golden Triangle of Meatpacking, responsible for about a quarter of the US beef supply.
Some here thought their importance to the nation’s food might spare them from the administration’s deportation campaigns, said Amy Soberanes, a 25-year-old local organizer.
Soberanes, the daughter of Mexican immigrants, said she and others tried for years to get people – particularly their young, Latino neighbors – engaged.
But, from rural Kansas, immigration raids in places like Minneapolis and Chicago felt abstract.
Then they saw their own streets in social media videos.

People were furious, said Soberanes, who worried the daily protests could get out of hand. They told people not to slash tires or break windows, to store up their anger and take it out on election day.
“We’ll see them at the ballot box,” she recalls repeating.
body_zh: 在移民定居在屠宰场和饲料场工作的地区，严厉的突袭迫使人们投票给民主党
何塞·德尔·雷亚尔（José Del Real）在公园的舞台上俯瞰人群，看着数百名腋下夹着愤怒标语的邻居，向来到他们小镇并开始围捕他们的朋友和家人的移民官员表达了他们的愤怒。他的女儿们坐在前排，正在哭泣。
德尔·雷亚尔是一名退伍军人，曾两次前往伊拉克服役，他已经十年没有投票了。他认为在堪萨斯这个红宝石色的角落里这并不重要。但距离中期选举还有几周时间。他将一面美国国旗披在肩上，戴上伊拉克退伍军人的帽子，并以这样的信息结束了他的演讲：“如果你不投票，这一切都无关紧要。让我们去投票吧。”
他们做到了。这个县及其位于堪萨斯州西南部的两个邻县，都是共和党的大本营，几十年来源源不断的移民在这里定居，在饲养场和屠宰场工作，这些县都疯狂地左转。这一转变帮助堪萨斯州近一个世纪以来首次选出了一位民主党美国参议员，这表明唐纳德·特朗普激进的驱逐议程存在局限性。
自从民主党通过对共和党的果断谴责重新赢得国会控制权以来，特朗普就他计划如何处理未来的移民执法问题发出了复杂的信息。他表示，他的驱逐方式过于严厉，但也任命强硬派斯蒂芬·米勒为新任白宫幕僚长。双方都将在下一次总统竞选之前重新调整他们的策略。
在堪萨斯州，九月底的突袭激起了愤怒的漩涡，使许多像德尔·雷亚尔这样冷漠的人变成了坚定的选民。
黎明前，身着战术装备的蒙面警察敲门。他们把车停在十字路口中间。企业纷纷关门。家人害怕离开自己的家。孩子们停止上学。一些人直播了自己被拘留的情况。一名男子用西班牙语恳求“上帝帮助我”，他的双手颤抖着，并要求观看的人告诉他的家人。
抵制不仅来自民主党或拉丁裔人口，道奇城的拉丁裔人口已占到三分之二左右。堪萨斯州陷入困境的共和党参议员罗杰·马歇尔在连任竞选中输给了亚当·汉密尔顿，他发表声明，恳求政府在发动突袭之前咨询当地官员。
德尔·雷亚尔很遗憾自己没有在 2024 年投票，当时特朗普咆哮着重新上任，承诺大规模驱逐出境。
“我们必须看到它就在我们面前，”德尔雷亚尔说。 “我必须亲眼目睹它。”
堪萨斯州的这个角落出产了全国大部分的牛肉。通往道奇城的大门被誉为“牛镇女王”，其主要街道以这里的经典西部片《枪烟》命名。庆祝牛仔历史的壁画与不断变化的文化证据相结合：展示成人礼服装的店面、墨西哥面包店、用西班牙语和英语印制的城市标志。
德尔·雷亚尔（Del Real）上幼儿园时，他的家人来自墨西哥。像这里的大多数人一样，他们来上班。该地区——道奇城以及该地区的其他中心花园城和自由城——被称为肉类加工金三角，负责美国约四分之一的牛肉供应。
25 岁的当地组织者艾米·索贝拉内斯 (Amy Soberanes) 表示，这里的一些人认为，他们对国家粮食的重要性可能会让他们免受政府的驱逐行动。
墨西哥移民的女儿索贝拉内斯说，她和其他人多年来一直试图让人们——尤其是年轻的拉丁裔邻居——参与进来。
但是，在堪萨斯州农村地区，明尼阿波利斯和芝加哥等地的移民突袭让人感觉很抽象。
然后他们在社交媒体视频中看到了自己的街道。
索贝拉内斯说，人们非常愤怒，他担心每天的抗议活动可能会失控。他们告诉人们不要割轮胎或打破窗户，要储存愤怒并在选举日发泄出来。
“我们会在投票箱见到他们，”她回忆道。

title_en: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout
title_zh: 政治周：参议院领袖之战；年轻且独立的中期投票率
summary: The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.
summary_zh: 美国参议院下一任多数党领袖的争夺反映了中期选举中年轻和独立选民的投票率。
body_en: Week in Politics: Battle for Senate leader; young and independent midterm turnout The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.
The battle over the next majority leader in the U.S. Senate reflects the turnout by younger and independent voters in the midterm elections.
Democratic senators gathered in Colorado yesterday, among them, Chris Van Hollen.

CHRIS VAN HOLLEN: This is about answering the call of the American people, because what I'm very afraid of is that their calls to end political corruption, their calls to end a rigged economic system will require that we organize the Senate in a different way.

SIMON: And that's the Maryland senator on his bid to try to replace New York's Chuck Schumer as the Democratic leader in the U.S. Senate. NPR senior contributor Ron Elving joins us. Ron, thanks so much for being with us.
RON ELVING, BYLINE: Good to be with you, Scott.
SIMON: What do you make of the senator's argument here?

ELVING: It has a lot of appeal, especially to younger voters, first-time voters, independents - the people who fueled this extraordinary Democratic surge, especially in the Senate races that Democrats won when nobody thought they were even close. And yes, the voters want an end to corruption and a rigged economy. But when Van Hollen says he wants to organize the Senate in a different way to achieve those ends, does he just mean a new leader, someone other than the longtime leader Chuck Schumer? What else do we know will change? And how do we know it will be better?

Schumer says he has the vote commitments for most of the Senate Democrats already. He needs 29. Some of his allies are saying he'll have 40 votes or more. But Van Hollen still has time to make his case, and in the end, the vote is cast by secret ballot. And I've seen leadership elections in the past where someone claimed to have the votes before they were cast but did not have a majority when the votes were counted.

SIMON: Let me ask about the House. What does it mean that a week after they won a majority, House Democrats couldn't pass a motion to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth because 11 Democrats didn't make it to the chambers to vote, which, of course, is what they're elected to do?

ELVING: There's a lot of anger about this out there, especially among people who wanted the Democrats to do a lot on Day 1. The problem is they won't actually have the majority in the House until January 3, when the new Congress convenes. So Day 1 for the new majority is still seven weeks away.

This week's vote on Hegseth was forced by a rogue Republican but scheduled and managed by the current Republican leadership. They got every other Republican who voted to oppose the impeachment - they are still the majority party. That's what made the difference. But there were no-shows for the vote in both parties. And in the final tally, it appeared that, had all the Democrats gotten there, they could have prevailed. And that, of course, assumes that the current GOP leadership would allow the vote to end that way when they had more Republican votes available, as well.

So how much difference did this vote make? Hegseth will still face investigations and impeachment when the Democrats actually do take over, and then the Senate will need two-thirds to convict and remove him. The Senate is more likely to do that in January with its new Democratic majority than it would have been with its current majority right now.
SIMON: You say Hegseth impeachment will be back on the agenda in January - perhaps also one for Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.?

ELVING: Those two names leap out - Hegseth for Iran, to be sure, but also for his wholesale demotion of generals and admirals and his efforts to instill his notion of warrior culture throughout the armed forces, Kennedy for some recent issues that have come up about his travels, but perhaps mostly because the measles outbreak has brought us fatalities and thousands of new cases, sometimes more than 200 in a week. In the first four years of this decade, we did not see 200 new cases of measles in a whole year.

Now, Trump has stood by both Hegseth and Kennedy in a way he didn't when the pressure was on some other members of his Cabinet, such as Kristi Noem with Homeland Security and Lori Chavez-DeRemer at Labor. So we'll see if he stands by these men in January, as well.
SIMON: And tell us about the mutual finger-pointing of the Trump administration over Nvidia and China and chip sales.
body_zh: 政治周：参议院领袖之战；年轻和独立的中期选举投票率 美国参议院下一任多数党领袖的争夺反映了中期选举中年轻和独立选民的投票率。
美国参议院下一任多数党领袖的争夺反映了中期选举中年轻和独立选民的投票率。
民主党参议员昨天聚集在科罗拉多州，其中包括克里斯·范·霍伦。
克里斯·范·霍伦：这是为了回应美国人民的呼吁，因为我非常担心的是，他们呼吁结束政治腐败、结束受操纵的经济体系，这将要求我们以不同的方式组织参议院。
西蒙：马里兰州参议员试图取代纽约州的查克·舒默成为美国参议院的民主党领袖。 NPR 高级撰稿人 Ron Elving 加入我们。罗恩，非常感谢你和我们在一起。
罗恩·埃尔文连线：很高兴和你在一起，斯科特。
西蒙：你对参议员的论点有何看法？
埃尔文：它有很大的吸引力，特别是对年轻选民、首次选民、独立人士——这些人推动了民主党的非凡崛起，尤其是在参议院竞选中，民主党赢得了胜利，而当时没有人认为他们接近。是的，选民希望结束腐败和受操纵的经济。但是，当范霍伦说他希望以不同的方式组织参议院以实现这些目标时，他是否只是指一位新领导人，而不是长期领导人查克·舒默？我们还知道还有什么会改变吗？我们怎么知道它会更好？
舒默表示，他已经承诺为大多数参议院民主党人投票。他需要 29 票。他的一些盟友表示他将获得 40 票或更多。但范霍伦还有时间阐明自己的观点，最终，投票以无记名投票方式进行。我过去见过领导人选举，有人在投票前声称拥有选票，但在计票时并未获得多数票。
西蒙：让我问一下众议院的情况。在赢得多数席位一周后，众议院民主党人无法通过弹劾国防部长皮特·赫格斯的动议，因为 11 名民主党人未能进入众议院投票，这意味着什么？这当然是他们当选的结果？
埃尔文：对此有很多人感到愤怒，尤其是那些希望民主党在第一天就做很多事情的人。问题是，直到 1 月 3 日新国会召开时，他们实际上才能在众议院获得多数席位。因此，距离新多数派的第一天还有七周时间。
本周对赫格塞斯的投票是由一位流氓共和党人强迫进行的，但却是由现任共和党领导层安排和管理的。他们吸引了所有投票反对弹劾的共和党人——他们仍然是多数党。这就是造成差异的原因。但双方都没有出席投票。在最终的计票中，似乎如果所有民主党人都到达那里，他们就可以获胜。当然，这是假设当前的共和党领导层也会允许投票以这种方式结束，因为他们也有更多的共和党选票。
那么这次投票产生了多大的差异呢？当民主党真正接管时，赫格斯塞斯仍将面临调查和弹劾，然后参议院将需要三分之二的票数才能对他定罪并罢免他。参议院在民主党新占多数的情况下，一月份这样做的可能性比目前占多数的情况要大。
西蒙：你说赫格斯弹劾案将在一月份重新提上议程——也许还有卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪的弹劾案？
埃尔文：这两个名字脱颖而出——赫格赛斯代表伊朗，当然，也因为他对将军和海军上将的大规模降级，以及他努力在整个武装部队中灌输战士文化的观念；肯尼迪是因为他旅行中最近出现的一些问题，但也许主要是因为麻疹疫情给我们带来了死亡和数千例新病例，有时一周就超过 200 例。在本十年的前四年里，全年新增麻疹病例并没有达到200例。
现在，特朗普以一种在其他内阁成员面临压力时（例如国土安全部的克里斯蒂·诺姆和工党的洛里·查韦斯-德雷默）所没有的方式支持赫格塞斯和肯尼迪。所以我们会在一月份看看他是否也支持这些人。
西蒙：请告诉我们特朗普政府在英伟达和中国以及芯片销售问题上的相互指责。

title_en: Ecuadorian fishermen who survived US boat strikes sue Trump administration
title_zh: 在美国船只袭击中幸存的厄瓜多尔渔民起诉特朗普政府
summary: US military has killed nearly 250 people in attack on ‘narco-terrorism’, and on 17 March, sank the 16 plaintiffs’ boat, leaving two with serious burns More than a dozen Ecuadorian fishermen are suing the US government after they survived a military drone attac
summary_zh: 美军在打击“毒品恐怖主义”的行动中已造成近250人死亡，并于3月17日击沉了16名原告的船只，造成两人严重烧伤
body_en: US military has killed nearly 250 people in attack on ‘narco-terrorism’, and on 17 March, sank the 16 plaintiffs’ boat, leaving two with serious burns

More than a dozen Ecuadorian fishermen are suing the US government after they survived a military drone attack in the Pacific ocean earlier this year that sank their boat and left two of them with serious burns from the explosions.

The 17 March attack on the La Negra Francesca Duarte II was part of the Trump administration’s Operation Southern Spear campaign, announced in November 2025 ostensibly to counter “narco-terrorists” it said operated in the Caribbean and Pacific.

The Washington office on Latin America (Wola) said as many as 250 people have been killed by the US military in subsequent attacks. The group considers the actions extrajudicial executions because the government has provided no proof that the victims were engaged in trafficking.

In the lawsuit seen by the Guardian, to be filed in US district court for the western district of Pennsylvania on Monday, the 16 fishermen insist they had no connection with the drug trade and were illegally targeted by the crew of an unidentified US military vessel about 385 nautical miles from the port of Manta as they returned from a two-week fishing trip.
Two armed drones, the filing states, exploded on their boat, setting it ablaze and destroying it completely, and two of the crew “were themselves set on fire and burned on their legs, arms and back”.
US military says strike on alleged drug vessel in eastern Pacific kills five people

The men say they jumped overboard and into small emergency boats that they rowed towards the vessel, pursued by a surveillance drone. They were greeted by US military personnel in camouflage uniforms who, they said, restrained them with zip ties and placed plastic hoods over their heads.

In an interview in June, the boat’s captain, Hernán Flores, described the moments after the boat he commanded for about 20 years was set alight. “Some guys looked for an extinguisher, but the fire was already spreading,” he said. “So some of our crew leapt into the water.”

The lawsuit seeks unspecified financial compensation for the attack, and for their subsequent “kidnapping and torture” that they say occurred when they were taken to a detention center in El Salvador and imprisoned for several weeks.

“They go out fishing, they don’t come home for a month, they’re like in a migrant detention center in El Salvador, and as we know those centers are not so nice,” said Dan Kovalik, a Pittsburgh-based attorney who is filing the lawsuit on behalf of the men.
“So there’s a lot of trauma there. It was catastrophic for them. They are home now, but they are struggling financially, and the two guys who were hurt bad are still dealing with that.”

Kovalik said the loss of the fishing vessel meant none of the plaintiffs had been able to work or support their families, and they were angry that, until their lawsuit, there was no recourse against the US authorities for what happened to them.
“They would also like the US to stop these boat strikes. That’s another goal of all this, and I think the US public and the media have been, honestly, not outraged enough about these strikes.”

The lawsuit states that the “manifestly unlawful” attack on the fishermen came soon after Ecuadorian authorities inspected the boat for themselves and determined it was not carrying drugs, nor its crew affiliated with any cartels.
It said the attack was illegal because, as with other strikes during Operation Southern Spear, it was conducted without congressional authority.
Additionally, the lawsuit alleges, “the wanton, willful and outrageous attacks upon, and kidnapping and torture of, plaintiffs at sea constitute torts under general admiralty and maritime law.

“There is no actual armed conflict that could justify the use of military force against the boats, nor was there one on March 17 when the attack took place. The US’s campaign of bombings against defenseless vessels and individuals violates long-standing and well-accepted international law.”
A spokesperson for the department of defense said in a statement on Friday: “As a matter of policy, the department does not comment on pending or ongoing litigation.”
body_zh: 美军在打击“毒品恐怖主义”的行动中已造成近250人死亡，并于3月17日击沉了16名原告的船只，造成两人严重烧伤
今年早些时候，十多名厄瓜多尔渔民在太平洋的一次军用无人机袭击中幸存下来，他们的船沉没，其中两人因爆炸严重烧伤，他们正在起诉美国政府。
3 月 17 日对 La Negra Francesca Duarte II 号的袭击是特朗普政府 2025 年 11 月宣布的南方之矛行动的一部分，表面上是为了打击据称在加勒比海和太平洋地区活动的“毒品恐怖分子”。
华盛顿拉丁美洲办事处（Wola）表示，在随后的袭击中，美军已造成多达 250 人死亡。该组织认为这些行为属于法外处决，因为政府没有提供证据证明受害者参与人口贩运。
《卫报》看到的诉讼将于周一向美国宾夕法尼亚州西区地方法院提起，在这起诉讼中，这 16 名渔民坚称他们与毒品交易没有关系，他们在结束为期两周的捕鱼之旅返回时，在距离曼塔港约 385 海里的地方遭到一艘身份不明的美国军舰船员的非法攻击。
文件称，两架武装无人机在他们的船上爆炸，将其点燃并完全摧毁，两名船员“自己也被点燃，腿部、手臂和背部被烧伤”。
美国军方称东太平洋袭击涉嫌贩毒船造成五人死亡
这些人说，他们跳下船，进入小型应急船，并在一架无人侦察机的追击下划向这艘船。他们受到身穿迷彩服的美国军事人员的欢迎，他们说，他们用拉链绑住他们，并将塑料头罩戴在他们的头上。
在 6 月的一次采访中，船长埃尔南·弗洛雷斯 (Hernán Flores) 描述了他指挥了大约 20 年的船被点燃后的情景。 “有些人寻找灭火器，但火势已经蔓延，”他说。 “所以我们的一些船员跳入水中。”
该诉讼要求对这次袭击以及随后的“绑架和酷刑”寻求未具体说明的经济赔偿，他们说，这些事件是在他们被带到萨尔瓦多的拘留中心并被监禁几周时发生的。
“他们出去钓鱼，一个月不回家，就像在萨尔瓦多的移民拘留中心一样，据我们所知，这些中心并不那么好，”代表这些人提起诉讼的匹兹堡律师丹·科瓦利克(Dan Kovalik)说。
“所以那里有很多创伤。这对他们来说是灾难性的。他们现在回家了，但他们在经济上陷入困境，而受伤严重的两个人仍在处理这个问题。”
科瓦利克表示，渔船的损失意味着所有原告都无法工作或养家糊口，他们感到愤怒的是，在提起诉讼之前，美国当局无法就他们所遭遇的事情向美国当局追索。
“他们还希望美国停止这些船只袭击。这是这一切的另一个目标，老实说，我认为美国公众和媒体对这些袭击还没有感到足够的愤怒。”
该诉讼称，在厄瓜多尔当局亲自检查该船并确定该船没有携带毒品，也没有与任何卡特尔有关联的船员之后不久，就发生了对渔民的“明显非法”袭击。
声明称，这次袭击是非法的，因为与南方之矛行动期间的其他袭击一样，这次袭击是在没有国会授权的情况下进行的。
此外，诉讼称，“根据一般海事法和海事法，对原告进行肆意、故意和无耻的攻击、绑架和酷刑，构成侵权行为。”
“不存在任何实际的武装冲突可以证明对这些船只使用武力是合理的，3月17日袭击发生时也不存在。美国对手无寸铁的船只和个人进行的轰炸违反了长期存在且广为接受的国际法。”
国防部发言人在周五的一份声明中表示：“根据政策，国防部不会对未决或正在进行的诉讼发表评论。”

title_en: Hegseth's failed impeachment was a warning to Democrats. Where will they go from here?
title_zh: 赫格塞斯的弹劾失败是对民主党人的警告。他们将何去何从？
summary: Democrats have been given a huge opportunity with majorities in both the House and Senate — but the balance of priorities, timing, messaging and discipline are all going to be major tests.
summary_zh: 民主党在众议院和参议院都获得了多数席位，因此获得了巨大的机会，但优先事项、时机、信息传递和决策之间的平衡
body_en: After the Hegseth impeachment failure, what will Democrats focus on? : NPR

After the Hegseth impeachment failure, what will Democrats focus on? Democrats have been given a huge opportunity with majorities in both the House and Senate — but the balance of priorities, timing, messaging and discipline are all going to be major tests.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., speaks during a news conference on Nov. 4, 2025, on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C. Tom Brenner/Getty Images hide caption
Democrats are not in the majority yet , but the first post-election test of their ability to get things done was a failure.

The House was unable to advance an impeachment effort of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Eleven Democrats were no-shows for the vote. Based on the math in this vote: If those 11 had been there and if no more Republicans showed up, the attempt would have gone forward.

Now, for those who want to see Hegseth impeached, it's fair to ask why only one Republican was in favor of it, Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky, who led the effort , especially after an election that saw GOP wipeouts in no small measure because of the Iran war? The GOP still controls the floor, so a Democratic speaker would have been able to leave the vote open longer for the 11 to be able to cast their votes.
House votes to effectively end the impeachment effort against Pete Hegseth

But it's also fair to ask if this would have happened under Nancy Pelosi's watch? (Ironically, she was one of the 11 who didn't vote for advancing Hegseth's impeachment because she had flown back to San Francisco for a veterans' event.) Or if this kind of effort is what people want in the first place.

First, on the Pelosi point: The former House speaker and retiring congresswoman was known for the discipline she kept in her caucus. She knew where the votes were, who was voting how and why – and, most importantly, did not move forward with efforts that didn't have the votes.

Hakeem Jeffries, the heir apparent Democratic leader , is going to have the largest majority in Congress since the early 1990s. His leadership and agenda priorities are going to be scrutinized and compared to Pelosi – and this wasn't a great start to this new era.
Second, on whether impeachments are what people want to see: it depends on which people. Certainly, the Democratic base — and some beyond that — wants accountability for the Trump administration.
Voters more broadly also said corruption was a top issue in the campaign. But walking the line between reasonable accountability and oversight versus impeachments is a potential tight rope.

Democrats will have to balance the mandate they were given to bring down prices (sound familiar?) and end the war with the accountability of the Trump administration that many in the Democratic base feverishly wants and expects.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll taken after the election, found that 8-in-10 people think Democrats' focus in the first 100 days should be on the cost of living, three-quarters said lowering health care costs, 7 in 10 said lowering gas prices, while 6 in 10 said ending the Iran war and eliminating President Trump's tariffs.
Hakeem Jeffries is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House

What about investigations and impeachment? Only 40% said investigating the Trump administration should be a priority in those early days. But 71% of Democrats do want this to be a first 100 days focus. Only 36% of independents said the same.
Almost two-thirds said they are concerned that Democrats will spend too much time on investigations, which included, by the way, half of Democrats.

When it comes specifically to pursuing impeachment of Trump, only 33% said they think it would be good for the country. On the other hand, 63% of Democrats do. Only 30% of independents said it would be good for the country.
More than half also said they think Democrats should at least make efforts to work with the Trump administration. That, however, only included 40% of Democrats.
body_zh: 赫格斯弹劾失败后，民主党将重点关注什么？ ： 美国国家公共电台
赫格斯弹劾失败后，民主党将重点关注什么？民主党在众议院和参议院都获得了多数席位，因此获得了巨大的机会，但优先事项、时机、信息和纪律的平衡都将成为重大考验。
纽约州民主党众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯于 2025 年 11 月 4 日在华盛顿特区国会山举行的新闻发布会上发表讲话。汤姆·布伦纳/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
民主党尚未占多数，但选举后对他们完成任务的能力的第一次测试失败了。
众议院无法推进对国防部长皮特·赫格斯的弹劾努力。十一名民主党人没有出席投票。根据这次投票的计算结果：如果这 11 人都在场，并且没有更多的共和党人出现，那么投票就会继续进行。
现在，对于那些希望看到赫格赛斯被弹劾的人来说，可以公平地问，为什么只有一位共和党人支持弹劾，即领导这项努力的肯塔基州众议员托马斯·马西，尤其是在共和党因伊朗战争而惨败的选举之后？共和党仍然控制着议席，因此民主党发言人本来可以延长投票时间，以便 11 人能够投票。
众议院投票有效结束对皮特·赫格斯的弹劾努力
但也可以公平地问，这是否会在南希·佩洛西的监督下发生？ （讽刺的是，她是 11 名没有投票支持推进赫格斯弹劾案的人之一，因为她飞回旧金山参加退伍军人活动。）或者如果这种努力是人们首先想要的。
首先，关于佩洛西的观点：这位前众议院议长、即将退休的女议员以其在核心小组中保持的纪律而闻名。她知道选票在哪里，谁在投票，如何投票以及为什么投票，而且最重要的是，她不会继续进行没有选票的努力。
民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 将成为自 20 世纪 90 年代初以来国会中最多的席位。他的领导力和议程优先事项将受到仔细审查，并与佩洛西进行比较——这对于这个新时代来说并不是一个好的开始。
第二，关于弹劾是否是人们愿意看到的：这取决于哪些人。当然，民主党基础——以及其他一些人——希望对特朗普政府负责。
更广泛的选民还表示，腐败是竞选中的首要问题。但在合理的问责和监督与弹劾之间行走是一条潜在的紧绳。
民主党人必须在降低价格（听起来很熟悉？）和结束战争的任务与特朗普政府的问责制之间取得平衡，而特朗普政府的问责制是许多民主党基础人士热切希望和期望的。
路透社/益普索在大选后进行的一项民意调查发现，十分之八的人认为民主党在前 100 天的重点应该放在生活成本上，四分之三的人表示降低医疗保健成本，十分之七的人表示降低汽油价格，十分之六的人表示结束伊朗战争并取消特朗普总统的关税。
哈基姆·杰弗里斯有望成为第一位黑人众议院议长
调查和弹劾怎么样？只有 40% 的人表示调查特朗普政府应该是早期的优先事项。但 71% 的民主党人确实希望这是第一个 100 天的焦点。只有 36% 的独立人士也这么说。
近三分之二的人表示，他们担心民主党人会花太多时间进行调查，顺便说一句，其中包括一半的民主党人。
当具体谈到弹劾特朗普时，只有 33% 的人表示他们认为这对国家有利。另一方面，63% 的民主党人则持此观点。只有 30% 的独立人士表示这对国家有利。
超过一半的人还表示，他们认为民主党人至少应该努力与特朗普政府合作。然而，这仅包括 40% 的民主党人。

summary_zh: 特朗普的语气转变只会增加这场战争接下来会发生什么的不确定性，这场战争在战争爆发之前没有征求美国盟友的意见
body_en: Aamer Madhani, Associated Press Aamer Madhani, Associated Press
Matthew Lee, Associated Press Matthew Lee, Associated Press
Ben Finley, Associated Press Ben Finley, Associated Press

WASHINGTON (AP) — President Donald Trump has had a lot to say about his thinking on the way ahead in the Iran war since Republicans were trounced in last week's midterm elections.

In exchanges with reporters, broadcast interviews and social media posts since Election Day, he's somehow managed to back away from carrying out additional strikes while also backing away from the prospect of additional talks with the Islamic Republic's negotiators on ending the 8-month-old conflict.

The president acknowledged on the day after the midterms that the war and the global economic tumult it's caused were partly to blame for Republicans' electoral losses, while maintaining it was the right thing to do.

Then, at the start of this week, he huddled with Qatar's prime minister at the White House and afterward told reporters that he believed it was highly unlikely he'd need to order new major strikes on Iran, declaring that the war "militarily is effectively over."

But by Thursday, he was again raising questions about whether he needed to rush to find an endgame. He declared that the U.S. no longer needs a deal with Tehran and brusquely directed Vice President JD Vance — who served as his chief negotiator in earlier peace talks with Iran — to shift his attention to the administration's domestic anti-fraud campaign targeting Democrat-controlled cities and states.
All the while, Trump warned Iran that the U.S. military is "locked and loaded" and keeping an eye on Pickaxe Mountain, a facility linked to Iran's nuclear program, for signs of activity.
"If something does not work out, I would not hesitate" to act, Trump told conservative broadcaster Hugh Hewitt on Thursday.
Iran war will shadow Trump during his trip to Asia

Trump's tonal shifts have only added to the uncertainty about what comes next in a war in which America's allies were not consulted before it was started but nonetheless struggle to deal with its economic ramifications.

"President Trump is now acting like an arsonist who has set ablaze our foreign policy," Democratic Sen. Cory Booker of New Jersey said in an interview Friday on the sidelines of the Democrats' postelection gathering in Denver. "And now he just wants to walk away."

The president's ambiguous positioning on the war is expected to loom large during a visit next week to the Philippines and the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meetings in the Chinese tech hub of Shenzhen.
WATCH: After midterms, world leaders await Trump's next move in Iran

While in Shenzhen, Trump will hold an unprecedented three-way summit with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin. Trump is expected to discuss Iran and the three powers' nuclear stockpiles with Xi and Putin.

The White House declined to comment directly to queries on Trump's postelection rhetoric on Iran. But Secretary of State Marco Rubio underscored that Trump's approach is leading to the Iranian economy collapsing.

华盛顿（美联社）——自从共和党在上周的中期选举中惨败以来，唐纳德·特朗普总统就他对伊朗战争未来的想法说了很多话。
自选举日以来，在与记者的交流、广播采访和社交媒体帖子中，他以某种方式设法放弃了进行更多罢工的想法，同时也放弃了与伊斯兰共和国谈判代表就结束长达 8 个月的冲突进行额外谈判的前景。
总统在中期选举后的第二天承认，战争及其引发的全球经济动荡是共和党选举失败的部分原因，但他坚称这是正确的做法。
然后，本周初，他在白宫与卡塔尔总理会面，随后告诉记者，他认为他不太可能下令对伊朗进行新的大规模打击，并宣称战争“在军事上实际上已经结束”。
但到了周四，他再次质疑是否需要急于找到结局。他宣布美国不再需要与德黑兰达成协议，并粗暴地指示副总统 JD 万斯（曾在早些时候与伊朗的和平谈判中担任首席谈判代表）将注意力转移到政府针对民主党控制的城市和州的国内反欺诈运动上。
与此同时，特朗普警告伊朗，美军已“上膛并上膛”，并密切关注与伊朗核计划有关的镐山设施，寻找活动迹象。
特朗普周四对保守派广播公司休·休伊特表示，“如果事情没有解决，我会毫不犹豫地”采取行动。
伊朗战争将给特朗普亚洲之行带来阴影
特朗普的语气转变只会增加这场战争接下来会发生什么的不确定性，这场战争在战争开始前没有征求美国盟友的意见，但仍在努力应对其经济影响。
新泽西州民主党参议员科里·布克周五在丹佛举行的民主党选后集会间隙接受采访时表示，“特朗普总统现在的行为就像纵火犯一样，点燃了我们的外交政策。” “现在他只想走开。”
总统对战争的模糊立场预计将在下周访问菲律宾以及在中国科技中心深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织会议上凸显出来。
观看：中期选举后，世界领导人等待特朗普在伊朗问题上的下一步行动
在深圳期间，特朗普将与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京举行史无前例的三方峰会。预计特朗普将与习近平和普京讨论伊朗和三个大国的核库存问题。
白宫拒绝直接回应有关特朗普当选后对伊朗言论的询问。但国务卿马可·卢比奥强调，特朗普的做法正在导致伊朗经济崩溃。

title_zh: 伊利诺伊州乙醇工厂发现炸弹后疏散区解除
summary: Peoria officials said a bomb was found at BioUrja Renewables and later defused; FBI said it is investigating Residents were ordered to evacuate parts of an Illinois community on Friday after the mayor there said authorities found a bomb at a local ethanol- and
summary_zh: 皮奥里亚官员表示，在 BioUrja Renewables 发现了一枚炸弹，随后拆除了炸弹； FBI表示正在调查居民被命令撤离零件
body_en: Peoria officials said a bomb was found at BioUrja Renewables and later defused; FBI said it is investigating
Residents were ordered to evacuate parts of an Illinois community on Friday after the mayor there said authorities found a bomb at a local ethanol- and alcohol-production plant.

The discovery reported at BioUrja Renewables in Peoria triggered a mandatory evacuation over a one-mile evacuation zone encompassing sections of that city as well as the adjacent municipality of East Peoria. Officials ultimately lifted the evacuation zone at about 1.25pm local time on Saturday – but only after making it clear there had genuinely been a bomb found and ruling out the presence of any other explosives.
“It is real – this is a real thing,” Peoria’s mayor, Rita Ali, initially said , according to local news outlet WMBD. “We know that is a real threat. We know it is a bomb.”
Illinois man arrested over alleged plot to attack Hindu place of worship, police say
Peoria’s police chief, Brad Dixon, said at a news conference early on Saturday that explosives technicians had rendered the bomb in question safe.
But Dixon asked for the public’s patience as investigators searched BioUrja Renewals’ expansive facility for other explosive devices, as the Peoria news outlet WEEK reported .
“We don’t know if there are other devices,” Ali remarked.

Meanwhile, Ryan Presley of the FBI, who is in charge of the bureau’s field office about an hour away in Springfield, Illinois , said agents would pursue whoever was responsible “tirelessly” and “bring them to justice”.
No arrests had immediately been announced, with authorities saying updates would be provided as an investigation into the case continued.

At about 7.05pm local time on Friday, the Peoria police department had announced that officers were “actively investigating a reported bomb threat at BioUrja Renewables”. The agency then urged “anyone who lives or works within a one-mile radius of the facility to immediately evacuate their homes and businesses until further notice”.

The police’s statement said the evacuation notice had been “issued out of an abundance of caution while officers and emergency personnel investigate the threat”, which officials initially referred to as a suspicious package. The city offered the Manual Academy school as a temporary shelter, and police said anyone who needed assistance evacuating their home or business could call for help.
“Most streets in this area have been closed off,” police also said.

In separate statement , the municipal government of neighboring East Peoria acknowledged that the evacuation zone associated with the package at BioUrja Renewables extended into part of that city. That area remained in effect as of 9am local time on Saturday, East Peoria’s government said .
A hockey game and a dance-themed charity event scheduled for Saturday had all been delayed, as WEEK reported .
And at least the Saturday portion of a Comic Con event scheduled to last through Sunday had been canceled, organizers said .
“This is not a hoax,” the Illinois state senator Dave Koehler said during the early Saturday news conference. “This has gone beyond that … This is serious. This is serious.”

In the Saturday afternoon update, Peoria police said “state, federal, and local law enforcement had conducted an extensive search of the BioUrja facility [and] … found no other items of concern at this time”.
Police said the evacuation order implemented on Friday would no longer have effect, and any closed streets would be reopened.
body_zh: 皮奥里亚官员表示，在 BioUrja Renewables 发现了一枚炸弹，随后拆除了炸弹； FBI表示正在调查
周五，伊利诺伊州一个社区的市长表示，当局在当地一家乙醇和酒精生产厂发现了一枚炸弹，当地居民被命令撤离部分地区。
皮奥里亚 BioUrja Renewables 报告的这一发现引发了一英里疏散区的强制疏散，该疏散区涵盖了该市的部分地区以及东皮奥里亚的邻近市镇。官员们最终于当地时间周六下午 1 点 25 分左右解除了疏散区，但前提是明确确实发现了一枚炸弹，并排除了任何其他爆炸物的存在。
据当地新闻媒体 WMBD 报道，皮奥里亚市市长丽塔·阿里最初表示：“这是真实的——这是真实的事情。” “我们知道这是一个真正的威胁。我们知道这是一枚炸弹。”
警方称，伊利诺伊州男子因涉嫌密谋袭击印度教礼拜场所而被捕
皮奥里亚市警察局长布拉德·迪克森 (Brad Dixon) 在周六早些时候的新闻发布会上表示，爆炸物技术人员已确保这枚炸弹的安全。
但据皮奥里亚新闻媒体《WEEK》报道，迪克森请求公众耐心等待，调查人员正在 BioUrja Renewals 的大型设施中搜查其他爆炸装置。
“我们不知道是否还有其他设备，”阿里说道。
与此同时，联邦调查局驻伊利诺伊州斯普林菲尔德办事处负责人瑞安·普雷斯利表示，特工们将“不知疲倦地”追捕肇事者，并将他们绳之以法。
当局尚未立即宣布逮捕任何人，当局表示，随着案件调查的继续，将提供最新情况。
当地时间周五晚上 7 点 05 分左右，皮奥里亚警察局宣布，警员正在“积极调查 BioUrja 可再生能源公司报告的炸弹威胁”。该机构随后敦促“在该设施一英里半径范围内生活或工作的任何人立即撤离家园和企业，直至另行通知”。
警方的声明称，疏散通知是“在官员和应急人员调查威胁期间出于高度谨慎而发出的”，官员们最初将其称为可疑包裹。该市提供手动学院学校作为临时避难所，警方表示，任何需要帮助撤离家园或企业的人都可以打电话寻求帮助。
警方还表示：“该地区的大多数街道已被封锁。”
在另一份声明中，邻近的东皮奥里亚市政府承认，与 BioUrja 可再生能源公司一揽子计划相关的疏散区延伸到了该市的部分地区。东皮奥里亚政府表示，截至当地时间周六上午 9 点，该区域仍然有效。
据《WEEK》报道，原定于周六举行的一场曲棍球比赛和一场以舞蹈为主题的慈善活动均被推迟。
组织者表示，原定持续到周日的动漫展活动至少周六部分已被取消。
“这不是骗局，”伊利诺伊州参议员戴夫·科勒在周六早些时候的新闻发布会上表示。 “这已经超出了……这很严重。这很严重。”
在周六下午的更新中，皮奥里亚警方表示，“州、联邦和地方执法部门对 BioUrja 设施进行了广泛搜查，[并且]……目前没有发现其他值得关注的物品”。
警方表示，周五实施的疏散令将不再有效，所有关闭的街道都将重新开放。

title_en: Mike Johnson: ‘Leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong’
title_zh: 迈克·约翰逊：“当出现问题时，领导者必须承担责任”
summary: Republican House speaker not running for re-election contrasts sharply with president who avoids accountability In his first interview since the midterm elections , the US House speaker, Mike Johnson , said that the Republican party’s crushing losses during th
summary_zh: 共和党众议院议长不竞选连任，与自中期以来首次接受采访时逃避责任的总统形成鲜明对比
body_en: Mike Johnson: ‘Leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong’ | Mike Johnson
Republican House speaker not running for re-election contrasts sharply with president who avoids accountability

In his first interview since the midterm elections , the US House speaker, Mike Johnson , said that the Republican party’s crushing losses during the 3 November elections prompted his decision to step away from party leadership.
“Leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong,” Johnson said on Fox News on Saturday.
The Republican leader, who informed aides on 4 November that he would not seek re-election for House leadership, said on Saturday that he reached the decision “pretty quickly after election night”.

“We worked around the clock, left it all on the field to win. We had to defy history, as you and I both know, it’s only happened twice in 90 years, but we did everything that we could to make that happen,” Johnson said. “But, you know, this was the a year where history was not defied …
Progressive versus moderate? Democrats deny party rift as they head into new Congress

“We don’t like the results,” he said. “But, real leadership, I’ve always believed, you lead from the front, and leaders have to take responsibility when things go wrong whether it’s individually deserved or not, that’s part of it …
“I’m going to remain in this fight, but from a role different than as minority leader in the next Congress,” he added.

Johnson’s decision came after Republicans suffered historic losses in this year’s midterm elections, with Democrats flipping key seats in Republican strongholds, including Texas, to seize control of both the Senate and House . It stood in sharp contrast to the reaction of Donald Trump, who has deflected all responsibility for the devastating losses suffered by his party, including defeats for at least 10 Republican Senate candidates in states where he held rallies in the closing weeks of the campaign. That number could rise to 11, should Alaska’s incumbent Republican senator, Dan Sullivan, be defeated.

As it stands, come 3 January, Democrats will have at least 55 seats in the Senate, and Republicans will have 44. In the House, Democrats will have at least 256 seats, while Republicans will have at least 169. Each party leads in four of the eight House races where votes are still being counted , and the final two seats will be determined in runoff elections next month in Louisiana. The Senate race in Alaska has not yet been called.

On Tuesday, House Republicans elected the congressman Jim Jordan, of Ohio, to replace Johnson next year, when Republicans will be the minority party in both chambers of Congress. Senate Republicans, meanwhile, re-elected the senator John Thune, of South Dakota, to continue as their leader.

Democrats have not yet voted on who will lead their party in the House and Senate when the new Congress convenes in January. The representative Hakeem Jeffries, of New York, currently serves as House minority leader for the Democrats, and is expected to become the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, while the senator Chuck Schumer, also of New York, currently leads Senate Democrats.
However, the contest for Senate leadership has intensified in recent days, after Chris Van Hollen , of Maryland, announced a challenge to Schumer for the position.

“In this election, the American people called for change. They called for a change from Donald Trump’s disastrous policies – but even bigger than that, a change from the status quo that isn’t working for working people,” Van Hollen said. “It’s now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership. This is not about any one person – it’s about answering the call of the American people. That is why I’m running for Senate Majority leader.”

Bernie Sanders, the progressive senator from Vermont, said this week that he would not support Schumer’s bid to serve as the Democratic leader in the Senate, saying that “the time is now for change”. Sanders then endorsed Van Hollen and outlined the stakes of that contest in a Guardian opinion article .
Senate Democrats are scheduled to hold a closed-door vote on 1 December .
Currently, Jeffries does not face a challenger, but he has faced resistance from some members of his party, including from several Democrats elected earlier this month.
body_zh: 迈克·约翰逊：“当出现问题时，领导者必须承担责任”|迈克·约翰逊
共和党众议院议长不竞选连任与逃避责任的总统形成鲜明对比
美国众议院议长迈克·约翰逊在中期选举后首次接受采访时表示，共和党在 11 月 3 日选举中惨败，促使他决定辞去党内领导职务。
“当出现问题时，领导人必须承担责任，”约翰逊周六在福克斯新闻中表示。
这位共和党领袖于 11 月 4 日通知助手，他不会寻求连任众议院领导，并于周六表示，他“在选举之夜后很快”就做出了这一决定。
“我们夜以继日地工作，把一切都放在场上以取得胜利。我们必须挑战历史，正如你我都知道的，这种情况在 90 年来只发生过两次，但我们竭尽全力来实现这一目标，”约翰逊说。 “但是，你知道，这是历史没有被违抗的一年……
渐进式还是温和式？民主党在进入新一届国会时否认党派分歧
“我们不喜欢这个结果，”他说。 “但是，我一直相信，真正的领导力是从前线领导的，当出现问题时，领导者必须承担责任，无论是否是个人应得的，这就是其中的一部分......
他补充道：“我将继续参与这场斗争，但我的角色不同于下一届国会的少数党领袖。”

约翰逊做出这一决定之前，共和党在今年的中期选举中遭受了历史性的失败，民主党翻转了包括德克萨斯州在内的共和党据点的关键席位，以夺取参议院和众议院的控制权。这与唐纳德·特朗普的反应形成鲜明对比，特朗普推卸了他的政党所遭受的毁灭性损失的所有责任，其中包括在竞选最后几周他举行集会的州中至少 10 名共和党参议员候选人的失败。如果阿拉斯加州现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文 (Dan Sullivan) 被击败，这一数字可能会上升至 11 名。
按照目前的情况，到1月3日，民主党将在参议院至少拥有55个席位，共和党将拥有44个席位。在众议院，民主党将至少拥有256个席位，而共和党将至少拥有169个席位。在仍在计票的八场众议院竞选中，各党派均领先四场，最后两个席位将在下个月路易斯安那州的决选中确定。阿拉斯加的参议院竞选尚未宣布。
周二，众议院共和党人选举俄亥俄州国会议员吉姆乔丹接替约翰逊明年，届时共和党将成为国会参众两院的少数党。与此同时，参议院共和党人再次选举南达科他州参议员约翰·图恩继续担任他们的领导人。
民主党尚未投票决定一月份新一届国会召开时谁将在众议院和参议院领导本党。纽约众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯目前担任民主党众议院少数党领袖，预计将成为美国第一位黑人众议院议长，而同样来自纽约的参议员查克·舒默目前领导参议院民主党。
然而，在马里兰州的克里斯·范·霍伦(Chris Van Hollen)宣布向舒默挑战这一职位后，参议院领导权的争夺最近几天变得更加激烈。
“在这次选举中，美国人民呼吁变革。他们呼吁改变唐纳德·特朗普的灾难性政策——但更重要的是，改变不利于劳动人民的现状，”范霍伦在社交媒体上发布的一份声明中表示。
来自佛蒙特州的进步派参议员伯尼·桑德斯本周表示，他不会支持舒默担任参议院民主党领袖，并表示“现在是变革的时候了”。随后桑德斯支持了范霍伦，并在《卫报》的一篇评论文章中概述了这场竞选的利害关系。
参议院民主党定于 12 月 1 日举行闭门投票。
目前，杰弗里斯没有面临挑战者，但他面临着党内一些成员的抵制，其中包括本月早些时候当选的几名民主党人。

title_en: 'We can't let them down' -- After midterm wins, Democrats turn to charting path ahead
title_zh: “我们不能让他们失望”——中期选举获胜后，民主党转向规划未来道路
summary: Democrats from across the country descended on Denver for a two-day conference to chart the course of their party after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.
summary_zh: 来自全国各地的民主党人齐聚丹佛，召开为期两天的会议，在中期大获全胜后制定党的路线。
body_en: Texas Senator-elect James Talarico speaks at the Mission Ballroom during the What's Next Denver political convention on Nov. 12, 2026. David Zalubowski/AP hide caption
DENVER — Democrats descended on Denver for a two-day conference that was half victory party, half sober look at the road ahead on delivering for the voters who elected them.

The "What's Next" conference, hosted by the group Majority Democrats, was scheduled long before Democrats outperformed expectations with their best electoral performance since Watergate. It brought together rising stars — like incoming Gov. Rob Sand in Iowa and Sen.-elect James Talarico in Texas — along with strategists, organizers, state and federal lawmakers and potential presidential contenders.

Held at a concert hall, with colorful artwork of party heavy hitters dotting the venue, Democrats attended sessions like "What Voters Want" and "What Needs To Change." The overwhelming emphasis from speakers was that Democrats have to earn back trust.
A compilation of posters on display at the What's Next conference in Denver on November 12, 2026. hide caption

"We won races in places where we haven't won in a long time, even in some places where we've never won. And the message shouldn't be that [voters] are fully embracing the Democratic Party," said Colorado Rep. Jason Crow in an interview.

"It took us decades to dig ourselves in a hole and to push people away from us, and it's going to take us more than one cycle to earn that trust," said Crow, who is one of the party's recruitment co-chairs.

Attendees cheer during the What's Next summit. Following the midterm elections, prominent Democrats and political insiders gathered for the event to evaluate election results, and debate party strategy. Mark Makela/Getty Images/Getty Images North America hide caption
Anderson Clayton, chair of the North Carolina Democratic Party, took the party to task for not investing more in the South and in Black voters.

"When we say that Black voters are the base of our party, then I ask why are we not investing in a region of the country that on Tuesday night just proved everybody wrong of what is possible," said Clayton to much applause. "Rural America deserves the investment from the Democratic Party and we must run towards communities that our party has run away from."
Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg said Democrats shouldn't rest on their laurels.

"I think we are adequately politically traumatized by the last few cycles, so that we will not draw the wrong lessons from all of this," Buttigieg said. "Because here's the thing: it is yet to be written whether what we just experienced is one more oscillation from one side to the other and back, or whether it is the beginning of a tectonic movement changing American politics."

He said Democrats can learn from the current White House on two fronts, by having: "a bias towards action and a readiness to get things done coming out of the gate and at the very same time a readiness to plan for the long-term," adding Democrats should come out of the gate strong, with a rapid-fire series of bills to lower the cost of living.

Presumptive next Speaker of the House Hakeem Jeffries told the audience he has plans to do just that, with a robust agenda that includes reversing Medicaid cuts, banning congressional stock trading and mid-decade redistricting, establishing a statutory right to abortion, and overturning the Supreme Court's Citizens United decision that did away with limits on political spending by corporations and unions.

The conference itself was peppered with potential presidential contenders, including Buttigieg, New Jersey Sen. Cory Booker, Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego, and California Rep. Ro Khanna, one of the few progressive speakers.
No one announced an official run, but many gave previews of their theory of the case.

"I do think it's important that whoever we hire to be the chief executive of this country knows how to run something, knows how to get stuff done, knows how to not just have a vision but knows how to deliver on it," Shapiro told reporters.

Someone who was previously kicking the tires for a possible White House bid — Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen — told reporters he's no longer considering it, as he instead pursues the top leadership post in the Senate .
Throughout the conference, Democrats debated whether and how to work with the Trump administration in order to deliver meaningful change for voters.
body_zh: 德克萨斯州当选参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科 (James Talarico) 在 2026 年 11 月 12 日丹佛下一步政治大会期间在 Mission Ballroom 发表讲话。David Zalubowski/美联社 隐藏标题栏
丹佛——民主党人来到丹佛参加为期两天的会议，会议一半是胜利，一半是清醒地审视未来的道路，为选举他们的选民做出贡献。
由多数民主党团体主办的“下一步是什么”会议早在民主党以水门事件以来最好的选举表现超出预期之前就安排好了。它汇集了新星——比如即将上任的爱荷华州州长罗布·桑德(Rob Sand)和德克萨斯州当选参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科(James Talarico)——以及战略家、组织者、州和联邦立法者以及潜在的总统竞争者。
会议在音乐厅举行，会场点缀着党派重量级人物的彩色艺术作品，民主党人参加了诸如“选民想要什么”和“需要改变什么”等会议。发言者压倒性地强调民主党必须重新赢得信任。
2026 年 11 月 12 日在丹佛举行的 What's Next 会议上展示的海报汇编。隐藏标题栏
科罗拉多州众议员杰森·克劳在接受采访时表示：“我们在很长时间没有赢过的地方赢得了比赛，甚至在一些我们从未赢过的地方赢得了比赛。而且传达的信息不应该是[选民]完全拥护民主党。”
“我们花了几十年的时间给自己挖了一个坑，把人们从我们身边赶走，而我们将需要一个不止一个周期才能赢得这种信任，”该党的招聘联席主席之一克劳说。
与会者在 What's Next 峰会期间欢呼雀跃。中期选举结束后，民主党知名人士和政治内部人士齐聚一堂，评估选举结果，并辩论政党策略。马克·马克拉/盖蒂图片社/盖蒂图片社北美隐藏标题栏
北卡罗来纳州民主党主席安德森·克莱顿指责该党没有对南方和黑人选民进行更多投资。
“当我们说黑人选民是我们政党的基础时，我会问为什么我们不投资这个国家的一个地区，周二晚上，这个地区刚刚证明每个人都错误地认识到了可能性，”克莱顿在热烈的掌声中说道。 “美国农村值得民主党投资，我们必须奔向我们党逃离的社区。”
前交通部长皮特·布蒂吉格表示，民主党人不应该固步自封。
布蒂吉格说：“我认为过去几个周期我们在政治上受到了足够的创伤，因此我们不会从这一切中吸取错误的教训。” “因为事情是这样的：我们刚刚经历的是否是从一侧到另一侧再返回的又一次振荡，或者是否是改变美国政治的构造运动的开始，还有待书写。”
他说，民主党人可以在两个方面向现任白宫学习，“偏向于采取行动，愿意立即完成工作，同时做好长期规划”，并补充说，民主党人应该以强有力的方式走出大门，推出一系列旨在降低生活成本的法案。
即将当选的众议院议长哈基姆·杰弗里斯告诉观众，他计划做到这一点，并制定强有力的议程，包括扭转医疗补助削减、禁止国会股票交易和十年中期重新划分选区、建立法定堕胎权，以及推翻最高法院公民联盟取消对企业和工会政治支出限制的决定。
会议本身充斥着潜在的总统候选人，包括布蒂吉格、新泽西州参议员科里·布克、宾夕法尼亚州州长乔什·夏皮罗、亚利桑那州参议员鲁本·加列戈和加利福尼亚州众议员罗·卡纳，后者是为数不多的进步派发言者之一。
没有人宣布正式竞选，但许多人预览了他们的案件理论。
夏皮罗对记者说：“我确实认为，重要的是，无论我们聘请谁担任这个国家的首席执行官，都知道如何经营某事，知道如何完成工作，知道如何不仅拥有愿景，而且知道如何实现它。”
马里兰州参议员克里斯·范·霍伦(Chris Van Hollen)此前曾为可能入主白宫而苦苦挣扎，他告诉记者，他不再考虑这一点，因为他转而追求参议院最高领导职位。
在整个会议期间，民主党人讨论了是否以及如何与特朗普政府合作，以便为选民带来有意义的改变。

title_en: Trump and Zohran sitting in a tree…
title_zh: 特朗普和佐兰坐在树上……
body_en: FRIENDS WITH (SNAP) BENEFITS: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled the latest perk of his chummy relationship with President Donald Trump, announcing a deal today that will give stores across the country more time to comply with changes to federal food assistance rules.
New rules from the Department of Agriculture, which took effect last week, required retailers to stock a greater diversity of products in order to continue receiving SNAP benefits.

Just before they kicked in, Mamdani signed onto a bipartisan letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins urging the Trump administration to delay implementing the new requirements. He warned the rules would threaten the viability of the city’s more than 10,000 bodegas and corner stores, as well as the New Yorkers who rely on them, if the stores could not meet the mandates in time and lost the ability to accept SNAP payments.

Now, after negotiations with Rollins and foe-turned-bro Trump, Mamdani secured a 90-day extension for small retailers to comply with the rules — not just in New York City, but nationwide. The extension starts Friday.
Mamdani said he personally escalated the extension request to President Trump after City Hall reached out to the federal government.

“What I told the president was that this is a rule that, if allowed to be implemented on the timeline as it was scheduled, would be one that would throw the lives of so many working New Yorkers into a real place of anxiety and chaos,” he said. “And the president took that concern seriously.”
Mamdani declined to share how often he chats with Trump — “I’ll keep the cadence of that between the two of us,” he said — but he emphasized their conversations are ongoing.
As the two executives approach the one-year anniversary of their unexpected bromance, today’s announcement serves as a reminder that Mamdani’s Trump strategy has largely paid off.

After a seemingly love-struck Trump emerged from the duo’s first Oval Office meeting on Nov. 21, the threat of an immigration enforcement surge on par with Minneapolis largely evaporated, eliminating a potentially explosive situation that at the time loomed over the mayor’s early days in office.

In February, Mamdani successfully petitioned Trump to release a Columbia University student who had been taken into the custody by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement and, as POLITICO reported this week , Mamdani has continued to make those requests privately to the president. The two have also discussed the federal government’s involvement in a massive development project that would span the Sunnyside Yard rail depot in Queens.
The price for these spoils has so far been one Mamdani’s base is willing to accept.

The mayor rarely, if ever, criticizes Trump directly. He demurs when asked by reporters about their private phone calls. And during a joint appearance outside Gracie Mansion in late September, when asked about Trump’s short-lived White House media ban, Mamdani only said that he himself supported having a variety of news outlets covering City Hall. — Molly Reinmann and Joe Anuta
NVIDIA AND BEYOND: Gov. Kathy Hochul isn’t worried that the scandal engulfing former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will impact the broader semiconductor sector.

“It’s a resilient industry,” she said today. “We’ve already planted the flag in places from Malta and all the way to Syracuse. New York’s economy will continue to be sound and continue to grow. This will not have an effect on meeting our obligations to continue the investments and create more jobs.”

New York has placed a massive, long-term bet on the industry, which has toeholds in the Syracuse area and the Saratoga County town of Malta, where Hochul appeared today to tout the groundbreaking of a new chip manufacturing facility.
Huang resigned amid allegations of multiple affairs, including a relationship with a woman who may be a potential Chinese spy .
The tech boom has helped lift Wall Street and swell New York’s coffers. A slowdown may spell trouble for the economy. — Nick Reisman
LEADERSHIP MOVES: State Sen. Liz Krueger told Playbook today she isn’t angling to chair the body’s housing committee.
“I’m not going to be the housing chair and I’m not lobbying to be the housing chair,” the Manhattan lawmaker said. “Several other people have voiced active interest and I think that’s great.”

“I actually think that whoever is willing to be the housing chair should recognize they need to probably make a six-year commitment to this assignment,” she added. “And I’m not actually planning necessarily to make an additional six-year commitment to the Senate.”
body_zh: 享有（临时）福利的朋友：纽约市市长佐兰·马姆达尼（Zohran Mamdani）公布了他与唐纳德·特朗普总统的亲密关系的最新福利，并于今天宣布了一项协议，该协议将给全国各地的商店更多时间来遵守联邦食品援助规则的变化。
农业部上周生效的新规定要求零售商储存更多种类的产品，以便继续获得 SNAP 福利。
就在他们开始实施之前，马姆达尼签署了一封两党致美国农业部部长布鲁克·罗林斯的信，敦促特朗普政府推迟实施新​​要求。他警告说，如果这些商店不能及时满足要求并失去接受 SNAP 付款的能力，这些规定将威胁到该市 10,000 多家酒窖和街角商店以及依赖它们的纽约人的生存能力。
现在，在与罗林斯和曾是敌人的兄弟特朗普谈判后，马姆达尼为小型零售商争取了 90 天的延期，以遵守这些规定——不仅是在纽约市，而且是在全国范围内。延期从周五开始。
马姆达尼表示，在市政厅与联邦政府联系后，他亲自向特朗普总统提出了延期请求。
他说：“我告诉总统的是，这项规定如果允许按计划的时间表实施，将会使众多纽约工薪阶层的生活陷入真正的焦虑和混乱。” “总统认真对待了这一担忧。”
马姆达尼拒绝透露他与特朗普聊天的频率——“我会保持我们两人之间的聊天节奏，”他说——但他强调他们的对话正在进行中。
在两位高管即将迎来他们意外的兄弟情谊一周年之际，今天的声明提醒人们，马姆达尼的特朗普战略已基本获得回报。
11 月 21 日，在两人首次椭圆形办公室会面后，看似陷入爱情的特朗普出现后，与明尼阿波利斯市相当的移民执法激增的威胁基本上消失了，消除了当时笼罩在市长上任初期的潜在爆炸性局势。
今年二月，马姆达尼成功请求特朗普释放一名被美国移民和海关执法局拘留的哥伦比亚大学学生，正如《政治》杂志本周报道的那样，马姆达尼继续私下向总统提出这些请求。两人还讨论了联邦政府参与一项横跨皇后区 Sunnyside Yard 火车站的大型开发项目。
到目前为止，这些战利品的价格是马姆达尼的基地愿意接受的价格。
市长很少（如果有的话）直接批评特朗普。当记者询问他们的私人电话时，他表示反对。 9月底，在格雷西大厦外联合露面时，当被问及特朗普短暂的白宫媒体禁令时，马姆达尼仅表示，他本人支持各种新闻媒体报道市政厅。 — 莫莉·莱因曼和乔·阿努塔
NVIDIA 及其他领域：州长 Kathy Hochul 并不担心 Nvidia 前首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 的丑闻会影响更广泛的半导体行业。
“这是一个有弹性的行业，”她今天表示。 “我们已经在从马耳他一直到锡拉丘兹的地方插上了旗帜。纽约的经济将继续健康并继续增长。这不会影响我们履行继续投资和创造更多就业机会的义务。”
纽约对该行业下了巨大的长期赌注，该行业在锡拉丘兹地区和马耳他萨拉托加县小镇立足，霍赫尔今天在当地宣传了新芯片制造工厂的破土动工。
黄因多项婚外情指控而辞职，其中包括与一名可能是潜在中国间谍的女性的关系。
科技繁荣帮助提振了华尔街并增加了纽约的金库。经济放缓可能会给经济带来麻烦。 — 尼克·赖斯曼
领导层变动：州参议员 Liz Krueger 今天告诉 Playbook，她无意担任该机构住房委员会的主席。
这位曼哈顿议员表示：“我不会担任住房委员会主席，也不会游说担任住房委员会主席。” “其他几个人也表达了积极的兴趣，我认为这很好。”
“我实际上认为，无论谁愿意担任住房主席，都应该认识到他们可能需要对这项任务做出六年的承诺，”她补充道。 “而且我实际上并不打算向参议院做出额外的六年承诺。”
