summary_zh: 考克斯企业继承人詹姆斯·“菲姬”·钱伯斯因涉嫌支持哈马斯而面临两小时的听证会 周五在西班牙高等法院举行了两小时的听证会
body_en: James ‘Fergie’ Chambers, a Cox Enterprises heir, faced a two-hour hearing about alleged support for Hamas
A two-hour hearing in Spain’s high court Friday on the US extradition request of wealthy leftwing activist and philanthropist James “Fergie” Chambers turned out to be a study in contrasts.

Chambers’s defense took most of the session to query the US citizen and detail irregularities in the Trump administration’s extradition request – several of which the Guardian has reported on – as well as the figures of Spanish law that would lead the three-judge panel to deny the request; while the prosecutor sped through his case, head down, asking Chambers no questions at all.

Notably, neither the judges or the prosecutor asked Chambers to address the insinuation in the extradition request that the wealthy activist had supported Hamas. Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money laundering charge and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

But the defense’s queries did allow him to speak for the first time since his 10 July arrest in Ibiza about events at the center of the case: 2023 protests against Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit in Massachusets and New Hampshire and 2024 transfers of $7.2m to Tunisia, where he lived at the time. The latter was buttressed with testimony from a financial expert.

On the whole, Chambers painted a picture different from the depiction contained in the extradition request, that of a violent backer of Hamas on the run from the US. At one point, he noted that his family’s next door neighbor in Tunis was the US ambassador.

The court will decide next week on extraditing Chambers. If the decision is affirmative, Spain’s council of ministers can reverse the court’s decision. This means Chambers’s extradition may be among the last decisions made under Pedro Sánchez, the socialist prime minister, before national elections on 29 November.

Friday’s hearing began with Chambers’s defense asking about his wealth. A self-described communist and anti-imperialist, Chambers sold stock back to his family’s business, Atlanta-based Cox Enterprises, worth about $250m in mid-2023.

Then he started a foundation, he told the court. He and the foundation’s three-member board decide on funding and ensure that no projects seeking support are under US sanctions, Chambers said. The foundation has funded an estimated 100 progressive and humanitarian projects in 20 countries, according to his partner, activist and actor Stella Schnabel – including, Chambers said Friday, organizations in Gaza working on issues such as “medical treatment for children, transportation out of dangerous areas and clean water and food”.
Two of the request’s three charges – riot and conspiracy to riot – are related to the late-2023 protests against Elbit.

Chambers detailed his participation in the protests: locking himself to a door, marching in the street and – in New Hampshire – standing in the road, speaking to the media and paying bail for four protesters who were eventually found guilty of misdemeanor charges and served 30 days in jail.

As for the $7.2m, the defense and a financial expert serving as a witness laid out how ten bank transfers from the US to Tunisia mostly went to sponsor the football club Club Africain – described by Chambers as “one of the largest football clubs in Africa” – and a sporting business Chambers launched while living in Tunisia.
“Is there any indication that the money went to support terrorist activities?” asked defense attorney Aitor Martínez. “None,” said financial expert Albert Deulofeu Schilt.

Then, in about 15 minutes of rapid-fire monotone, prosecutor Juan Hernández Villalba laid out a wholly different picture of Chambers as backing “an organized structure … aimed at repeatedly committing illegal acts … together with funds destined for terrorist organizations”.
He accused the defense of laying out the facts of the case “in a fragmented way … when what’s most relevant is an evaluation of the whole picture”.
“The extradition petition isn’t based on ideology or political statements, but on actions [Chambers] organized, financed and carried out, causing material damage,” Hernández Villalba asserted.
The actions against Elbit “were presented as a simple protest”, he said. “Nevertheless, the actions described by the US were planned for days … with objectively violent content.”
Given all this, the prosecutor said, “there are more than enough indications to consider … that [Chambers’s] funding was aimed at terrorism”.

Among the 100-plus people in varying time zones following Friday’s hearing on the court’s YouTube channel was Irish film-maker and journalist Sinéad O’Shea, whose documentary on Chambers called All About the Money makes its New York premiere this weekend . It covers the time period cited by the FBI affidavit underpinning the US request. O’Shea said that extradition case “builds a false narrative which begins with the protest in New Hampshire – a piece of vandalism at worst and for which people ended up serving 30 days. I saw myself the football club in which he invested in Tunisia and his donations to Palestinian and other charities are a matter of public record. It is impossible not to see this as a politically motivated case.”
body_zh: 考克斯企业继承人詹姆斯·“菲姬”·钱伯斯因涉嫌支持哈马斯而面临长达两个小时的听证会
周五，西班牙高等法院就美国引渡富有的左翼活动家和慈善家詹姆斯·“菲姬”·钱伯斯的请求举行了两个小时的听证会，结果证明这是一项对比研究。
钱伯斯的辩护律师在会议的大部分时间里询问了这位美国公民，并详细说明了特朗普政府引渡请求中的违规行为（《卫报》已经报道了其中几起事件），以及导致三名法官组成的小组拒绝引渡请求的西班牙法律数据；而检察官则低着头，快速审理他的案件，根本没有向钱伯斯提出任何问题。
值得注意的是，法官和检察官都没有要求钱伯斯回应引渡请求中暗示这位富有的活动人士支持哈马斯的问题。钱伯斯的案件是美国因涉嫌支持哈马斯而寻求引渡公民的第一起已知案件，这一指控显然与国际洗钱指控和向帮助加沙巴勒斯坦人的组织捐款有关。
但辩方的询问确实让他自 7 月 10 日在伊维萨岛被捕以来首次谈论了案件的核心事件：2023 年马萨诸塞州和新罕布什尔州针对以色列武器制造商埃尔比特的抗议活动，以及 2024 年向他当时居住的突尼斯转移的 720 万美元。后者得到了一位金融专家的证词的支持。
总体而言，钱伯斯描绘了一幅与引渡请求中所描述的不同的画面，即一名哈马斯的暴力支持者正在逃离美国。有一次，他指出他家在突尼斯的隔壁邻居是美国大使。
法院将于下周就引渡钱伯斯做出决定。如果裁决是肯定的，西班牙部长会议可以推翻法院的裁决。这意味着引渡钱伯斯可能是社会党总理佩德罗·桑切斯 (Pedro Sánchez) 在 11 月 29 日全国选举之前做出的最后决定之一。
周五的听证会开始时，钱伯斯的辩护律师询问了他的财富情况。钱伯斯自称是共产主义者和反帝国主义者，他在 2023 年中期将股票卖回给其家族企业、总部位于亚特兰大的考克斯企业 (Cox Enterprises)，价值约 2.5 亿美元。
他告诉法庭，然后他成立了一个基金会。钱伯斯说，他和该基金会的三人董事会决定资金，并确保寻求支持的项目不会受到美国制裁。据他的合作伙伴、活动家兼演员斯特拉·施纳贝尔称，该基金会已资助了 20 个国家的大约 100 个进步和人道主义项目，钱伯斯周五表示，其中包括加沙的一些组织，致力于“儿童医疗、危险地区运输以及清洁水和食品”等问题。
该请求的三项指控中的两项——骚乱和阴谋骚乱——与 2023 年末针对埃尔比特的抗议活动有关。
钱伯斯详细描述了他参与抗议活动的情况：将自己锁在门上，在街上游行，以及在新罕布什尔州站在路上向媒体发表讲话，并为四名抗议者支付保释金，这四名抗议者最终被判犯有轻罪，并入狱 30 天。
至于这 720 万美元，辩方和作为证人的金融专家列出了从美国到突尼斯的 10 笔银行转账，大部分用于赞助足球俱乐部非洲俱乐部（钱伯斯形容为“非洲最大的足球俱乐部之一”）以及钱伯斯在突尼斯生活期间创办的体育企业。
“有任何迹象表明这些钱用于支持恐怖活动吗？”辩护律师艾托·马丁内斯问道。 “没有，”金融专家阿尔伯特·德乌洛费乌·希尔特 (Albert Deulofeu Schilt) 说。
然后，在大约 15 分钟的连珠炮般的单调中，检察官胡安·埃尔南德斯·比利亚尔巴 (Juan Hernández Villalba) 描绘了一幅完全不同的钱伯斯画面：支持“一个有组织的结构……旨在反复实施非法行为……以及用于恐怖组织的资金”。
他指责辩方“以支离破碎的方式陈述案件事实……而最相关的是对整个情况的评估”。
“引渡请愿不是基于意识形态或政治声明，而是基于[钱伯斯]组织、资助和实施的行动，造成了物质损失，”埃尔南德斯·比利亚尔巴断言。
他说，针对埃尔比特的行动“只是一次简单的抗议”。 “尽管如此，美国描述的行动是计划了数天的……客观上包含暴力内容。”
检察官表示，鉴于这一切，“有足够多的迹象可以考虑……[钱伯斯]的资金是针对恐怖主义的”。

周五在法庭 YouTube 频道上举行听证会后，来自不同时区的 100 多人中有爱尔兰电影制片人和记者 Sinéad O’Shea，她的关于钱伯斯的纪录片《All About the Money》将于本周末在纽约首映。它涵盖了支持美国请求的联邦调查局宣誓书所引用的时间段。奥谢表示，引渡案“建立了一个虚假的叙述，从新罕布什尔州的抗议活动开始，最严重的是一场破坏行为，人们最终被判入狱 30 天。我看到了他在突尼斯投资的足球俱乐部，他对巴勒斯坦和其他慈善机构的捐款是公开记录的问题。不可能不将此视为出于政治动机的案件。”

title_en: Napping Kansas driver whose truck sped on to soccer field and killed two won’t be charged
title_zh: 卡车冲进足球场并造成两人死亡的堪萨斯州司机打瞌睡将不会被指控
summary: Authorities declined to file charges against napping woman whose truck accelerated on to field during youth game A soccer mom napping in her pickup truck when it suddenly accelerated on to the field at a Kansas youth tournament where her child was playing, kil
summary_zh: 当局拒绝对在青少年比赛期间卡车加速驶入球场的打瞌睡的妇女提出指控。
body_en: Authorities declined to file charges against napping woman whose truck accelerated on to field during youth game

A soccer mom napping in her pickup truck when it suddenly accelerated on to the field at a Kansas youth tournament where her child was playing, killing two people , won’t face criminal charges, a prosecutor has said.

Investigators believe the 34-year-old woman had failed to put the Chevrolet 1500 in park and likely put her foot on the gas pedal while sleeping at the Stryker Sports Complex in Wichita on 17 October. They conducted multiple interviews and even ran a test in the same parking spot with a similar vehicle.
“I cannot prove she consciously disregarded a tremendous risk to people on that field,” the Sedgwick county district attorney, Marc Bennett, said on Thursday.
Father pays tribute to son, six, killed by truck on Kansas soccer field

He acknowledged the public might find his decision strange. Bennett’s 28-page report listed possible crimes that might be triggered when a person causes the death of another person but said none fit the soccer field tragedy under Kansas law.
“If I could charge somebody, why wouldn’t I?” Bennett said at a news conference. “But I also have an obligation to stand up and say, ‘It’s not here.’”

The two people killed at the scene were Cole Adrian , six, and Nicholas Schafer, 35, both from McPherson, Kansas, police said. Ten others ranging in age from five to 68 were reported injured and treated at area hospitals.
The Wichita police chief, Joe Sullivan, said his department spoke to victims and families before the report and other information were released publicly.

“Every lead was examined. Every piece of evidence was reviewed. Every reasonable avenue available to us was pursued … Our responsibility is not to fill gaps with assumptions or speculation,” Sullivan said.
The report said the day started with the woman driving to the soccer field with three children. After two games, they left the Stryker complex for a meal and returned by 2.30pm for another game.

While one child went to a field to play, the mom and her two other children remained in the pickup truck. She said she was going to take a nap, and a daughter covered the windshield with a two-panel sunscreen, the report said. Less than an hour later, the vehicle began to move.
“There is no evidence to support the conclusion that she knew the truck was still in drive, or evidence to explain what motive she would have had to do so,” the report said.

Wichita police detectives ran an identical test. They parked a Chevy 1500 in the same stall and also in drive mode – and “the truck stayed in place until the accelerator was pressed,” the report said.
“We sat there and waited and waited,” Bennett said at a news conference. “After about 15 minutes we went, ‘This truck isn’t moving.’ … Tires against a 7in curb and it did not move.”
Investigators said they interviewed more than 30 witnesses. Blood tests showed no evidence of drugs that would have impaired the driver’s judgment, the report said.
The report said the woman awoke to screams inside and outside the truck and the feeling of the vehicle moving.
Bennett said people who immediately pulled the driver from the truck found her sleepy, “sobbing, at turns described as frantic, hysterical, saying, ‘I’m sorry, I’m sorry. What have I done?’”
body_zh: 当局拒绝对在青少年比赛期间打瞌睡的妇女提出指控，该妇女的卡车加速驶入球场
一名足球妈妈在堪萨斯州一场青少年锦标赛上打盹，当时她的孩子正在比赛，卡车突然加速驶入球场，造成两人死亡，检察官表示，她不会面临刑事指控。
调查人员认为，这名 34 岁的女子 10 月 17 日在威奇托的 Stryker Sports Complex 睡觉时未能将雪佛兰 1500 停入停车位，并可能将脚放在油门踏板上。他们进行了多次采访，甚至在同一停车位用类似的车辆进行了测试。
“我无法证明她有意识地忽视了该领域人们面临的巨大风险，”塞奇威克县地方检察官马克·贝内特周四表示。
父亲向在堪萨斯足球场被卡车撞死的六岁儿子致敬
他承认公众可能会觉得他的决定很奇怪。贝内特的 28 页报告列出了当一个人导致另一个人死亡时可能引发的犯罪行为，但表示没有一个符合堪萨斯州法律规定的足球场悲剧。
“如果我可以指控某人，我为什么不呢？”贝内特在新闻发布会上说道。 “但我也有义务站出来说，‘它不在这里。’”
警方称，当场死亡的两人是 6 岁的科尔·阿德里安 (Cole Adrian) 和 35 岁的尼古拉斯·谢弗 (Nicholas Schafer)，两人都来自堪萨斯州麦克弗森。据报道，另有 10 名年龄从 5 岁到 68 岁不等的人受伤，并在地区医院接受治疗。
威奇托警察局长乔·沙利文表示，在报告和其他信息公开发布之前，他的部门与受害者和家属进行了交谈。
沙利文说：“每一条线索都经过审查。每一条证据都经过审查。我们采取了一切可用的合理途径……我们的责任不是用假设或猜测来填补空白。”
报道称，这一天从这名妇女带着三个孩子开车前往足球场开始。两场比赛结束后，他们离开 Stryker 大楼去吃饭，并于下午 2.30 回来参加另一场比赛。
当一个孩子去田野玩耍时，母亲和她的另外两个孩子留在皮卡车里。报道称，她说她要小睡一下，女儿用两片防晒霜遮住了挡风玻璃。不到一个小时后，车辆开始行驶。
报告称：“没有证据支持她知道卡车仍在行驶的结论，也没有证据可以解释她这样做的动机。”
威奇托警探也进行了同样的测试。报告称，他们将一辆雪佛兰 1500 停在同一个摊位上，并且同样处于驾驶模式，“卡车一直保持原状，直到踩下油门”。
“我们坐在那里等啊等，”贝内特在新闻发布会上说。 “大约 15 分钟后，我们说，‘这辆卡车不动了。’……轮胎撞到 7 英寸的路缘石上，它就不动了。”
调查人员表示，他们采访了 30 多名目击者。报告称，血液测试显示没有证据表明药物会损害司机的判断力。
报道称，这名女子因卡车内外的尖叫声以及车辆在移动的感觉而醒来。
贝内特说，人们立即将司机从卡车上拉出来，发现她昏昏欲睡，“抽泣着，时而疯狂，时而歇斯底里，说，‘对不起，对不起。我做了什么？’”

title_en: Indigenous students retrace Lewis and Clark’s historic journey: ‘We can’t protect what we cannot see’
title_zh: 原住民学生回顾刘易斯和克拉克的历史之旅：“我们无法保护我们看不到的东西”
summary: Two centuries after the expedition, Indigenous students are conducting a new wildlife survey along the route In 1804, when Thomas Jefferson dispatched Meriwether Lewis and William Clark and their Corps of Discovery to explore the newly acquired land west of th
summary_zh: 探险队两个世纪后，土著学生正在沿途进行一项新的野生动物调查。 1804 年，托马斯·杰斐逊 (Thomas Jefferson) 派遣
body_en: Two centuries after the expedition, Indigenous students are conducting a new wildlife survey along the route

In 1804, when Thomas Jefferson dispatched Meriwether Lewis and William Clark and their Corps of Discovery to explore the newly acquired land west of the Mississippi, the president’s primary aim was political: Americans needed to establish presence, power and trade routes in these territories before the Europeans beat them to it.

But Jefferson, an ardent naturalist, had a secondary agenda. He ordered that the expedition also survey the flora and fauna of these landscapes. On their two-year jaunt across the western half of the country, Lewis and Clark kept meticulous journals of the animals and plants they encountered: bison, horned lizards, sage grouse, prairie dogs, wild licorice and catfish, among them. These observations were pivotal in shaping an early understanding of North American biodiversity.
body_zh: 探险两个世纪后，土著学生正在沿途进行新的野生动物调查
1804 年，托马斯·杰斐逊 (Thomas Jefferson) 派遣梅里韦瑟·刘易斯 (Meriwether Lewis) 和威廉·克拉克 (William Clark) 以及他们的探索队去探索密西西比河以西新获得的土地，总统的主要目标是政治性的：美国人需要在欧洲人抢先之前在这些领土上建立存在、权力和贸易路线。
但杰斐逊是一位热心的博物学家，他有一个次要议程。他命令探险队也调查这些地区的动植物群。在穿越该国西部地区的两年短途旅行中，刘易斯和克拉克详细记录了他们遇到的动植物：野牛、角蜥蜴、鼠尾草、土拨鼠、野生甘草和鲶鱼等。这些观察对于形成对北美生物多样性的早期理解至关重要。

title_en: Alaska voters aren't ditching ranked choice voting, top-four primaries
title_zh: 阿拉斯加选民不会放弃排名选择投票、前四名初选
summary: This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.
summary_zh: 这是阿拉斯加人第二次投票否决了废除该州独特选举制度的努力，选民于 2020 年首次批准了该制度。
body_en: Alaska upholds ranked choice voting and top-four primaries : NPR

Alaska upholds ranked choice voting and top-four primaries This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly.
A voter walks into a booth at the Valley Bible Chalet to cast his ballot on Election Day, Nov. 3, in Indian, Alaska. Lindsey Wasson/AP hide caption
A ballot measure that would have repealed Alaska's nonpartisan primary system and ranked choice voting has failed, according to an overnight race call by the Associated Press.
This is the second time Alaskans voted down an effort to repeal the state's unique election system, which voters first approved in 2020. A repeal effort in 2024 also failed narrowly .

This year, though, Alaska's system was under intense nationwide scrutiny, due to the inclusion of two candidates with the same name on the four-person U.S. Senate general election ballot. That race appears likely to move on to a ranked-choice tabulation.

"Alaskans of all political stripes have spoken: They want the freedom to vote for any candidate, regardless of party, in every taxpayer-funded election," Nick Troiano — the executive director of Unite America, a philanthropic venture fund that invests in nonpartisan electoral reform — said in a statement before the AP call. "At a time when most general elections across the country are essentially coronations, the Last Frontier is showing that a better way is possible. It is time to honor the voters' decision and move forward."

Just a few states have nonpartisan primary systems that allow voters of all political affiliations to vote on the same primary ballot. While California and Washington's systems allow the top two vote getters to advance to the general election, Alaska's system allows the top four candidates to move on. Then, if no candidate gets a majority of the general election vote, ranked choice voting is used to determine the winner.
Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins wins race for Alaska governor, replaces a Republican
Opponents of Alaska's elections say the current system is confusing and can be manipulated.

Those opponents seized on this year's closely watched Senate race, in which an independent candidate named Dan Sullivan was alleged to be a Democratic-backed spoiler recruited to siphon votes that were meant for the Republican incumbent, also named Dan Sullivan.
Democrats denied recruiting the independent Sullivan, who made the top-four general election ballot and has defended his candidacy.

However, proponents of Alaska's system have said that the state's ranked choice voting system could blunt the effects of any confusion. Voters had the ability to rank both Dan Sullivans and not rank Democrat Mary Peltola, for example.

Massachusetts voters this year decided not to switch to a top-two nonpartisan primary system. And during the last election cycle, in 2024, several states considered measures that would create a nonpartisan system similar to Alaska's. Voters rejected all of those ballot measures.

body_zh: 阿拉斯加州坚持排名选择投票和前四名初选：NPR
阿拉斯加州坚持排名选择投票和前四名初选这是阿拉斯加人第二次投票否决了废除该州独特选举制度的努力，选民于 2020 年首次批准了该制度。2024 年的废除努力也以微弱优势失败。
11 月 3 日选举日，阿拉斯加州印第安人，一名选民走进山谷圣经小屋的投票亭投票。林赛·沃森/美联社隐藏标题栏
据美联社隔夜举行的竞选电话称，一项旨在废除阿拉斯加无党派初选制度和排名选择投票的投票措施已经失败。
这是阿拉斯加人第二次投票否决了废除该州独特选举制度的努力，选民于 2020 年首次批准了该制度。2024 年的废除努力也以微弱优势失败。
然而，今年，由于在美国参议院四人大选选票上出现了两名同名候选人，阿拉斯加的制度受到了全国范围内的严格审查。这场比赛似乎很可能会进入排名选择表。
投资无党派选举改革的慈善风险基金Unite America的执行董事尼克·特罗亚诺(Nick Troiano)在美联社电话会议前的一份声明中表示，“各种政治派别的阿拉斯加人都发声了：他们希望在每一次纳税人资助的选举中自由投票给任何候选人，无论党派如何。” “在全国大多数大选本质上都是加冕典礼的时候，《最后的边疆》表明，更好的方式是可能的。现在是尊重选民决定并继续前进的时候了。”
只有少数几个州拥有无党派初选制度，允许所有政治派别的选民在同一张初选选票上投票。加州和华盛顿州的系统允许得票最高的两名候选人晋级大选，而阿拉斯加州的系统则允许前四名候选人继续前进。然后，如果没有候选人获得大选多数选票，则采用排名选择投票来确定获胜者。
民主党人乔纳森·克莱斯·汤姆金斯赢得阿拉斯加州州长竞选，取代共和党人
阿拉斯加选举的反对者表示，现行制度令人困惑并且可能被操纵。
这些反对者抓住了今年备受关注的参议院竞选机会，其中一位名叫丹·沙利文的独立候选人被指是民主党支持的搅局者，被招募来窃取共和党现任议员丹·沙利文的选票。
民主党否认招募独立人士沙利文，沙利文在大选选票中名列前四，并为自己的候选资格进行了辩护。
然而，阿拉斯加州制度的支持者表示，该州的排名选择投票制度可以削弱任何混乱的影响。例如，选民可以对丹·沙利文进行排名，但不能对民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉进行排名。
马萨诸塞州选民今年决定不改用排名前两名的无党派初选制度。在 2024 年的上一个选举周期中，几个州考虑采取措施，建立类似于阿拉斯加的无党派制度。选民拒绝了所有这些投票措施。

title_en: Perspective: A new kind of White House press secretary
title_zh: 观点：新型白宫新闻秘书
summary: With the White House press secretary job still left unfilled, maybe an AI assistant might be the answer?
summary_zh: 由于白宫新闻秘书的职位仍然空缺，也许人工智能助理可能是答案？
body_en: Perspective: A new kind of White House press secretary With the White House press secretary job still left unfilled, maybe an AI assistant might be the answer?
Dana White, UFC president and CEO, speaks in the James Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House Monday, Nov. 9, 2026, in Washington. Alex Brandon/AP hide caption
There has been no White House press secretary for almost a month. But have you really noticed?
Katie Zacharia held the position for 5 days in the middle of October, but her lone briefing was … brief and not well-reviewed.

After several secretary-less weeks, President Trump declared in an online post that he would ask Dana White, the head of the UFC, to take the job, calling him "a violent Fighter and Warrior." Reporters imagined how the CEO of a martial arts league might answer a sharp question with a swift kick to their journalistic chops. "What's the President's plan to bring down inflation?" Then, Bang! Thwap! Ooof!
The president later clarified that he, "was only kidding," about Dana White. He added wistfully, "You wouldn't mess around with him so much."

Even as the number of White House press briefings has declined during the second Trump administration, the president himself has had almost 500 "interactions" with the press: in interviews and press conferences, or impromptu Q&As at a ceremony, aboard Air Force One or while walking to the new White House helipad.

And, really, what is the need for a press secretary when a chief executive can announce whatever they want directly to millions of people on social media at any hour? President Trump posts dozens of times a day on his Truth Social platform, without those pesky reporters around to interrupt his message with fact-checking, contrary opinions or context.
I'd like to float another idea. Why not make the next White Press secretary an AI chat bot? That's how so many corporations now respond to customer complaints and inquiries.
They could call the new White House spokesperson Ben. As in Ben Franklin. Who doesn't like Ben Franklin?

When reporters call or log in to Robo-Ben and ask, "What is the president's response to President Putin's latest statement?" Ben might mellifluously reply, "I'm glad you asked that. I understand your interest." And nothing else. If White House reporters snap back, "But Ben, you're not answering the question!" Robo-Ben might respond, soothingly, "I understand your frustration. Thank you for your patience. Please stay on the line for our Media Satisfaction Survey."

body_zh: 观点：一种新型的白宫新闻秘书 由于白宫新闻秘书的职位仍然空缺，也许人工智能助理可能是答案？
UFC 总裁兼首席执行官达纳·怀特 (Dana White) 于 2026 年 11 月 9 日星期一在华盛顿白宫詹姆斯·布雷迪新闻发布会上发表讲话。亚历克斯·布兰登/美联社隐藏标题栏
白宫新闻秘书已经近一个月没有出现了。但你真的注意到了吗？
凯蒂·扎卡里亚 (Katie Zacharia) 在 10 月中旬担任该职位 5 天，但她唯一的简报……很简短，而且没有得到很好的审查。
在没有秘书的几周后，特朗普总统在网上发帖宣布，他将请 UFC 主席达纳·怀特 (Dana White) 接任这一职务，称他是“一名暴力的斗士和战士”。记者们想象着一个武术联盟的首席执行官如何快速地发挥他们的新闻才能来回答尖锐的问题。 “总统降低通货膨胀的计划是什么？”然后，砰！扑通！噢！
总统后来澄清说，关于达纳·怀特，他“只是在开玩笑”。他若有所思地补充道：“你不会跟他这么纠缠的。”
尽管在特朗普第二届政府期间，白宫新闻发布会的次数有所减少，但总统本人与媒体进行了近 500 次“互动”：在采访和新闻发布会上，或者在仪式上、在空军一号上或走向新的白宫直升机停机坪时进行即兴问答。
事实上，当首席执行官可以随时在社交媒体上直接向数百万人宣布他们想要的任何消息时，还需要新闻秘书吗？特朗普总统每天在他的真相社交平台上发帖数十次，周围没有那些讨厌的记者用事实核查、相反的观点或背景来打断他的信息。
我想提出另一个想法。为什么不让下一任白人新闻秘书成为人工智能聊天机器人呢？这就是现在许多公司回应客户投诉和询问的方式。
他们可以给新任白宫发言人本打电话。正如本·富兰克林那样。谁不喜欢本·富兰克林？
当记者致电或登录Robo-Ben询问“总统对普京总统的最新声明有何回应？”本可能会轻松地回答：“我很高兴你这么问。我理解你的兴趣。”没有别的。如果白宫记者反驳道：“但是本，你没有回答问题！”机器人本可能会安慰地回答：“我理解您的沮丧。感谢您的耐心等待。请继续拨打我们的媒体满意度调查。”

title_en: Legal scholar Stephen Vladeck on Texas' new Democratic AG and federal litigation
title_zh: 法律学者斯蒂芬·弗拉德克 (Stephen Vladeck) 谈德克萨斯州新的民主党 AG 和联邦诉讼
summary: NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.
summary_zh: NPR 的斯科特·西蒙 (Scott Simon) 与法律学者、乔治敦大学教授斯蒂芬·弗拉德克 (Stephen Vladeck) 谈论德克萨斯州当选总检察长内森·约翰逊 (Nathan Johnson)。
body_en: Legal scholar Stephen Vladeck on Texas' new Democratic AG and federal litigation NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.
NPR's Scott Simon speaks with legal scholar and Georgetown professor Stephen Vladeck about Texas Attorney General-elect Nathan Johnson, a Democrat, and what that could mean for federal litigation.

Possibly no state's politics will change more next year than Texas. For nearly three decades, Republicans won every single statewide race there. But this year, Democrats swept those statewide races, including one with huge national implications for the federal courts - Texas attorney general. Stephen Vladeck is a constitutional law expert and a professor at Georgetown University's Law Center, and he formerly taught at the University of Texas School of Law in Austin. Professor, thanks so much for being with us.
STEPHEN VLADECK: Thanks for having me, Scott.
SIMON: How did it come to be that the Texas attorney general's office has such a - I think I can refer to what is an outsized role in shaping national policy?

VLADECK: Yeah. It really was the brainchild of then-Attorney General Greg Abbott about 13 or 14 years ago, where he really viewed his job, as he put it, as waking up in the morning, going to work and suing the Obama administration. And that started this trend of the Texas attorney general basically becoming the lawyer general for right-wing litigants - for red states - either to challenge Democratic presidents or to challenge blue-state policies they didn't like. And that attracted many, many cases to Texas. So it really is an outsized role that Texas has been playing for more than a decade now.
SIMON: What high-profile cases would you point to in particular?

VLADECK: Well, you know, Texas has been the plaintiff in some of the biggest challenges to Obama- and Biden-era immigration policies. The DACA case started in Texas, the Remain in Mexico case. You know, it's not just that the attorney general of Texas has been spearheading these cases. It's also that this has basically brought other parties - private parties, other states - to try bringing their cases in Texas. Even the Trump administration has brought a series of cases about nationwide policies in Texas because the Texas attorney general's office has shown itself to be so solicitous. It's going to be a pretty radical shift come January.

VLADECK: The new incoming attorney general, Nathan Johnson, has already said he's going to abandon Texas' position in some of these cases. I suspect he'll drop some of the cases that Texas is currently bringing, including, just to take one example, efforts to challenge telehealth provider shield laws in blue states and to try to prevent doctors from prescribing mifepristone, an abortion-related drug, to folks in states where it's not legal. Texas might drop its litigation continuing to object to any kind of residual status for DACA recipients, the Obama-era immigration program.

And we might even see Texas use the powers that Republican attorneys general have harnessed over the last 13 years in the other direction, perhaps to go after private entities - Elon Musk obviously has a huge corporate home in Texas - and maybe even to sue Republican presidents. I mean, it would be, I think, not beyond the realm of possibility to have a Texas-versus-United States lawsuit that's now blue Texas against the Trump administration.
SIMON: Aren't federal courts in Texas in the Fifth Judicial Circuit still very friendly to conservative viewpoints?

VLADECK: They are. And so, you know, I think it won't be quite a mirror image of what we saw under Attorney General Abbott and Attorney General Paxton because you still have the reality that the federal appeals court in Texas is deeply conservative, probably more conservative than the U.S. Supreme Court. But I think just the fact that you no longer have Texas leading the way in sort of right-coded nationwide litigation - I think it's going to create something of a vacuum. And it's not clear that there are other states that have the same political structure, that have the same interests, that have the same resources to fill the gap that losing the Texas attorney general's office will create.

VLADECK: Mississippi, of course, already has slightly more complicated politics, as we saw, having just elected Senator-elect Colom. Louisiana's politics have always been a little more complicated in this space. I don't doubt that they'll try in some cases. But, you know, everything's bigger in Texas. And I think it's really hard to see from the outside just how much that particular office staffed up and, you know, was given resources to basically bring nationwide litigation on a regular basis. It's hard to imagine another red state, at least, that's going to have similar capacity without a substantial investment that would have to start, you know, right away.

SIMON: Let me ask you a Washington, D.C. question, if I might. It's the first time President Trump will face Democrats in control of both chambers of Congress. Democrats made a campaign pledge to investigate alleged corruption. Are they going to face roadblocks?

VLADECK: Well, I think there's no question that we'll see roadblocks. I mean, the Trump administration has already been putting out these memoranda by the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel, trying to identify new grounds on which executive privilege could be asserted to resist those kinds of investigations and inquiries from Congress - even perhaps for third parties to resist those kinds of investigations.

You know, we've seen already this week letters from the White House counsel and from the U.S. attorney in the Southern District of Texas, basically sort of lecturing members of Congress about the limits on their constitutional investigative powers. So I think there's no question, Scott, that, you know, whatever role Texas is going to play, whatever role Congress is going to play, the administration is going to be subject to a lot more litigation and oversight in the next two years. How much of that succeeds, I think, is going to be very much up to the courts and to the Supreme Court in the final analysis.
SIMON: Stephen Vladeck, professor at Georgetown University's Law Center. Thanks so much for being with us.
body_zh: 法律学者史蒂芬·弗拉德克 (Stephen Vladeck) 谈得克萨斯州新的民主党 AG 和联邦诉讼 NPR 的斯科特·西蒙 (Scott Simon) 与法律学者、乔治城大学教授史蒂芬·弗拉德克 (Stephen Vladeck) 谈论了德克萨斯州当选总检察长、民主党人内森·约翰逊 (Nathan Johnson)，以及这对联邦诉讼可能意味着什么。
NPR 的斯科特·西蒙 (Scott Simon) 与法律学者、乔治城大学教授斯蒂芬·弗拉德克 (Stephen Vladeck) 谈论了德克萨斯州当选总检察长、民主党人内森·约翰逊 (Nathan Johnson)，以及这对联邦诉讼可能意味着什么。
明年可能没有哪个州的政治变化会比得克萨斯州更大。近三十年来，共和党赢得了那里的每一场全州竞选。但今年，民主党横扫了全州范围的竞选，其中包括对联邦法院具有巨大全国影响的德克萨斯州总检察长。斯蒂芬·弗拉德克（Stephen Vladeck）是一位宪法专家，也是乔治城大学法律中心的教授，曾在奥斯汀的德克萨斯大学法学院任教。教授，非常感谢您和我们在一起。
史蒂芬·弗拉德克： 谢谢你邀请我，斯科特。
西蒙：德克萨斯州总检察长办公室是如何拥有这样一个——我想我可以指的是在制定国家政策方面发挥着巨大作用？
弗拉德克：是的。这实际上是大约 13 或 14 年前时任司法部长格雷格·阿博特 (Greg Abbott) 的创意，正如他所说，他真正将自己的工作视为早上醒来，去上班并起诉奥巴马政府。这开启了德克萨斯州总检察长基本上成为红州右翼诉讼当事人的总律师的趋势，要么挑战民主党总统，要么挑战他们不喜欢的蓝州政策。这吸引了很多很多病例来到德克萨斯州。因此，德克萨斯州十多年来一直发挥着巨大的作用。
西蒙：您会特别提到哪些备受瞩目的案例？

弗拉德克：嗯，你知道，德克萨斯州一直是奥巴马和拜登时代移民政策面临的一些最大挑战的原告。 DACA 案始于德克萨斯州，而“留在墨西哥”案则始于德克萨斯州。你知道，不仅仅是德克萨斯州总检察长一直在带头处理这些案件。这也使得其他各方——私人团体、其他州——尝试在德克萨斯州提起诉讼。就连特朗普政府也对德克萨斯州提起了一系列有关全国政策的案件，因为德克萨斯州总检察长办公室表现得如此热心。一月份到来时这将是一个相当彻底的转变。
弗拉德克：新任司法部长内森·约翰逊已经表示，他将放弃德克萨斯州在其中一些案件中的立场。我怀疑他会放弃德克萨斯州目前提起的一些案件，包括，仅举一个例子，努力挑战蓝色州的远程医疗提供商保护法，并试图阻止医生向不合法的州的人们开出米非司酮（一种与堕胎相关的药物）。德克萨斯州可能会放弃继续反对奥巴马时代移民计划 DACA 受益者任何形式的剩余身份的诉讼。
我们甚至可能会看到德克萨斯州将共和党总检察长在过去 13 年中所掌握的权力用于另一个方向，也许是为了追捕私人实体——埃隆·马斯克显然在德克萨斯州拥有庞大的企业总部——甚至可能起诉共和党总统。我的意思是，我认为德克萨斯州与美国之间的诉讼并非不可能，现在是德克萨斯州针对特朗普政府的蓝色诉讼。
西蒙：德克萨斯州第五巡回法院的联邦法院对保守派观点不是仍然非常友好吗？
弗拉德克：是的。所以，你知道，我认为这不会是我们在司法部长阿博特和司法部长帕克斯顿领导下所看到的完全镜像，因为你仍然看到德克萨斯州联邦上诉法院非常保守的现实，可能比美国最高法院更保守。但我认为，事实上，德克萨斯州不再在某种正确编码的全国性诉讼中处于领先地位，我认为这将造成某种真空。目前尚不清楚是否还有其他州具有相同的政治结构、相同的利益、相同的资源来填补失去德克萨斯州总检察长办公室将造成的空白。
弗拉德克：当然，密西西比州的政治已经稍微复杂一些，正如我们所看到的，刚刚选出了当选参议员科罗姆。路易斯安那州的政治在这个领域一直有点复杂。我毫不怀疑他们在某些情况下会尝试。但是，你知道，德克萨斯州的一切都更大。我认为从外部很难看出该办公室配备了多少人员，并且获得了资源来基本上定期提起全国性诉讼。至少很难想象另一个红色州将拥有类似的能力，而无需立即启动大量投资。
西蒙：如果可以的话，让我问你一个华盛顿特区的问题。这是特朗普总统首次面对控制参众两院的民主党人。民主党人在竞选时承诺调查涉嫌腐败的行为。他们会遇到障碍吗？
弗拉德克：嗯，我认为毫无疑问我们会遇到障碍。我的意思是，特朗普政府已经发布了司法部法律顾问办公室的这些备忘录，试图找到新的理由，可以主张行政特权来抵制国会的此类调查和质询——甚至可能让第三方抵制此类调查。
你知道，我们本周已经看到了白宫法律顾问和德克萨斯州南区联邦检察官的来信，基本上是在向国会议员宣讲宪法调查权的限制。因此，斯科特，我认为毫无疑问，无论德克萨斯州将扮演什么角色，无论国会将扮演什么角色，政府在未来两年都将受到更多的诉讼和监督。我认为，其中的成功程度最终取决于法院和最高法院。
西蒙：斯蒂芬·弗拉德克（Stephen Vladeck），乔治城大学法律中心教授。非常感谢您与我们在一起。

summary: City has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce threat, and saw 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths this year Fires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters, have become regular occurrences in New York, causing deaths and fear amo

body_en: City has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce threat, and saw 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths this year

F ires from lithium-ion batteries, which power ebikes and scooters, have become regular occurrences in New York , causing deaths and fear among residents, but the city has failed to build infrastructure that could reduce the threat.

New York has seen a dramatic uptick this year in fires from the batteries. In 2025, there were 292 fires, 51 injuries and one death, according to the New York fire department (FDNY). This year, there have already been more than 400 fires, 83 injuries and 12 deaths.

In late October, four members of a family, including an 11-year-old boy, died in a fire caused by a battery in an ebike that was in the pathway to an exit of an 11th floor apartment in a public housing building in the Bronx.

Then recently in a fire at a home in Brooklyn , six people died and nine were injured, including three firefighters and two police officers. Investigators discovered lithium-ion batteries at the scene but have not determined whether they caused the fire, the city council speaker, Julie Menin, said in a statement .
“The presence of lithium-ion batteries at the scene is a serious concern, and more must be done to encourage and mandate safe storage practices. Enough is enough,” Menin stated.
London and Toronto have also recently seen a dramatic increase in lithium-ion battery fires, which are often caused by overcharging and defective or damaged batteries.
Some of that trend is simply because ebikes, often used by food delivery workers and commuters, have become more popular.

But in New York, the city has not executed its plan to build outdoor charging stations which would prevent people from plugging in the batteries in their apartments, where an overheated or defective battery poses a greater risk, experts say.

“There is a ton of red tape around this sort of new technology, and while it’s well intended to not let something new roll out too quickly, I think in this case, it is time to do something quickly,” said Laura Kavanagh, former commissioner of the FDNY.
In 2025, there were 2.2m ebikes imported into the United States, according to Light Electric Vehicle Association , double the number from just three years earlier.

In response to the increased usage and related increase in fires, the New York City department of transportation conducted a 2024 pilot in which it hired companies to offer battery-swapping cabinets where delivery workers could exchange exhausted batteries for charged ones.
The riders did more than 12,000 swaps over six months, and among participants, there was a 35% reduction in charging batteries at home, according to the city.
Following its success, the city announced that it would install 25 charging sites but not until 2027. The city first needed to “gather feedback on site selection, design and implementation”.
In April, New York mayor Zohran Mamdani asked residents to provide feedback on where they would like the 25 cabinets. The city planned to make them available in 2028, the announcement stated.
In 2023, the city also announced that it received a $25m federal grant to build 173 electric-micromobility charging and storage stations at 53 public housing developments.
“This means that residents will no longer need to charge their ebikes in their apartments, what we find to be extremely dangerous,” Mayor Eric Adams said at the time.
At the time, the deputy mayor, Meera Joshi, said residents would start “ seeing evidence ” of the stations in early 2024.
Even though the Biden administration allocated the $25m for the infrastructure, the federal government has not actually provided the funds, according to the New York department of transportation.
body_zh: 该市未能建设可以减少威胁的基础设施，今年发生了 400 起火灾、83 人受伤和 12 人死亡
为电动自行车和踏板车提供动力的锂离子电池起火在纽约已成为常态，导致居民死亡和恐惧，但该市未能建设可以减少威胁的基础设施。
今年，纽约的电池火灾急剧增加。据纽约消防局 (FDNY) 统计，2025 年发生了 292 起火灾，造成 51 人受伤和 1 人死亡。今年，已发生400多起火灾、83人受伤、12人死亡。
10 月下旬，布朗克斯区一栋公共住房大楼 11 楼公寓的出口通道上一辆电动自行车的电池引发火灾，导致一个家庭的四名成员（包括一名 11 岁男孩）死亡。
最近，布鲁克林一所房屋发生火灾，造成六人死亡、九人受伤，其中包括三名消防员和两名警察。市议会发言人朱莉·梅宁(Julie Menin)在一份声明中表示，调查人员在现场发现了锂离子电池，但尚未确定它们是否引起了火灾。
“现场存在锂离子电池是一个严重问题，必须采取更多措施来鼓励和强制执行安全存储做法。够了，”梅宁表示。
伦敦和多伦多最近也出现了锂离子电池火灾的急剧增加，这些火灾通常是由过度充电以及有缺陷或损坏的电池引起的。
这种趋势的部分原因只是因为经常被送餐工人和通勤者使用的电动自行车变得更受欢迎。
但专家表示，在纽约，该市尚未执行建设户外充电站的计划，该计划将阻止人们在公寓里插入电池，因为过热或有缺陷的电池会带来更大的风险。
纽约消防局前局长劳拉·卡瓦纳 (Laura Kavanagh) 表示：“此类新技术存在大量繁文缛节，虽然它的初衷是不让新事物推出得太快，但我认为在这种情况下，是时候迅速采取行动了。”
根据轻型电动汽车协会的数据，到 2025 年，美国将进口 220 万辆电动自行车，这一数字是三年前的两倍。
为了应对使用量的增加和火灾的增加，纽约市交通局在 2024 年进行了一项试点，聘请公司提供电池更换柜，送货员可以将耗尽的电池更换为充满电的电池。
据该市称，乘客在六个月内进行了超过 12,000 次更换，参与者在家中充电的电池数量减少了 35%。
取得成功后，该市宣布将安装 25 个充电站，但要到 2027 年。该市首先需要“收集有关站点选择、设计和实施的反馈”。
4 月，纽约市长佐兰·马姆达尼 (Zohran Mamdani) 要求居民就 25 个橱柜的位置提供反馈。公告称，该市计划于 2028 年投入使用。
2023 年，该市还宣布获得 2500 万美元的联邦拨款，用于在 53 个公共住房开发项目中建设 173 个微型电动汽车充电和存储站。
“这意味着居民将不再需要在公寓里给电动自行车充电，我们发现这是极其危险的，”市长埃里克·亚当斯当时表示。
当时，副市长 Meera Joshi 表示，居民将于 2024 年初开始“看到这些车站的证据”。
据纽约交通部称，尽管拜登政府拨款2500万美元用于基础设施建设，但联邦政府实际上并未提供资金。

summary_zh: 在该党的“下一步是什么”会议上，共识是他们需要迅速采取行动，但负担能力或问责制是问题 D 的下一步是什么
body_en: At party’s ‘What’s Next’ conference, consensus is they need to act quickly, but over affordability or accountability is the question

It’s the question thousands of Democrats, including lawmakers, strategists, pollsters, creators, organizers, staffers and 2028 presidential hopefuls are trying to answer at a three-day gathering in Denver, after a sweeping victory in the 2026 midterm elections.
“We must deliver immediate, bold relief during this affordability crisis,” James Talarico, the senator-elect from Texas, said at the “What’s Next” conference on Thursday.

“Now, we’ll have the collective responsibility to really get to work, fighting for an affordable America, working hard to drive down the high cost of … groceries, high cost of gas, high cost of housing,” Hakeem Jeffries, the congressman of New York, said on Friday.
The consensus is Democrats need to act quickly when they become the majority in January. But the how in that is much more complicated.

There’s a looming question of whether lawmakers should focus more on accountability and pursuing investigations into the administration or focus on moving legislation forward to make life more affordable for Americans.
Rob Sand, the governor-elect of Iowa , told reporters on Thursday he thought the focus should be on delivering tangible economic relief.

“Every time I read, right now, about more investigations of things that have already been reported on in the media, I’m thinking: ‘Why do we need to investigate that? It’s already been reported on.’ Why don’t you do something actually productive or better people’s lives,” Sand said.
Jamie Raskin, the congressman from Maryland who is expected to lead the House judiciary committee, told reporters he believed lawmakers could do both.
Not to mention, there’s a fight brewing over party leadership in the Senate. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is now challenging Chuck Schumer, the party’s longtime leader, as Senate majority leader.
“I’m not voting for senator Schumer,” Elissa Slotkin, a senator for Michigan, told reporters on Friday.

Yet the mood at the Democrats’ de facto victory party – which was planned months in advance by a new group called Majority Democrats – was mostly celebratory. Attendees reveled in the massive wins in longtime Republican strongholds that handed the party sizable majorities in both chambers of Congress and expanded Democrats’ control of governorships and state legislatures across the country.

A six-piece jazz band welcomed attendees to a spacious outdoor plaza on Thursday afternoon. Attendees hugged and congratulated one another. The plaza was packed with smiling Democrats, some wearing “Talarico for Texas” shirts and “Jamie Ager for Congress” pins, others wore “pay your taxes” hats.
Most of the attendees were young. Many of the organizers and strategists are people who joined Democratic groups or campaigns in or after 2016, when Donald Trump was first elected.
Multiple attendees described the event like a class reunion.
The crowd was filled with hugs, laughter and selfies of overjoyed organizers who have spent the last decade working toward a Democratic sweep.

“I think it is important to debrief elections, win or lose. I think we saw the negative ramifications of not properly debriefing an election after 2024,” said Danielle Butterfield, the executive director of Priorities USA, a Democratic-aligned Super Pac.
By 4pm on Friday, alcoholic beverages were flowing and what seemed like an endless stream of happy hours began.
Yet, beneath the excitement appeared to be a fear that Democrats would fail to seize the moment.
body_zh: 在该党的“下一步是什么”会议上，共识是他们需要迅速采取行动，但负担能力或问责制是问题
在 2026 年中期选举取得压倒性胜利后，数千名民主党人，包括立法者、战略家、民调专家、创作者、组织者、工作人员和 2028 年总统候选人，在丹佛举行的为期三天的聚会上试图回答这个问题。
来自德克萨斯州的当选参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科在周四的“下一步是什么”会议上表示：“在这场负担能力危机中，我们必须立即提供大胆的救助。”
纽约州众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯 (Hakeem Jeffries) 周五表示：“现在，我们将承担起真正开始工作的集体责任，为建设一个负担得起的美国而奋斗，努力降低食品杂货、高天然气成本、高住房成本等高成本。”
人们一致认为，民主党在一月份成为多数党后需要迅速采取行动。但其中的方法要复杂得多。
一个迫在眉睫的问题是，立法者是否应该更多地关注问责制和对政府进行调查，还是应该专注于推动立法，让美国人的生活变得更加负担得起。
爱荷华州当选州长罗布·桑德周四对记者表示，他认为重点应该放在提供切实的经济救助上。
“现在，每当我读到对媒体已经报道过的事情进行更多调查时，我都会想：‘为什么我们需要对此进行调查？已经报道过了。’为什么不做一些真正富有成效或改善人们生活的事情呢？”桑德说。
预计将领导众议院司法委员会的马里兰州国会议员杰米·拉斯金 (Jamie Raskin) 告诉记者，他相信立法者可以做到这两点。
更不用说，参议院正在酝酿一场关于政党领导权的斗争。马里兰州的克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 现在正在挑战该党长期领导人查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer)，担任参议院多数党领袖。
“我不会投票给舒默参议员，”密歇根州参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金周五告诉记者。
然而，民主党事实上的胜利派对——这是一个名为“多数民主党”的新团体提前几个月计划的——的气氛大多是庆祝的。与会者对共和党在长期据点取得的巨大胜利感到兴奋，这些胜利使该党在国会参众两院获得了相当大的多数席位，并扩大了民主党对全国州长和州立法机构的控制。
周四下午，六人爵士乐队在宽敞的户外广场欢迎与会者。与会者互相拥抱并祝贺。广场上挤满了微笑的民主党人，一些人穿着“德克萨斯州的塔拉里科”衬衫和“国会的杰米·艾格”徽章，其他人则戴着“纳税”帽子。
大多数与会者都是年轻人。许多组织者和战略家都是在 2016 年唐纳德·特朗普首次当选期间或之后加入民主党团体或竞选活动的人。
多名与会者形容这次活动就像同学聚会。
人群中充满了拥抱、笑声和欣喜若狂的组织者的自拍照，他们在过去的十年里一直致力于民主党的大获全胜。
“我认为，无论输赢，汇报选举情况都很重要。我认为，我们已经看到了 2024 年之后不正确汇报选举的负面影响，”与民主党结盟的超级政治行动委员会 Priorities USA 的执行董事丹妮尔·巴特菲尔德 (Danielle Butterfield) 表示。
周五下午 4 点，酒精饮料源源不断，似乎源源不断的欢乐时光开始了。
然而，在兴奋的背后似乎是对民主党无法抓住时机的担忧。

title_en: SpaceX pulls off first Starship recovery from orbit in spectacular fashion
title_zh: SpaceX 以壮观的方式成功从轨道上回收了第一艘星际飞船
summary: It was the first recovery of a Starship from orbit, a major milestone for a rocket SpaceX founder Elon Musk says will dramatically lower launch costs.
summary_zh: 这是星际飞船首次从轨道上回收，这是火箭的一个重要里程碑，SpaceX 创始人埃隆·马斯克表示，这将大大降低发射成本。
body_en: SpaceX pulls off dramatic midair catch of Starship rocket after fiery plunge from orbit - CBS News

After a 22-hour stay in space, a SpaceX Starship rocket plunged back to Earth Saturday, enduring the blazing heat of reentry while homing in on its Texas Gulf Coast launch site, flipping vertical at the last moment and settling into the grasp of two huge mechanical arms on its launch gantry.

Throngs of SpaceX employees gathered nearby cheered and applauded as the rocket restarted three of its six methane-fueled Raptor engines to flip upright, rapidly slowing to a near hover as the robot arms moved in for a mechanical embrace, catching the rocket a moment before engine shutdown.

"This is so incredible to see!" said SpaceX commentator Jessie Anderson. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes. Congratulations to our teammates at SpaceX, and to everyone who supported the Starship program."

It was the first such recovery of a Starship from orbit — previous test flights ended with planned ocean splashdowns — marking a major milestone in SpaceX's drive to develop the first fully reusable orbit-class rocket, a vehicle company founder Elon Musk says will dramatically lower the cost of launching payloads to Earth orbit, the moon and, eventually, Mars.

The Starship was launched atop a Super Heavy booster Friday using the same pad at SpaceX's Starbase facility on the Texas coast. Standing 407 feet tall, the two-stage rocket is the most powerful launcher ever built, generating some 16 million pounds of thrust at liftoff from 33 first-stage Raptor engines.
After propelling the Starship upper stage out of the lower atmosphere, the Super Heavy first stage attempted its own return to the launch site for capture by the gantry's mechanical arms.

Going into the giant rocket's 15th test flight, SpaceX had successfully recovered the first-stage boosters used in three previous launches. But the Super Heavy launched Friday was diverted to an offshore splashdown because of a guidance problem. The vehicle ran out of fuel and exploded moments before hitting the water.

While a disappointment to the SpaceX team, Musk said in a posting on the social media platform X the problem was a "slight underperformance of engines," adding that "these early ships and boosters are already outdated by improved designs in production or on the test stand."
"This booster loss does not change our timeline to reach high volume, fully reusable Starship flights," he said.

Beaming down crystal-clear views from cameras mounted on its steering fins, the spacecraft's belly, covered in heat-shield tiles, glowed red as the ship heated up in a fireball of atmospheric friction.

Crossing the Baja Peninsula and then northern Mexico, the big rocket rapidly descended before flying just north of the launch site, banking and dropping belly first out of low clouds, restarting its engines to flip upright and then falling at an angle toward the gantry, slowing to a near standstill as the arms closed around it.

"The room behind me going absolutely insane," SpaceX commentator Dan Huot said from the mission control center. "These people have done so much to earn this. ... I mean, that was the missing link. That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes."

But SpaceX will need to successfully launch and recover a large number of Super Heavy-Starships to demonstrate the statistical reliability needed for crewed flights. And the company will need to demonstrate its ability to autonomously refuel Starships in Earth orbit and keep their propellants from boiling away in the space environment.

While the system is designed to be fully reusable, the Starship upper stage uses most of its propellant getting into Earth orbit. NASA wants to use a variant of the Starship to carry astronauts to the lunar surface in 2028 and multiple Super Heavy-tanker flights will be needed to refuel the lander in Earth orbit before it can head for the moon.

SpaceX plans to begin orbital fueling tests in the next several Super Heavy-Starship flights. But the rocket's development has taken longer than initially expected and the space agency is now hedging its bets, saying it's open to using Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 2 lander depending on which spacecraft is ready in time.

body_zh: SpaceX 在从轨道猛烈坠落后完成了 Starship 火箭的戏剧性空中捕获 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
在太空停留 22 小时后，SpaceX 的一艘星舰火箭于周六坠入地球，在返回德克萨斯州墨西哥湾沿岸发射场的同时，忍受着再入的酷热，在最后一刻垂直翻转，落入发射架上两个巨大机械臂的手中。
当火箭重新启动六台以甲烷为燃料的猛禽发动机中的三台并直立翻转时，聚集在附近的 SpaceX 员工欢呼雀跃，并迅速减速至接近悬停状态，而机械臂则移动到机械臂上，在发动机关闭前一刻抓住了火箭。
“这真是令人难以置信！” SpaceX 评论员 Jessie Anderson 说道。 “有史以来最令人难以置信、最具历史意义的工程壮举之一就在我们眼前发生了。祝贺我们在 SpaceX 的队友，以及所有支持星舰计划的人。”
这是星际飞船首次从轨道上回收——之前的试飞都以计划中的海洋溅落而告终——标志着 SpaceX 开发第一枚完全可重复使用的轨道级火箭的一个重要里程碑，该公司创始人埃隆·马斯克表示，这将大大降低向地球轨道、月球乃至火星发射有效载荷的成本。
周五，星舰在超重型助推器顶部发射，使用的是位于德克萨斯州海岸的 SpaceX Starbase 设施中的同一发射台。两级火箭高 407 英尺，是有史以来最强大的发射器，在升空时由 33 个第一级猛禽发动机产生约 1600 万磅的推力。
将星舰上级推出低层大气后，超重型第一级尝试自行返回发射场，以便被龙门架的机械臂捕获。
在进入这艘巨型火箭的第 15 次试飞时，SpaceX 已成功回收了之前三次发射中使用的第一级助推器。但由于导航问题，周五发射的“超重型”号被转移到海上溅落。车辆耗尽燃料并在落入水面前爆炸。
虽然令 SpaceX 团队感到失望，但马斯克在社交媒体平台 X 上发帖表示，问题是“发动机性能略有下降”，并补充说“这些早期的飞船和助推器已经过时了，因为生产或测试台上的设计改进了。”
他说：“助推器的损失不会改变我们实现大容量、完全可重复使用的星舰飞行的时间表。”
从安装在其转向鳍上的摄像机拍摄出水晶般清晰的图像，飞船的腹部覆盖着隔热瓦，当飞船在大气摩擦的火球中升温时，它发出红光。
穿过巴哈半岛，然后是墨西哥北部，这枚大型火箭迅速下降，然后飞到发射场以北，先从低云层中倾斜并下降，重新启动发动机，使其垂直翻转，然后以一定角度落向龙门架，当手臂将其包围时，它的速度减慢至近乎静止。
“我身后的房间简直太疯狂了，”SpaceX 评论员 Dan Huot 在任务控制中心说道。 “这些人为了获得这个而做了很多事情……我的意思是，这就是缺失的一环。那是太空飞行的圣杯，从火中坠落，然后被钢铁从空中夺走。我们抓住了一艘星舰，现在一切都改变了。”
但 SpaceX 需要成功发射和回收大量超重型星舰，以证明载人飞行所需的统计可靠性。该公司还需要展示其在地球轨道上为星际飞船自动加油并防止其推进剂在太空环境中沸腾的能力。
虽然该系统被设计为完全可重复使用，但星舰上级使用其大部分推进剂进入地球轨道。 NASA 希望在 2028 年使用星际飞船的变体将宇航员运送到月球表面，并且需要多次超重型加油机飞行来为着陆器在地球轨道上加油，然后才能前往月球。
SpaceX 计划在接下来的几次超重型星舰飞行中开始轨道加油测试。但火箭的开发时间比最初预期的要长，航天局现在正在两面下注，表示它对使用蓝色起源的蓝月马克 2 号着陆器持开放态度，具体取决于哪个航天器及时准备好。

title_en: Passengers rescued after tanker hit river cruise in New Orleans
title_zh: 油轮在新奥尔良游轮撞上乘客后获救
summary: A tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans Friday, partially submerging the passenger boat.
summary_zh: 星期五，一艘油轮在新奥尔良港附近的密西西比河上撞上了一艘内河游轮，部分客船被淹没。
body_en: A major rescue operation took place Friday after a tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans, leaving the American Heritage passenger boat on its side and largely submerged in the water.
Everyone aboard both vessels has been accounted for, officials said, and there were no fatalities reported.

The much larger tanker, identified as the Atlantic Asphalt, crashed into the paddlewheel cruise boat while it was docked at about 12:30 p.m. local time, the Port of New Orleans said. The American Heritage had docked about two hours earlier for passengers to disembark.

New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno said in a news briefing late Friday afternoon that 32 passengers from the cruise ship were taken to area hospitals for treatment, but none with critical injuries. No one aboard the tanker was hurt, Moreno said. New Orleans Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said two of her officers were also hospitalized during the rescue operation, but were in good condition.
Eight people remained hospitalized Saturday afternoon, with two in serious condition, Moreno said at a news conference.
There were 191 passengers and crew members aboard the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the mayor.

Moreno said the tanker "lost control" and crashed into the cruise ship. As passengers were disembarking from the cruise ship, it "began to sink, and then eventually toppled over and flipped," sending people into the water, the mayor said.

Some people were seen in the water in life jackets or standing near the railing as the other side of the ship listed farther into the water. Moreno said at a news conference Saturday that rescuers pulled approximately 100 people from the water. Nearby boats had reported rescuing more than a dozen people from the water.

Emergency responders, including Port NOLA Harbor Police, the New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department and the U.S. Coast Guard, conducted rescue and response operations, Port NOLA said. Moreno said that along with local and federal agencies, private vessels that happened to be on the river at the time responded "as volunteers to try and get people out of the water."
Moreno described the successful rescue operation as a "miracle on the Mississippi."

One witness, Jamie Holford, told CBS News he saw the American Heritage hit the dock after the collision. He described seeing people hurrying off the boat. Then, as it rolled over, some were climbing over the railings of the boat, he said.
"It looked like something off the Titanic," he said.
Asked what the collision sounded like, Holford said, "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like."
U.S. Coast Guard Capt. Melanie Burnham said Coast Guard investigators were on scene working to determine what caused the tanker to lose control.
"The investigation is still ongoing, there seems to be some kind of a loss of steering," Burnham told reporters. "The exact reason why, we don't know that."

The National Transportation Safety Board sent a "Go Team" to the scene Saturday to begin its own investigation into the cause. The agency said at a news conference that investigators have recovered a Voyage Data Recorder (VDR) from the Atlantic Asphalt and asked the public for video and information. A VDR captures the vessel's speed through the water, direction, course and audio from the bridge of the vessel, according to the NTSB.

Burnham said at a news conference Saturday that approximately 16,000 gallons of fuel remain on board and that officials are assessing how to address the potential pollution. She told reporters it is too early to give a timeline on salvaging the wreckage, saying, "We're talking weeks."
Burnham noted Friday that she was working to reopen the river, which the Coast Guard had closed when the collision occurred.
"We're going to start evaluating how to reopen it as soon as possible," Burnham said.

In a Truth Social post , President Trump praised the response of the Coast Guard and other law enforcement agencies for "doing such an incredible job of rescue, and other work, having to do with the crash of the two ships in Louisiana."
body_zh: 周五，一艘油轮在新奥尔良港附近的密西西比河上撞上了一艘内河游轮，导致美国传统客船侧翻并大部分淹没在水中，随后进行了一次重大救援行动。
官员称，两艘船上的所有人都已经被查清，目前还没有人员死亡的报道。
这艘更大的油轮被确认为“大西洋沥青”号，于中午 12 点 30 分左右撞上了明轮游船。当地时间，新奥尔良港表示。美国遗产号大约提前两个小时停靠，供乘​​客下船。
新奥尔良市市长海伦娜·莫雷诺在周五下午的新闻发布会上表示，游轮上的 32 名乘客被送往当地医院接受治疗，但没有人伤势严重。莫雷诺说，油轮上没有人受伤。新奥尔良港警察局长梅兰妮·蒙特罗尔表示，她的两名警察在救援行动中也住院，但情况良好。
莫雷诺在新闻发布会上说，周六下午有八人仍在医院治疗，其中两人伤势严重。
据市长称，事故发生时，American Heritage 号上有 191 名乘客和机组人员。
莫雷诺表示，油轮“失去控制”并撞上了游轮。市长说，当乘客从游轮上下来时，游轮“开始下沉，然后最终翻倒并翻转”，导致人们落入水中。
有人看到一些人穿着救生衣在水中，或者站在栏杆附近，而船的另一侧则进一步沉入水中。据报道，附近的船只从水中救出了十几人。
诺拉港表示，包括诺拉港警察局、新奥尔良消防局、新奥尔良警察局和美国海岸警卫队在内的应急人员进行了救援和响应行动。莫雷诺表示，当时恰好在河上的私人船只与当地和联邦机构一起做出了反应，“作为志愿者，试图将人们从水中救出来”。
莫雷诺将这次成功的救援行动描述为“密西西比河上的奇迹”。
一位目击者杰米·霍尔福德告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，他看到美国遗产号在碰撞后撞上了码头。他描述看到人们匆匆下船。他说，然后，当船翻倒时，一些人爬上了船的栏杆。
“它看起来就像泰坦尼克号上的东西，”他说。
当被问及碰撞的声音时，霍尔福德说：“听起来就像一部战争电影。想象一下成吨的钢铁嘎吱作响。这就是它的声音。”
美国海岸警卫队上尉梅兰妮·伯纳姆表示，海岸警卫队调查人员正在现场调查导致油轮失控的原因。
伯纳姆告诉记者：“调查仍在进行中，似乎存在某种转向缺失。” “具体原因，我们不知道。”
美国国家运输安全委员会周六派出一个“行动小组”前往现场，开始调查事故原因。该机构在新闻发布会上表示，调查人员已从大西洋沥青公司找到了航行数据记录仪（VDR），并要求公众提供视频和信息。据 NTSB 称，VDR 可以捕获船舶在水中的速度、方向、航向以及船桥上的音频。
伯纳姆在周六的新闻发布会上表示，船上仍有大约 16,000 加仑的燃料，官员们正在评估如何解决潜在的污染问题。她告诉记者，现在给出打捞残骸的时间表还为时过早，“我们正在讨论几周的时间。”
伯纳姆周五指出，她正在努力重新开放这条河流，碰撞发生时海岸警卫队已关闭这条河流。
伯纳姆说：“我们将开始评估如何尽快重新开放。”
在《真相社会》的一篇帖子中，特朗普总统赞扬海岸警卫队和其他执法机构的反应，“在路易斯安那州两艘船失事的相关救援和其他工作中做了如此令人难以置信的工作”。

title_en: As Democrats win big, thirst traps of male candidates take social media by storm
title_zh: 随着民主党大获全胜，男性候选人的口渴陷阱席卷社交媒体
summary: It's everywhere on social media: Democrats celebrating the attractive men voters elected in the midterms. But it's bigger than a meme and says a lot about politics of masculinity in the age of Trump.
summary_zh: 社交媒体上随处可见：民主党人庆祝中期选举中选出的有魅力的男性选民。但它比模因更大并且说了很多
body_en: Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-GA) walks on stage to speak during a midterm election rally at the Cobb County Convention Center in Atlanta, on Oct. 17, 2026. Erik S. Lesser/AFP via Getty Images hide caption
If you're on social media, there's a good chance you've seen the videos: people getting hot and bothered about the young men Democrats just elected.

"I'm looking at you, Rob Sand. I'm looking at you, Jon Ossoff. I'm looking at you, El-Sayed," said fitness coach Jesse Barton, reacting to the midterm results . "I am looking, I am not the only one, and I'm very happy about what I see."
There are debates over candidates' relative levels of hotness. There are a lot of AI-generated images. And there are many, many montages of the politicians set to sexy pop music.
One of the most viral pieces of content was a parody Tiger Beat magazine cover featuring Democratic men … which Manoushka Guerrier, an LA-based chef and content-creator, took one step further.

"I created the entire Tiger Beat style personality quiz , complete with the different boy band personas," she said. The quiz gives people matches including "the Babyface" (Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico) and "the Heartthrob" (Colorado Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel).
Guerrier pays a lot of attention to politics, and she emphasizes that these guys' looks are just a bonus.
"They're young and they're ballsy and they're smart, and they're not just smart; they're brilliant," she says.

The tidal wave of attention on these young men creates a striking contrast to the first Trump midterm, in 2018. That election — after the Women's March, Me Too and the long list of assault and misconduct allegations against President Trump — yielded a record-setting wave of Democratic women . It all suggests that the thirsty social media posts aren't just a cheeky trend; they also say a lot about how Democrats have responded to the Trump era.
Two main forces are behind the wave of attention on these men according to Christina Wolbrecht, a political science professor at Notre Dame University.
"I think it's a function of our kind of society-wide debate about masculinity," she said. "And I also think it's about age."

The age side is straightforward — just ahead of the midterms , a majority of likely voters said they favored candidates with new ideas over those with experience in the job, according to a NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll.
The masculinity side, meanwhile, is in response to MAGA and its elevation of a very specific type of manhood, Wolbrecht said.
"For 10-plus years, Donald Trump has presented one very distinct version of masculinity," she said. "It's very much power over [others]. It's very much power through wealth and status."

Manliness took center stage on the Democratic side this election. Candidates leaned into it, with people like Rutinel and Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El Sayed posting weightlifting videos. El Sayed at one point did a video spoofing Love Island.

Voters noticed, posting admiring videos well before the election. Meanwhile, the media noticed and amplified this narrative, with profiles and think pieces throughout the midterm cycle, and reporting on Democrats' " rugged " and " authentic " candidates.

Amplifying young, "manly" men may have boosted the party in this election. That's because Democrats had a problem after Kamala Harris lost the presidency in 2024, according to Democratic strategist Monica Venske.

"The feeling within the straight male demographic, if you will, [was] that it just wasn't cool to be a Democrat," she said. "It wasn't sexy to be a Democrat. It's not manly to be a Democrat. That's a girly thing to be, is a Democrat."
That's why she started the Instagram account Boyfriends We Deserve, where she highlights attractive Democrats — mostly men, but a few women as well.
body_zh: 2026 年 10 月 17 日，佐治亚州民主党参议员乔恩·奥索夫 (Jon Ossoff) 在亚特兰大科布县会议中心举行的中期选举集会上走上讲台发表讲话。埃里克·S·莱瑟 (Erik S. Lesser)/法新社盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
如果您在社交媒体上，您很有可能看过这些视频：人们对刚刚当选的民主党年轻人感到愤怒和担忧。
“我在看着你，罗布·桑德。我在看着你，乔恩·奥索夫。我在看着你，埃尔-赛义德，”体能教练杰西·巴顿在谈到中期成绩时说道。 “我正在寻找，我不是唯一的一个，我对我所看到的感到非常高兴。”
关于候选人的相对热度程度存在争议。有很多人工智能生成的图像。还有很多很多政客的蒙太奇，背景是性感的流行音乐。
最具病毒性的内容之一是模仿《Tiger Beat》杂志封面，主角是民主党人……洛杉矶厨师兼内容创作者 Manoushka Guerrier 更进一步。
“我创建了整个 Tiger Beat 风格的个性测验，包括不同的男孩乐队角色，”她说。测验为人们提供了包括“娃娃脸”（德克萨斯州当选参议员詹姆斯·塔拉里科）和“万人迷”（科罗拉多州当选众议员曼尼·鲁蒂内尔）在内的比赛。
盖里尔非常关注政治，她强调这些人的外表只是一个额外的好处。
“他们年轻、勇敢、聪明，他们不仅聪明，而且才华横溢，”她说。
对这些年轻人的关注浪潮与 2018 年特朗普的第一次中期选举形成鲜明对比。那次选举——在妇女大游行、“我也是”以及针对特朗普总统的一长串攻击和不当行为指控之后——产生了创纪录的民主党女性浪潮。这一切都表明，社交媒体上的饥渴帖子不仅仅是一种厚颜无耻的趋势，而是一种厚颜无耻的趋势。他们还谈到了民主党如何应对特朗普时代的很多内容。
圣母大学政治学教授克里斯蒂娜·沃尔布雷希特表示，对这些人的关注背后有两个主要力量。
“我认为这是我们全社会关于男子气概的辩论的一个功能，”她说。 “而且我也认为这与年龄有关。”
年龄方面很简单——根据 NPR/PBS 新闻/Marist 民意调查，就在中期选举之前，大多数可能的选民表示，他们更喜欢有新想法的候选人，而不是那些有工作经验的候选人。
沃尔布雷希特说，与此同时，男子气概的一面是对 MAGA 及其对一种非常特殊的男子气概的提升的回应。
“十多年来，唐纳德·特朗普展现了一种非常独特的男性气质，”她说。 “这是对[他人]的巨大权力。这是通过财富和地位获得的巨大权力。”
这次选举中，男子气概成为了民主党的焦点。候选人们纷纷加入其中，鲁蒂内尔和密歇根州当选参议员阿卜杜勒·埃尔·赛义德等人都发布了举重视频。艾尔·赛义德曾制作过一段恶搞爱情岛的视频。
选民们注意到了这一点，并在选举前发布了钦佩的视频。与此同时，媒体注意到并放大了这一叙述，在整个中期周期中进行了简介和思考，并报道了民主党“粗犷”和“真实”的候选人。
扩大年轻、“有男子气概”的男性可能在这次选举中推动了该党的发展。民主党策略师莫妮卡·文斯克 (Monica Venske) 表示，这是因为卡马拉·哈里斯 (Kamala Harris) 在 2024 年失去总统职位后民主党遇到了问题。
“如果你愿意的话，异性恋男性群体的感觉是，成为一名民主党人并不酷，”她说。 “作为一名民主党人并不性感。作为一名民主党人并不男子气概。这是一个女孩子气的事情，是一名民主党人。”
这就是她创建 Instagram 账户“Boyfriends We Deserve”的原因，她在该账户中重点关注有吸引力的民主党人——大多数是男性，但也有少数女性。

title_en: US has lost measles elimination status, global health authorities say
title_zh: 全球卫生当局称美国已失去消除麻疹的地位
summary: The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, according to researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations at the Pan American Health Organization.
summary_zh: 直接了解泛泛会议审议情况的研究人员表示，美国已经失去了消灭麻疹国家的地位。
body_en: Anna Fajardo, a public health nurse, offers vaccines at a school registration event in southwestern Utah. Amy Maxmen/KFF Health News
The U.S. has lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a public health triumph secured a quarter century ago.

Researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations on the country's status told KFF Health News that the Pan American Health Organization reached the conclusion this week: Measles has reestablished regular transmission in the country.
PAHO had planned a public announcement on Nov. 17.
In public health parlance, measles elimination depends on a country's sporadic outbreaks ending within a year. That's no longer happening in the United States.
"It's a very sad moment," said Anne Schuchat, an epidemiologist and a former deputy director at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention who was not involved in PAHO's decision.

"Measles causes so much unnecessary suffering, everything from a high fever and missed work and school to long-term complications like progressive degenerative nerve disease and death," Schuchat said.

Measles outbreaks are entirely preventable: Two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine prevent about 97% of infections, so when almost everyone in a community is fully vaccinated, the virus can't spread.

In the past two years, over 830 people have been hospitalized with measles in the U.S. More than 8,000 people have been sickened in outbreaks that have cost roughly $125 million in medical care, public health response, and productivity losses, Johns Hopkins University researchers estimate .

States have reported 13 measles-associated deaths, including a 7-month-old in New York and infants in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin in recent months. Babies typically aren't vaccinated before they're a year old.

PAHO, an international group that oversees health in the Americas and works with the World Health Organization, based its assessment on two analyses: one by the CDC and another by an independent group of measles experts.
Researchers anticipated this conclusion after an outbreak in Utah surpassed the one-year mark in June.

A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, Emily Hilliard, attributed the resurgence of measles to vaccination gaps that opened years before this administration. Indeed, rates of childhood vaccination have steadily declined since the COVID pandemic started.
But many scientists also blame the Trump administration for spreading vaccine misinformation and stifling a swift, strong response to outbreaks.
For example, the administration cut millions of dollars from children's immunization programs run by state health departments and terminated funds for research on vaccine hesitancy.

After Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. sacked CDC director Susan Monarez in August 2025, she told Congress she was fired because she would not preapprove changes to vaccine recommendations "without reviewing the evidence."
Monarez added that "we already have seen the largest measles outbreak in more than 30 years" and that, "if vaccine protections are weakened, preventable diseases will return."

Spokespeople for HHS and the White House defended the administration, and Kennedy, who led a prominent anti-vaccine organization before he took the helm at HHS. "The President and the Secretary have repeatedly encouraged measles vaccination, coordinated with states, and facilitated the deployment of vaccine doses across the country," White House spokesperson Allison Schuster wrote in an email.

For more than three decades, the federal government treated measles as a preventable tragedy, with sizable outbreaks triggering national efforts to boost vaccination and stop the virus from spreading.
body_zh: 公共卫生护士安娜·法哈多 (Anna Fajardo) 在犹他州西南部的一次学校注册活动中提供疫苗。艾米·麦克斯曼/KFF 健康新闻
美国已经失去了消灭麻疹国家的地位，这是二十五年前取得的公共卫生胜利。
直接了解该国状况审议情况的研究人员告诉 KFF 健康新闻，泛美卫生组织本周得出结论：麻疹已在该国重新建立正常传播。
泛美卫生组织原计划于 11 月 17 日发布公告。
用公共卫生术语来说，麻疹的消除取决于一个国家的零星疫情在一年内结束。这种情况在美国已不再发生。
“这是一个非常悲伤的时刻，”流行病学家、美国疾病控制与预防中心前副主任安妮·舒查特（Anne Schuchat）说，她没有参与泛美卫生组织的决定。
舒查特说：“麻疹会造成很多不必要的痛苦，从高烧、缺勤、缺课到进行性退行性神经疾病和死亡等长期并发症。”
麻疹爆发是完全可以预防的：两剂麻疹-腮腺炎-风疹疫苗可预防约 97% 的感染，因此，当社区中几乎每个人都完全接种疫苗时，病毒就无法传播。
过去两年，美国有超过 830 人因麻疹入院治疗。据约翰·霍普金斯大学研究人员估计，麻疹疫情导致 8,000 多人患病，造成医疗保健、公共卫生应对和生产力损失约 1.25 亿美元。
近几个月来，各州报告了 13 例与麻疹相关的死亡，其中包括纽约州的一名 7 个月大的婴儿以及宾夕法尼亚州和威斯康星州的婴儿。婴儿通常在一岁之前不会接种疫苗。
泛美卫生组织是一个负责监督美洲健康并与世界卫生组织合作的国际组织，其评估基于两项分析：一项由疾病预防控制中心进行，另一项由麻疹专家独立小组进行。
六月份犹他州疫情爆发超过一年大关后，研究人员预计了这一结论。
美国卫生与公众服务部发言人艾米丽·希利亚德 (Emily Hilliard) 将麻疹的死灰复燃归因于本届政府之前几年就出现的疫苗接种缺口。事实上，自新冠病毒大流行开始以来，儿童疫苗接种率一直在稳步下降。
但许多科学家也指责特朗普政府传播疫苗错误信息并扼杀对疫情的迅速、强有​​力的反应。
例如，政府从州卫生部门运营的儿童免疫项目中削减了数百万美元，并终止了疫苗犹豫研究的资金。
2025 年 8 月，卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.) 解雇了疾病预防控制中心 (CDC) 主任苏珊·莫纳雷斯 (Susan Monarez)，她告诉国会，她被解雇是因为她不会“在不审查证据的情况下”预先批准对疫苗建议的修改。
莫纳雷斯补充说，“我们已经看到了三十多年来最大规模的麻疹疫情”，并且“如果疫苗保护作用减弱，可预防的疾病将会卷土重来。”
卫生与公众服务部和白宫的发言人为政府和肯尼迪辩护，肯尼迪在掌管卫生与公众服务部之前领导了一个著名的反疫苗组织。白宫发言人艾莉森·舒斯特在一封电子邮件中写道：“总统和国务卿一再鼓励麻疹疫苗接种，与各州协调，并促进在全国范围内部署疫苗剂量。”
三十多年来，联邦政府一直将麻疹视为一场可以预防的悲剧，大规模的疫情爆发引发了全国范围内加强疫苗接种并阻止病毒传播的努力。

title_en: Travelers stranded, flights canceled after ground stop. Here's what we know
title_zh: 旅客滞留，航班在地面停留后取消。这是我们所知道的
summary: Officials attributed the ground stop to aging system infrastructure and legacy technology.
summary_zh: 官员们将停顿归因于老化的系统基础设施和遗留技术。
body_en: Travelers stranded and thousands of flights canceled after FAA ground stop. Here's what we know - CBS News
Airspace across the United States slowly began returning to normal on Saturday after a rare national ground stop canceled thousands of flights and stranded travelers.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a news conference Saturday, "We are back at full operations."
He thanked the pilots, airline staff, air traffic controllers and the FAA for their professionalism during the ground stop.
"They safely landed all of our aircraft," he said, also thanking the passengers for their patience during the significant disruption.
"Planes are pushing back, taxiing, and taking off, and it is safe to fly," Duffy said earlier in a social media post on Saturday.
"You will continue to see some delays and cancellations as carriers reschedule flights and reposition aircraft/crews where they are needed most."
More than 5,000 flights were canceled Saturday, according to flight tracking website FlightAware , while around 5,300 others were delayed.
The ground stop began at 3:36 p.m. EST Friday when the FAA ordered the stoppage while approximately 3,500 flights were in the air.
"The FAA issued a ground stop out of an abundance of caution while 3,500+ planes were in the air," Duffy said . All airborne planes were able to land safely.
This marked the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023, when a key FAA computer system malfunctioned. Before that, the last national ground stop occurred after the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks.
Around 9,159 flights were canceled on Friday and 7,190 were delayed, according to FlightAware, stranding passengers at major airports across the country.
Officials attributed the ground stop to aging system infrastructure and legacy technology.
"What we have is an incredibly old air traffic control system," Duffy said.

Duffy said Saturday that a preliminary investigation found that an L3Harris contractor was working in a remote FAA location and switching old copper wire to fiber while replacing a router. The router that was being switched then started flooding other routers, overloading the system. There were 1,000 attempts to log on every four to five seconds, he said.

The transportation secretary said the FAA is working to determine if the issue was human error or if a faulty router was installed. Duffy said that many contractors "take our money and provide really poor service." He also said that L3Harris, a technology and defense company, owned the system.
L3Harris said Saturday the company has been modernizing the communications infrastructure supporting the National Airspace System in close coordination with the FAA.

"We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation's air travel," the company said in a statement, adding they take the nationwide ground stop and "its impact" seriously.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said updating the wires was a routine maintenance issue that the agency had been working on for years. About 70% of the system has been transferred from copper wires to fiber. After the router began flooding the system for 45 minutes, the FAA could not determine the cause of the instability. The instability then spread to 17 facilities, he said.
"Out of an abundance of caution," the FAA decided to issue a ground stop, Bedford said. He said he stands behind that call.
body_zh: 美国联邦航空局地面停留后，旅客滞留，数千航班取消。这是我们所知道的 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
周六，在一次罕见的全国性地面停留取消了数千个航班并导致旅客滞留后，美国各地的空域开始慢慢恢复正常。
交通部长肖恩·达菲在周六的新闻发布会上表示，“我们已恢复全面运营。”
他感谢飞行员、航空公司工作人员、空中交通管制员和美国联邦航空局在地面停留期间的专业精神。
他说：“他们安全降落了我们所有的飞机。”他还感谢乘客在重大干扰期间的耐心等待。
达菲周六早些时候在社交媒体上发帖称：“飞机正在向后推、滑行、起飞，飞行是安全的。”
“随着航空公司重新安排航班并将飞机/机组人员重新部署到最需要的地方，您将继续看到一些延误和取消。”
根据航班跟踪网站 FlightAware 的数据，周六有 5,000 多个航班被取消，另外约 5,300 个航班被延误。
地面停车于下午 3 点 36 分开始。美国东部时间周五，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 下令停飞，当时大约有 3,500 架航班正在空中飞行。
达菲说：“当 3,500 多架飞机在空中飞行时，美国联邦航空局出于高度谨慎而发布了地面停止令。”所有空中飞机均能够安全着陆。
这是自 2023 年 1 月 FAA 关键计算机系统发生故障以来的首次全国性地面停留。在此之前，最后一次全国地面停留发生在 2001 年 9 月 11 日的袭击事件之后。
据 FlightAware 称，周五约有 9,159 架航班被取消，7,190 架航班延误，导致全国主要机场的乘客滞留。
官员们将停顿归因于老化的系统基础设施和遗留技术。
“我们拥有的是一个非常古老的空中交通管制系统，”达菲说。
达菲周六表示，初步调查发现，一名 L3Harris 承包商正在 FAA 的一个偏远地点工作，在更换路由器时将旧铜线更换为光纤。然后，正在切换的路由器开始淹没其他路由器，导致系统超载。他说，每四到五秒就有 1,000 次尝试登录。
交通部长表示，美国联邦航空局正在努力确定问题是否是人为错误，或者是否安装了有故障的路由器。达菲说，许多承包商“拿了我们的钱，却提供了非常差的服务”。他还表示，L3Harris 是一家技术和国防公司，拥有该系统。
L3Harris 周六表示，该公司一直在与 FAA 密切合作，对支持国家空域系统的通信基础设施进行现代化改造。
该公司在一份声明中表示：“我们正在支持美国联邦航空局的调查，以了解导致我国航空旅行于 11 月 13 日发生地面停止的情况。”并补充说，他们严肃对待全国范围内的地面停止及其“影响”。
美国联邦航空管理局局长布莱恩·贝德福德表示，更新电线是该机构多年来一直致力于解决的一个例行维护问题。大约70%的系统已经从铜线转移到光纤。路由器开始对系统造成 45 分钟的淹没后，FAA 无法确定不稳定的原因。他说，不稳定局势随后蔓延到 17 个设施。
贝德福德说，“出于谨慎考虑”，美国联邦航空局决定发布地面停止令。他说他支持这一呼吁。

title_en: U.S. facilitating direct engagement between Europe and Russia
title_zh: 美国促进欧洲和俄罗斯之间的直接接触
summary: President Trump's senior envoy and son-in-law, Jared Kushner, said they are also preparing for the next round of trilateral talks.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统的高级特使兼女婿贾里德·库什纳表示，他们也在为下一轮三边会谈做准备。
body_en: The United States is facilitating direct engagement between Russia and Europe amid a push to secure a peace deal in the war in Ukraine , President Trump's special envoy and son-in-law, Jared Kushner, said on Saturday.

Kushner and Steve Witkoff held separate meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy this past week as the Trump administration pushes to end the more than 4 ½-year conflict. The meetings came after the first round of U.S.-brokered talks between the two countries since February concluded on Wednesday with an announcement of plans for a new prisoner exchange and further talks, but nothing to suggest a wider peace deal.

"Our focus is now on facilitating direct engagement between Moscow and European partners and preparing the agenda for the next round of trilateral talks," Kushner said in a social media post on Saturday. "Several new ideas emerged from these discussions and are now being explored. Some may lead to breakthroughs directly, while others may evolve into new proposals that help bridge the remaining gaps."

Zelenskyy, in statements released Saturday, said the U.S. had raised the possibility of a new security framework for Europe, though he warned that Moscow could use such discussions to weaken NATO and reshape the continent's borders.
"In my view, this can be dangerous," Zelenskyy told reporters Friday, referring to the new security framework. "This should not be the main agenda." His comments were embargoed until Saturday.

Zelenskyy said the U.S. had asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas region in eastern Ukraine that Russia does not control if Kyiv were admitted to NATO. He reiterated that Kyiv would not surrender its territory.
He also said he believed Moscow was interested in reopening broader questions about European security rather than focusing exclusively on ending the war.

"Putin's desire to change borders in Europe is a fact. I am sure this is part of his concept of revising security guarantees in Europe," he said. "This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations."

European leaders have stressed that decisions about the continent's security must be made by Europeans themselves, warning against allowing Russia to dictate the terms of a new security order or negotiate NATO's future.

Ukraine is discussing a comprehensive security package with its partners that could include specific guarantees from NATO and the European Union, a strong Ukrainian military and financial support for a specified period, he said. It would also include a recovery plan, he said.
"If the American side confirms precisely this to us, together with other NATO partners, then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: Do we accept it or not?" Zelenskyy said.
He stressed that any arrangement would not involve recognizing occupied territories as Russian.
Zelenskyy also rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality, saying that would require changing the country's constitution.
"If Putin expects Ukraine's neutrality to be enshrined, that's not going to happen," he said. "We're not in NATO right now anyway."
Kushner said Saturday that a lasting peace in Ukraine requires security guarantees for Kyiv and "detailed, actionable postwar security arrangements that reduce the risk of another war."

"NATO will remain a critical pillar of European security, enhanced by stronger mechanisms for military, communication, deconfliction, and reciprocal de-escalation, with practical ways to address disputes before they become crises," he added. "This is why we are working to bring our European partners directly into these discussions. Any final agreement must be agreed to by the relevant parties, and President Trump will only support arrangements that strengthen Ukraine's and Europe's security and make future conflict less likely."
Zelenskyy warned that broader discussions about Europe's security could allow Putin to seek changes to NATO's military presence, including the withdrawal of American troops.
He said Putin had raised similar ideas with then-President Joe Biden in 2021, seeking a redistribution of power in Europe and the world.
"I think Putin will bring up Finland and Sweden. I'm sure he will raise the issue of Hungary and the presence of American troops in the Baltic countries," Zelenskyy said.
He said any changes to Europe's security arrangements must be decided by European NATO members only after the war ends.
body_zh: 特朗普总统的特使兼女婿贾里德·库什纳周六表示，美国正在促进俄罗斯与欧洲之间的直接接触，以推动在乌克兰战争中达成和平协议。
上周，库什纳和史蒂夫·威特科夫分别与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和乌克兰总统弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基举行了会晤，特朗普政府正在推动结束这场长达 4.5 年多的冲突。这些会议是在美国斡旋的两国自二月份以来的第一轮会谈于周三结束后举行的，会谈宣布了新的囚犯交换和进一步会谈的计划，但没有暗示达成更广泛的和平协议。
库什纳在周六的社交媒体帖子中表示：“我们现在的重点是促进莫斯科与欧洲伙伴之间的直接接触，并为下一轮三边会谈准备议程。” “这些讨论中出现了一些新想法，目前正在探索中。有些可能会直接带来突破，而另一些可能会演变成新的提案，帮助弥合剩余的差距。”
泽连斯基在周六发表的声明中表示，美国提出了为欧洲建立新安全框架的可能性，不过他警告称，莫斯科可能会利用此类讨论来削弱北约并重塑欧洲大陆的边界。
“在我看来，这可能很危险，”泽伦斯基周五对记者说，他指的是新的安全框架。 “这不应该是主要议程。”他的言论直到周六才发表。
泽伦斯基表示，美国首次询问乌克兰是否会从乌克兰东部顿巴斯地区部分地区撤军，如果基辅加入北约，俄罗斯无法控制这些地区。他重申基辅不会放弃其领土。
他还表示，他相信莫斯科有兴趣重新讨论有关欧洲安全的更广泛问题，而不是仅仅专注于结束战争。
“普京希望改变欧洲边界是事实。我确信这是他修改欧洲安全保障概念的一部分，”他说。 “这很危险，因为在我看来，正是这样的事情导致了战争或升级。”
欧洲领导人强调，有关欧洲大陆安全的决定必须由欧洲人自己做出，并警告不要允许俄罗斯决定新安全秩序的条款或谈判北约的未来。
他说，乌克兰正在与合作伙伴讨论全面的安全一揽子计划，其中可能包括北约和欧盟的具体保证，以及乌克兰在特定时期内的强大军事和财政支持。他说，其中还包括一项恢复计划。
“如果美国方面和其他北约伙伴向我们证实了这一点，那么我将问问我们乌克兰社会的想法：我们接受还是不接受？”泽连斯基说道。
他强调，任何安排都不会涉及承认被占领土为俄罗斯领土。
泽伦斯基还拒绝了乌克兰承诺中立的可能性，称这需要修改该国宪法。
他说：“如果普京希望乌克兰保持中立，那这种情况就不会发生。” “无论如何，我们现在不在北约。”
库什纳周六表示，乌克兰的持久和平需要基辅的安全保障和“详细、可操作的战后安全安排，以减少另一场战争的风险”。
他补充说：“北约仍将是欧洲安全的重要支柱，并通过更强大的军事、沟通、冲突消除和相互缓和升级机制以及在争端演变为危机之前解决争端的切实可行的机制来加强。” “这就是为什么我们正在努力让我们的欧洲伙伴直接参与这些讨论。任何最终协议都必须得到有关各方的同意，特朗普总统只会支持加强乌克兰和欧洲安全并减少未来冲突可能性的安排。”
泽伦斯基警告说，有关欧洲安全的更广泛讨论可能会让普京寻求改变北约的军事存在，包括撤出美军。
他说，普京在2021年向时任总统乔·拜登提出了类似的想法，寻求欧洲和世界权力的重新分配。
“我认为普京会提到芬兰和瑞典。我相信他会提出匈牙利问题以及美国军队在波罗的海国家的存在问题，”泽伦斯基说。
他表示，欧洲安全安排的任何改变都必须在战争结束后由欧洲北约成员国决定。
