title_en: Trump's Justice Department faces a new era of scrutiny under a Democratic-led Congress
title_zh: 特朗普的司法部在民主党领导的国会下面临新时代的审查
summary: The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress
summary_zh: 司法部作为白宫的延伸部分运行了近两年，不受共和党控制的国会的限制
body_en: The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress
By ERIC TUCKER Associated Press and ALANNA DURKIN RICHER Associated Press

WASHINGTON -- The Justice Department has functioned for nearly two years as an extension of the White House, unchecked by a Republican-controlled Congress as it pursued investigations into President Donald Trump's enemies, fired waves of career employees and defended administration stances that judges across the country repeatedly deemed legally dubious .

Now, sweeping Democratic gains in Congress have shifted the balance of power in Washington, teeing up an onslaught of expected investigations into those actions and others as well as scrutiny from the majority party that the current Justice Department had until now managed to skirt.
The department has, at least publicly, appeared unbowed by the altered landscape.

Attorney General Todd Blanche says the department will cooperate with Congress but has also insisted that “we will not back down” from the Republican president's agenda. Meanwhile, a top aide told prosecutors on a call to prepare to be on “wartime” footing and a U.S. attorney publicly warned a top Democrat about planned congressional investigations.

It sets the stage for a pugilistic dynamic as Democrats promise to join already-skeptical courts in reining in the Trump administration while a Justice Department depleted by the losses of thousands of career employees and the postelection departures of senior leaders pledges to push ahead with its agenda.

Even though Democrats hold the gavel, they’re short on foolproof ways to guarantee Republican cooperation. Lawsuits can take years, subpoenas can be arduous to enforce and criminal contempt referrals for noncompliance would be sent to the Trump administration Justice Department, where they will almost certainly not be acted on.
“It’s a standoff and I don’t know what the answer to that is yet,” said Stan Brand, a former general counsel for the House of Representatives. “I don’t know if the Congress knows.”

Nonetheless, Democrats are eager to highlight what they view as abuses of power, including a succession of investigations the department has launched into the president’s perceived adversaries, many of which have been rejected by grand juries, dismissed by judges or have otherwise stalled without apparent progress.

In just the eventful weeks leading up to the election, the department unsuccessfully sought an indictment against former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson, accelerated an investigation into Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar, employed an unusual maneuver to file a fresh criminal case against former FBI Director James Comey and charged two ex-FBI officials in a complaint that was swiftly dismissed by a judge.
Political pressure from the White House is unlikely to wane given the promotion of Stephen Miller, a devoted Trump loyalist, to chief of staff.

And Justice Department leadership has suggested it won’t let Democrats’ threats of investigations deter its pursuit of the White House’s priorities, and may become even more aggressive in pressing the president’s causes.

“We will not back down. This will not slow us down. This will not stop us,” Blanche said in a Fox News interview Monday. “President Trump has two years remaining in this administration and you better believe that we’re going to use it effectively.”

In a call with U.S. attorneys across the country this week, a top Blanche aide, Aakash Singh, told prosecutors to prepare to be on “wartime” footing, and suggested more U.S. attorneys may be pushed out after a spate of postelection departures, according to people familiar with the call who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss internal department discussions.

The Justice Department said the “‘wartime’ reference had everything to do with public safety,” noting that some “newly elected state and local leaders are no longer interested in partnering with federal law enforcement.”

Any additional U.S. attorney departures would be on top of a string of significant departures in the days after the election, when the Senate-confirmed leaders of the department’s National Security, Civil and Civil Rights divisions all announced their resignations. The divisions will have temporary leaders but are unlikely to get Senate-confirmed ones in light of the Democratic majority.

“What that means for DOJ, potentially, is just a lot of inaction, with tough decisions not being made because typically those tough decisions are made by confirmed people at the top of the components,” said Greg Brower, a former U.S. attorney in Nevada during President George W. Bush’s administration who was later the FBI’s chief congressional affairs official.
body_zh: 司法部作为白宫的延伸部分运行了近两年，不受共和党控制的国会的限制
埃里克·塔克 (ERIC TUCKER) 美联社和阿兰娜·德金·里彻 (ALANNA DURKIN RICHER) 美联社报道
华盛顿——近两年来，司法部一直充当白宫的延伸，不受共和党控制的国会的限制，对唐纳德·特朗普总统的敌人进行调查，解雇了一批职业雇员，并为全国各地法官一再认为法律上可疑的政府立场辩护。
现在，民主党在国会的全面胜利已经改变了华盛顿的权力平衡，引发了对这些行动和其他行动的一系列预期调查，以及现任司法部迄今为止一直设法避开的多数党的审查。
至少在公开场合，该部门似乎并没有因环境的改变而屈服。
司法部长托德·布兰奇表示，该部门将与国会合作，但也坚称“我们不会在共和党总统的议程上退缩”。与此同时，一名高级助手在电话中告诉检察官准备进入“战时”状态，一名美国检察官公开警告一名民主党高级官员有关计划中的国会调查。
这为一场拳击运动奠定了基础，因为民主党人承诺加入本已持怀疑态度的法院来遏制特朗普政府，而司法部因数千名职业雇员的流失和高级领导人的离职而精疲力尽，承诺推进其议程。
尽管民主党握有木槌，但他们缺乏保证共和党合作的万无一失的方法。诉讼可能需要数年时间，传票可能很难执行，因不遵守规定而提出的藐视法庭刑事案件将被送往特朗普政府司法部，而司法部几乎肯定不会采取行动。
“这是一场僵局，我还不知道答案是什么，”众议院前总法律顾问斯坦·布兰德说。 “我不知道国会是否知道。”
尽管如此，民主党人仍急于强调他们认为的滥用权力行为，包括该部门对总统的所谓对手发起的一系列调查，其中许多调查被大陪审团拒绝，被法官驳回，或者因其他原因而停滞不前，没有明显进展。
在大选前的动荡几周内，该部门未能成功起诉前白宫助手卡西迪·哈钦森，加快了对民主党众议员伊尔汗·奥马尔的调查，采取了不寻常的策略对前联邦调查局局长詹姆斯·科米提起新的刑事案件，并在一项指控中指控了两名前联邦调查局官员，但该指控很快被法官驳回。
鉴于特朗普的忠实拥护者史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)晋升为幕僚长，来自白宫的政治压力不太可能减弱。
司法部领导层表示，不会让民主党的调查威胁阻止其对白宫优先事项的追求，并且可能会更加积极地推动总统的事业。
“我们不会退缩。这不会让我们放慢脚步。这不会阻止我们，”布兰奇周一在接受福克斯新闻采访时表示。 “特朗普总统在本届政府的任期还剩两年，你最好相信我们会有效地利用它。”
据知情人士透露，在本周与全国各地美国检察官的电话会议中，布兰奇的高级助手阿卡什·辛格告诉检察官，要做好“战时”准备，并建议更多的美国检察官在选举后一连串离职后可能会被解雇。
司法部表示，“‘战时’的提法与公共安全密切相关”，并指出一些“新当选的州和地方领导人不再有兴趣与联邦执法部门合作”。
任何额外的美国检察官离职都将是选举后几天内一系列重大离职事件的基础上，参议院确认的该部门国家安全、民权和民权部门的领导人均宣布辞职。这些部门将有临时领导人，但鉴于民主党占多数，不太可能获得参议院确认的领导人。
“这对司法部来说可能意味着大量无所作为，无法做出艰难的决定，因为这些艰难的决定通常是由已确认的高层人士做出的，”乔治·W·布什总统执政期间内华达州前联邦检察官、后来担任联邦调查局首席国会事务官员的格雷格·布劳尔说。

title_en: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history
title_zh: SpaceX成功捕获星际飞船并创造历史
summary: The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.
summary_zh: 该公司的航天器以戏剧性的方式返回德克萨斯州的发射台——小心地降低自身，直到两个金属臂连接到发射台
body_en: SpaceX successfully catches Starship and makes history The company's spacecraft returned to its Texas launchpad in dramatic fashion — by carefully lowering itself until two metal arms attached to the launch tower could secure it.
SpaceX's mega rocket Starship lifts off for a test flight from Starbase, Texas, on Friday. Eric Gay/AP hide caption
CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. — SpaceX's Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday, caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.

It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday's liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.
SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad.
The dramatic, sci-fi-like capture helped blot out the booster's messy miss.
"Can you believe it?" shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot.

SpaceX officials said Saturday's catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. Although Friday's booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique.

NASA welcomed Saturday's news. The space agency is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the moon later this decade and help build a permanent lunar base. Musk's ambitions are even grander: He wants to launch a fleet of Starships to build a city on Mars.

The world's largest and most powerful rocket — a 407-foot (124-meter) behemoth — blasted off late Friday afternoon from SpaceX's Starship base near the U.S.-Mexican border. Separating neatly from its booster before things went awry, the upper-stage spacecraft soared into orbit and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites.

Starship continued circling the world 165 miles (265 kilometers) up, with live views of itself and Earth streaming down via Starlink. The spacecraft completed 14 laps around Earth, outshining the previous mission's one to two laps.
It was SpaceX's 15th flight of a full-scale Starship since 2023 and its only second trip to orbit.
SpaceX reported that everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well.

As for the booster, SpaceX's Kate Tice said its engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down. The booster's guidance system sensed it wasn't in the right position and automatically initiated the watery detour and self-destruction. Engineers are still investigating the cause.

SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida's Kennedy Space Center within the next few months. That is the starting point for NASA's next Artemis mission, which will skip the moon and remain in orbit around Earth for lunar lander practice.

Artemis III's four astronauts will attempt to dock their capsule with not only Starship but Blue Origin's Blue Moon. The two companies will take turns delivering crews to the lunar surface. NASA is targeting as soon as 2028 for Artemis IV, humanity's first moon landing since the Apollo era more than half a century ago.
NPR does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews.
body_zh: SpaceX 成功捕获 Starship 并创造历史该公司的航天器以戏剧性的方式返回德克萨斯州的发射台——小心地降低自身，直到连接在发射塔上的两个金属臂将其固定住。
周五，SpaceX 的巨型火箭 Starship 从德克萨斯州 Starbase 升空进行试飞。埃里克·盖伊/美联社隐藏标题栏
佛罗里达州卡纳维拉尔角——周六，SpaceX 的星际飞船成功返回地球，被巨大的机械臂抓住在半空中，它的旅程早在 22 小时前就开始了。
这是埃隆·马斯克和他的团队所希望的大结局——首次捕获从太空飞回的星际飞船。但周五从德克萨斯州升空后不久，第一级助推器发生爆炸，该公司未能实现预期的双倍捕获。
SpaceX 的巨型火箭可能会让 NASA 望尘莫及
当不锈钢子弹形航天器在发射台上直立下降时，残骸仍留在墨西哥湾，被浮标封锁。
戏剧性的、科幻般的捕捉帮助掩盖了助推器混乱的失误。
“你能相信吗？” SpaceX 评论员 Dan Huot 喊道。
SpaceX 官员表示，周六的捕获证明了 Starship 的完全可重复使用性，旨在进行月球和火星旅行。尽管周五的助推器回收失败，但该公司之前已经进行了三次助推器捕获，验证了该技术。
美国宇航局对周六的消息表示欢迎。美国宇航局正在斥资数十亿美元购买星际飞船，以便在本十年晚些时候将阿耳忒弥斯宇航员送上月球，并帮助建立一个永久的月球基地。马斯克的野心更加宏伟：他想发射一支星际飞船舰队，在火星上建造一座城市。
世界上最大、最强大的火箭——一枚 407 英尺（124 米）长的庞然大物——于周五下午从 SpaceX 位于美墨边境附近的 Starship 基地发射升空。在出现问题之前，上级航天器巧妙地与助推器分离，飞入轨道并释放了 26 颗先进的星链卫星。
星舰继续在 165 英里（265 公里）高空环绕地球飞行，并通过星链传送星舰自身和地球的实时图像。该航天器绕地球飞行了 14 圈，比之前的任务只绕了 1 到 2 圈。
这是 SpaceX 自 2023 年以来第 15 次全尺寸星际飞船飞行，也是其唯一第二次进入轨道。
SpaceX 报告称，飞船上的所有部件，包括重要的隔热罩，似乎都运行良好。
至于助推器，SpaceX 的 Kate Tice 表示，其发动机在返回途中过早停止点火。助推器的制导系统感知到它不在正确的位置，并自动启动水上绕行和自毁。工程师仍在调查原因。
SpaceX 预计将在未来几个月内开始从佛罗里达州肯尼迪航天中心发射星际飞船。这是美国宇航局下一次阿尔忒弥斯任务的起点，该任务将跳过月球并留在绕地球轨道上进行月球着陆器练习。
阿耳忒弥斯三号的四名宇航员将尝试将他们的太空舱不仅与星际飞船对接，还与蓝色起源的蓝月亮对接。两家公司将轮流将宇航员运送到月球表面。 NASA 的目标是最快在 2028 年实现阿尔忒弥斯 IV，这是半个多世纪前阿波罗时代以来人类首次登月。

Cans of Kirkland Signature Real Heavy Whipped Cream sold between Oct. 11 and Oct. 31 are subject to a voluntary recall after some customers reported a chemical taste and smell. Alamance Foods, the manufacturer, said it has received no reports of serious effects requiring medical care.
“We have learned that one batch of Kirkland Signature Whipped Cream may contain a small amount of a cleaning chemical,” the company said.
The product was sold in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee and Wisconsin.
Customers can return the cream to Costco for a full refund, according to Alamance Foods.

title_en: He was drafted as an NFL team’s future. It arrives now.
title_zh: 他被选为 NFL 球队的未来。现在到了。
summary: Fernando Mendoza, the Heisman-winning quarterback selected No. 1 overall in last year’s NFL draft, takes over as starter for the Las Vegas Raiders. Will he turn around the franchise?
summary_zh: 获得海斯曼奖的四分卫费尔南多·门多萨 (Fernando Mendoza) 在去年的 NFL 选秀中以第一顺位被选为拉斯维加斯突袭者队的先发球员。无线网络
body_en: Fernando Mendoza was drafted as the Las Vegas Raiders’ future. It arrives now.

When Heisman Trophy-winning quarterback Fernando Mendoza was selected first overall by the Las Vegas Raiders in April’s NFL draft, he updated his biography on LinkedIn to say that he was “focused on preparation, growth and discipline.”

It is a quirk of the NFL that teams historically race to draft a quarterback early, then play them as little as possible for much of their first season. Teams view the position as so demanding and the pro game so fast that they want their prized picks to prepare as much as possible before inheriting the pressure of an entire franchise.
Mendoza’s time to prepare ended Tuesday, nine games into his rookie season.

Before Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline, Las Vegas (4-5) traded veteran starting quarterback Kirk Cousins and elevated Mendoza to starter ahead of Sunday’s Week 10 matchup against the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (5-4). Cousins had thrown 20 touchdowns, the most by any quarterback to change teams midseason in NFL history, per NBC Sports research.

After starting 3-0, the Raiders have lost five of their last six games but still have what one playoff tracker pegged this week as a 15% chance to make what would be only the franchise’s third playoff appearance since 2003. Trading Cousins and elevating Mendoza “is no way to signify that we are punting on the season or looking forward to 2027,” Raiders general manager John Spytek said.

“It’s something that [Mendoza] worked very hard for since the moment he walked into this building,” Spytek told reporters this week. “He passed every test. I want to stop short of saying he’s earned it, but he put us in a position where we had to make a really hard decision today with his growth as a person, as a teammate, as a leader, as a quarterback.”

Mendoza is known as a quick study. While attending Cal, he spent his summers away from Berkeley interning at investment firms. In his first and only season at Indiana last fall, Mendoza picked up the Hoosiers’ offensive playbook so quickly that he led the perennial Big Ten doormat to a stunning national championship by using his arms and his feet.

Raiders coach Klint Kubiak, who as an offensive playcaller mentored Sam Darnold during last season’s Super Bowl run with the Seahawks, said that Cousins was “the right role model” for Mendoza to learn from and accelerate his acclimation to the NFL.

“It’s time to rally around Fernando,” center Tyler Linderbaum said. “Everyone has to step up and play for him. Obviously, it’s never easy being a rookie in that first game, but there’s 10 other guys on the field with him, there’s a whole defense, special teams unit, and just be there for him. Let him play with confidence. We’ve seen it every day in practice, the plays he can make.”
Dan Hicks, NBC Sports voice for 34 years of memorable moments, dies at age 64

Why Devin Booker is unlike almost any other superstar in the NBA

Mendoza’s only snaps to this point came Oct. 11 when he played late in a blowout loss to the New England Patriots and completed 6 of his 8 passes. Rookie debuts are inherently difficult; quarterbacks taken No. 1 overall are 5-23-1 in their first start since 1970, per NBC Sports research. Facing the Seahawks will make Mendoza’s big day even more challenging. Seattle leads the NFL in total defense, allowing just 244 yards per game.

Mendoza might not be under the most pressure of any Raiders player on Sunday, however. The team’s defense has allowed 30 or more points in each of its last six games, tied for the longest streak by a team in a season in NFL history.

“Fernando has done everything we’ve asked him to do in practice,” Kubiak said. “I think he’s exceeded those expectations, and we all know that live bullets Sunday is far different from practice. However, he showed us that he’s ready, not only physically, but mentally.”
Andrew Greif is a sports reporter for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 费尔南多·门多萨被选为拉斯维加斯突袭者队的未来。现在到了。
当海斯曼杯四分卫费尔南多·门多萨 (Fernando Mendoza) 在 4 月份的 NFL 选秀中以第一顺位被拉斯维加斯突袭者队选中时，他在 LinkedIn 上更新了自己的传记，表示自己“专注于准备、成长和纪律”。
NFL 的一个怪癖是，球队历来都会竞相尽早选拔四分卫，然后在第一个赛季的大部分时间里尽可能少地让他们上场。球队认为这个职位的要求如此之高，职业比赛的速度如此之快，以至于他们希望他们的珍贵选秀权在继承整个球队的压力之前做好尽可能多的准备。
门多萨的准备时间于周二结束，此时他的新秀赛季已经打了九场了。
在周二的 NFL 交易截止日期之前，拉斯维加斯队 (4-5) 交易了老将首发四分卫柯克·考辛斯 (Kirk Cousins)，并在周日第 10 周对阵卫冕超级碗冠军西雅图海鹰队 (5-4) 之前将门多萨提拔为首发。根据 NBC Sports 的研究，考辛斯共传出 20 次达阵，这是 NFL 历史上季中换队四分卫中最多的。
突袭者队以 3-0 开局，在过去的 6 场比赛中输掉了 5 场，但据一位季后赛追踪者本周预测，突袭者队仍有 15% 的机会进入季后赛，这将是球队自 2003 年以来第三次进入季后赛。交易考辛斯和提拔门多萨“并不意味着我们会押注这个赛季或期待 2027 年，”突袭者队总经理约翰·斯派泰克 (John Spytek) 表示。
“从他走进这座大楼的那一刻起，门多萨就为这件事付出了巨大的努力，”斯派泰克本周告诉记者。 “他通过了每一项测试。我不想说他是应得的，但他让我们今天不得不做出一个非常艰难的决定，因为他作为一个人、作为队友、作为领导者、作为四分卫的成长。”
门多萨以学习速度快而闻名。在加州大学就读期间，他暑假离开伯克利，在投资公司实习。去年秋天，在印第安纳的第一个也是唯一一个赛季中，门多萨很快就掌握了印第安纳州印第安纳队的进攻战术，以至于他用自己的手臂和双脚带领常年大十联盟获得了令人惊叹的全国冠军。
突袭者队教练克林特·库比亚克（Klint Kubiak）在上赛季海鹰队的超级碗比赛中作为进攻球员指导了萨姆·达诺德（Sam Darnold），他表示考辛斯是门多萨学习并加速他适应 NFL 的“正确榜样”。
“是时候团结在费尔南多周围了，”中锋泰勒·林德鲍姆说。 “每个人都必须挺身而出，为他打球。显然，作为一名新秀，在第一场比赛中绝非易事，但场上还有其他 10 名球员和他在一起，有一个完整的防守组、特别小组，就在他身边。让他充满信心地比赛。我们每天都在训练中看到他能打出的比赛。”
NBC 体育频道 (NBC Sports) 的代言人丹·希克斯 (Dan Hicks) 去世，享年 64 岁，34 年来为人们带来难忘的时刻
维京人队可能已经获得了超级碗之旅唯一缺失的部分
为什么德文·布克与 NBA 中几乎所有其他超级巨星不同
门多萨在这一点上唯一的表现是在 10 月 11 日，当时他在输给新英格兰爱国者队的比赛中打得很晚，并完成了 8 次传球中的 6 次。新秀首秀本质上是困难的；根据 NBC Sports 的研究，自 1970 年以来，排名第一的四分卫在首次首发时的战绩为 5 胜 23 胜 1 负。面对海鹰队将使门多萨的重要日子更具挑战性。西雅图队在总防守上领先 NFL，场均只允许 244 码。
然而，周日，门多萨可能不是突袭者队球员中承受最大压力的。球队的防守在过去六场比赛中每场都失分超过 30 分，追平了 NFL 历史上球队单赛季最长连续失分纪录。
“费尔南多在训练中完成了我们要求他做的一切，”库比亚克说。 “我认为他超出了这些预期，我们都知道周日的实弹比赛与训练有很大不同。然而，他向我们展示了他已经准备好了，不仅是身体上的，而且是精神上的。”
安德鲁·格雷夫 (Andrew Greif) 是 NBC 新闻数字频道的体育记者。

title_en: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom to Senate in massive upset
title_zh: 密西西比州选举民主党人斯科特·科洛姆为参议院议员
summary: Colom's win is a boost to the Democratic Party as it seeks to gain a larger foothold in the South.
summary_zh: 科罗姆的胜利对民主党寻求在南方获得更大立足点的推动。
body_en: Mississippi voted blue, in a shock win for Democrats.

Democrat Scott Colom ousted Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state that went for President Donald Trump by 23 points in 2024. He will be the first Black senator elected in Mississippi since the Reconstruction era — and the first Democrat from the state headed to the Senate in 44 years.
Colom, a Democratic district attorney, ran a scrappy campaign that saw some national money and resources in the final stretch of the race.

Hyde-Smith was appointed to the Senate in 2018 and had since won election to the seat twice, but she faced attacks from Colom that she was out of touch and indifferent to rising grocery and gas prices during Trump’s second term.
National Democratic groups hadn't paid much attention to the Mississippi Senate race until an October surge of excitement for Colom drew late spending and attention.

Colom's win is a boost to the Democratic Party as it seeks to gain a larger foothold in the South and improve their standing with Black voters. It’s also a major vindication for Colom and other Southern Democrats who argued Mississippi had been neglected for far too long.
body_zh: 密西西比州投票支持蓝色，民主党意外获胜。
民主党人斯科特·科洛姆 (Scott Colom) 在该州以 23 个百分点的优势击败了参议员辛迪·海德·史密斯 (Cindy Hyde-Smith)，该州在 2024 年以 23 个百分点的优势支持唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 总统。他将成为密西西比州自重建时代以来第一位当选的黑人参议员，也是 44 年来该州第一位进入参议院的民主党参议员。
民主党地方检察官科洛姆进行了一场斗志旺盛的竞选活动，在竞选的最后阶段获得了一些国家资金和资源。
海德-史密斯于 2018 年被任命为参议员，此后两次赢得该席位的选举，但她面临科罗姆的攻击，称她在特朗普第二任期内对不断上涨的食品杂货和汽油价格漠不关心。
全国民主党团体并没有对密西西比州参议员竞选给予太多关注，直到十月份对科罗姆的兴奋激增吸引了后期的支出和关注。
科罗姆的胜利对民主党来说是一个推动，因为它寻求在南方获得更大的立足点并提高他们在黑人选民中的地位。这也是科洛姆和其他南方民主党人的一个重要证明，他们认为密西西比州被忽视太久了。

title_en: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
title_zh: 解雇萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 的 OpenAI 董事会成员表示，我们仍然不能信任人工智能首席执行官
summary: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy communi
summary_zh: 今天，我正在与乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心执行主任海伦·托纳进行交谈。本集
body_en: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life.

Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely .

But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are.

Now, the question of AI safety is everywhere . This summer, AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic broke out of their testing environments and hacked real companies. The CEOs of these frontier labs have since called for a slowdown and asked Washington for help, but the White House’s answer was a voluntary accord — one that relies in part on the kind of board accountability that failed at OpenAI. Anthropic is also about to go public, which will put a whole new set of market pressures on OpenAI’s biggest competitor.

Helen has seen up close what happens when safety commitments run headlong into commercial incentives. And as she put it to me, if our hopes for the future depend on any one person being trustworthy, we’re in big trouble.

So we talked about what we might do instead: what the labs are actually trying to build, whether AI alignment is a problem that can be solved, and what a smarter approach to AI regulation might look like. That includes how to think about China, which is the issue that looms large in every policy conversation about AI right now — especially now after the Jensen Huang affair . Just for clarity, Helen and I talked before Nvidia opened its investigation and Jensen ultimately resigned, so you won’t hear us talk about that directly.
Okay: Helen Toner, the executive director of CSET, on the future of AI safety. Here we go.
This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.
Helen Toner, you’re the executive director for the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. Welcome to Decoder .

I have wanted to talk to you for 10 million years. I am so excited you’re here. You’ve been involved in a lot of AI safety and ethics ideas for a long time. You were obviously on the board of OpenAI during what everyone has come to call “the blip.”

Now, you’re talking a lot about AI safety, about which I have 10 million questions. But let’s just start at the start. You run the Center for Security and Emerging Technology, people call it CSET. What is CSET?
It’s awesome to be here. I’m really excited to talk to you as well. CSET is a team inside Georgetown, but we’re really not academics. We’re about 50 people and have been going since 2019.

Basically in 2019, a group of us decided that there was a lot happening and a lot of emerging technologies that were becoming very relevant in the national security space, and the security space more broadly,. And some policymakers who had very important jobs did not have the time or the expertise to get across what was going on with those emerging technologies. Already at the top of our list in 2019 was AI.

Basically our mission is to do analysis that is really rigorous, but also actionable, for policymakers and analysis that is both grounded in the technology and grounded in real national security expertise and understanding and issues. We produce long reports. We go do short briefings on those long reports to busy policymakers. We have a big data team that helps us do our research. We do all kinds of cool stuff.

Can I just ask about the dynamics of that for one minute? You and I are talking the day after the midterm elections in the United States of America, and there was a big blue wave. There’s a lot of polling that says the number one issue is corruption. We’re going to throw the bums out. We’re going to start over and get rid of these corrupt guys.

The AI industry, and the tech industry, has flooded a bunch of money into politics. And then somewhere next to that is, “Oh, there’s a bunch of well-meaning researchers who are going to show up and tell you how it actually works and what the real risks are.”

It just occurs to me that maybe people don’t believe that’s effective anymore, that the money and the corruption and the AI CEO standing next to Trump have completely outweighed the well-meaning, sincere, “here are the actual problems” research that you do. What is that dynamic actually like?

It’s a reasonable concern to have, and there are definitely some spaces where money just absolutely overwhelms everything. I’m Australian. I didn’t grow up in the US, and so the amount of money in US elections is pretty mind-blowing to me, but there are limits to what money can do.

AI is a great example. In this election, there were just unbelievable amounts of money being thrown at candidates, at messages, at opposition research. There was all kinds of astroturfing on Twitter, and some very strange things trying to get anyone who talked about AI governance, regulation, safety, any of those words thrown out or not elected. It turns out to have really not worked very well.

I think the reason that it didn’t work very well is one, this is an issue that voters increasingly care about. And two, also interestingly, it’s an issue that is pretty bipartisan at this point. What we see in our work is that there is a real thirst among policymakers for high-quality information. That’s members of Congress for sure, but they’re also in the executive branch, just a lot of people who have these very busy jobs and are seeing AI playing a larger and larger role in their work and their world.
body_zh: 今天，我正在与乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心执行主任海伦·托纳进行交谈。本集是我们现实生活中的人工智能系列的第二部分。
Helen 是人工智能安全和政策界的知名人物，不过她最出名的可能是在 OpenAI 董事会任职，当时她是投票解雇 Sam Altman 的四名董事会成员之一。这一事件现在有时被称为“短暂事件”，最终以山姆重新担任首席执行官、海伦辞职以及新的董事会而告终。此后，OpenAI 进行了彻底重组。
但值得记住的是 Helen 和董事会应该做的事情：OpenAI 的非营利性董事会的存在是专门为了确保公司不会因为将利润和增长置于安全之上而背离其构建安全人工智能的使命。当董事会真正试图拉动杠杆时，问责机制就崩溃了，我们就到了这一步。
现在，人工智能安全问题无处不在。今年夏天，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的人工智能模型突破了他们的测试环境并入侵了真实的公司。此后，这些前沿实验室的首席执行官们呼吁放慢速度，并向华盛顿寻求帮助，但白宫的答复是一项自愿协议——该协议在一定程度上依赖于 OpenAI 失败的董事会问责制。 Anthropic也即将上市，这将给OpenAI最大的竞争对手带来一系列全新的市场压力。
海伦亲眼目睹了当安全承诺与商业激励措施相冲突时会发生什么。正如她对我所说，如果我们对未来的希望取决于任何一个人是否值得信赖，那么我们就有大麻烦了。
因此，我们讨论了我们可能会做什么：实验室实际上正在尝试构建什么，人工智能对齐是否是一个可以解决的问题，以及更智能的人工智能监管方法可能是什么样子。这包括如何看待中国，这是目前每一次有关人工智能的政策对话中都突出的问题——尤其是在黄仁勋事件之后。为了清楚起见，海伦和我在英伟达展开调查和詹森最终辞职之前进行了交谈，所以你不会听到我们直接谈论这个问题。
好的：CSET 执行董事 Helen Toner 谈论人工智能安全的未来。开始了。
为了篇幅和清晰度，本次采访经过了轻微编辑。
海伦·托纳 (Helen Toner)，您是乔治城大学安全与新兴技术中心的执行主任。欢迎来到解码器。
一千万年来我一直想和你说话。我很高兴你在这里。您长期以来一直参与许多人工智能安全和道德理念。显然，在大家所说的“短暂时期”，你是 OpenAI 董事会的一员。
现在，您谈论了很多关于人工智能安全的问题，对此我有 1000 万个问题。但让我们从头开始吧。你负责管理安全和新兴技术中心，人们称之为 CSET。什么是 CSET？
来到这里真是太棒了。我也很高兴与您交谈。 CSET 是乔治敦大学内部的一个团队，但我们实际上不是学者。我们大约有 50 人，自 2019 年以来一直在这样做。
基本上在 2019 年，我们一群人认为发生了很多事情，出现了很多新兴技术，这些技术与国家安全领域以及更广泛的安全领域变得非常相关。一些担任非常重要工作的政策制定者没有时间或专业知识来了解这些新兴技术的发展情况。 2019 年，人工智能已经位居榜首。
基本上，我们的使命是为政策制定者提供真正严格且可操作的分析，并且分析既基于技术，又基于真正的国家安全专业知识、理解和问题。我们制作长报告。我们会向忙碌的政策制定者就这些冗长的报告做简短的简报。我们有一个大数据团队来帮助我们进行研究。我们做各种很酷的事情。
我可以用一分钟时间问一下这方面的动态吗？你和我正在美国中期选举后的第二天进行谈话，当时出现了一股巨大的蓝色浪潮。许多民意调查显示，第一大问题是腐败。我们要把流浪汉赶出去。我们要重新开始并除掉这些腐败分子。
人工智能行业和科技行业已经将大量资金投入政治。然后旁边的某个地方是，“哦，有一群善意的研究人员会出现并告诉你它实际上是如何运作的以及真正的风险是什么。”
我只是突然想到，也许人们不再相信那是有效的，金钱、腐败和站在特朗普身边的人工智能首席执行官已经完全超过了你所做的善意、真诚的“这就是实际问题”的研究。这种动态实际上是什么样的？
这是一个合理的担忧，而且肯定有一些空间是金钱绝对压倒一切的。我是澳大利亚人。我不是在美国长大的，所以美国选举中的金钱数额对我来说相当令人震惊，但金钱的作用是有限的。
人工智能就是一个很好的例子。在这次选举中，候选人、信息和反对派研究投入了令人难以置信的大量资金。 Twitter 上有各种各样的言论，还有一些非常奇怪的事情，试图让任何谈论人工智能治理、监管、安全的人被扔掉或不当选。事实证明确实效果不太好。
我认为效果不佳的原因之一是，这是选民越来越关心的问题。第二，同样有趣的是，目前这是一个两党共同关注的问题。我们在工作中看到，政策制定者确实渴望高质量的信息。这肯定是国会议员，但他们也在行政部门，只是很多人从事着非常繁忙的工作，并且看到人工智能在他们的工作和世界中发挥着越来越大的作用。
